In the whole Raghu clan, he was authenticated s raghhu clan, he was authenticated as Raghuraj, the king Raghu and the Yadavas considered him like Krishna.154.
The affliction saw him as the destroyer of suffering and Bali saw him as Vaman
The devotees of Shiva considered him as Shiva and also as Vyas and Parashar.155.
The Brahmins considered him as Veda and Kshatriyas as war
The person who thought of him in any manner, he presented himself in accordance with his desire.156.

626.e: He ruled in various ways after conquering various countries far and near
Seizing various countries, he performed Yajnas after short intervals.157.

626.g: ਪਗ ਪਗ ਜਗਿ ਖੰਭ ਕਹੁ ਗਾਡਾ ॥
626.t: pag pag jag kha(n)bh kahu gaaddaa ||

626.g: ਡਗ ਡਗ ਹੋਮ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਕਰਿ ਛਾਡਾ ॥
626.t: ddag ddag hom ma(n)tr kar chhaaddaa ||
626.e: He got planted the columns of Yajnas at short distances and performed heaven at various places by reciting mantras

626.g: ਜਗਿ ਖੰਭ ਜਿਹ ਠਉਰ ਨ ਹੋਈ ॥੧੫੮॥
626.t: jag kha(n)bh jeh Thaur na hoiee ||158||
626.e: No part of the earth was visible, where no columns of Yajnas were seen.158.
Inviting superb Brahmins, he performed many Gomedh Yajnas

626.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਭੂਯ ਕੇ ਰਸ ਲੀਨੇ ॥੧੫੯॥
626.t: bhaat bhaat bhooy ke ras leene ||159||
626.e: Enjoying various types of the luxuries of the earth, he also performed Ashvamedh Yajnas many times.159.

626.g: ਗਜਾ ਮੇਧ ਬਹੁ ਕਰੇ ਜਗਿ ਤਿਹ ॥
626.t: gajaa medh bahu kare jag teh ||

626.g: ਅਜਾ ਮੇਧ ਤੇ ਸਕੈ ਨ ਗਨ ਕਿਹ ॥
626.t: ajaa medh te sakai na gan keh ||
626.e: He also performed Gajmedh Yajnas and he performed Ajaamedh Yajnas so many times that they cannot be enumerated
Performing Gomedh Yajnas in various ways, he sacrificed many animals.160.
Performing many Raajsu Yajnas, the king Raghu seemed like a second Indra
After taking baths at different pilgrim-stations, he bestowed various types of charities according to Vedic injunctions.161.

626.g: ਅੰਨ ਛੇਤ੍ਰ ਘਰਿ ਘਰਿ ਮੈ ਸਾਧਾ ॥
626.t: a(n)n chhetr ghar ghar mai saadhaa ||
626.e: He got built places for drinking water at all the pilgrim-stations and stores of corn in every home,
So that if anyone comes with any desire, he may be able to obtain the desired thing.162.

626.g: ਭੂਖ ਨਾਗ ਕੋਈ ਰਹਨ ਨ ਪਾਵੈ ॥
626.t: bhookh naag koiee rahan na paavai ||

626.e: Nobody should remain hungry or naked and any beggar who came, may return like a king

626.g: ਬਹੁਰ ਦਾਨ ਕਹ ਕਰ ਨ ਪਸਾਰਾ ॥
626.t: bahur dhaan keh kar na pasaaraa ||

626.e: The king Raghu had such administration that anyone, who would see him once, he would become able to bestow charities himself on others.163.
He gave gifts of gold and silver in various ways

626.g: ਜਨ ਸਭ ਕਰੇ ਰੰਕ ਰਘੁ ਰਾਜਾ ॥੧੬੪॥
626.t: jan sabh kare ra(n)k ragh raajaa ||164||
626.e: He gave so much to everyone that the recipient became like a king form the status of poor.164.
He would take bath according to Shastric injunctions and then give gifts of elephants, camels and cows
By bestowing gifts of various types of garments, he had fascinated the whole earth.165.
By honouring various types of the lowly, he gave horses and elephants in charity

626.g: ਜੋ ਮੁਖ ਮਾਗੈ ਵਹ ਬਰੁ ਪਾਵੈ ॥੧੬੬॥
626.t: jo mukh maagai veh bar paavai ||166||
626.e: None was afflicted with suffering and hunger and whosoever asked with suffering and hunger and whosoever asked for anything, he obtained the same.166.
The king Raghu was the abode of charity and gentleness and an ocean of mercy on this earth
He was a great and expert archer and a glorious king, always remaining detached.167.

626.g: ਨਿਤਿ ਉਠਿ ਕਰਤ ਦੇਵ ਕੀ ਪੂਜਾ ॥
626.t: nit uTh karat dhev kee poojaa ||

626.e: He always worshipped the goddess with roses, pandanus and sugar-candyy
And while worshipping, he touched her lotus-feet with his head.168.
He introduced the religious traditions at all places and all the people lived peacefully everywhere

626.g: ਭੂਖ ਨਾਗ ਕੋਈ ਕਹੂੰ ਨ ਦੇਖਾ ॥
626.t: bhookh naag koiee kahoo(n) na dhekhaa ||

626.e: There did not seem to be any hungry and naked, high and low and everyone seemed to be a self-sufficient person.169.
The religious banners fluttered everywhere and there seemed to be no thief or Thug anywhere

626.g: ਜਹ ਤਹ ਯਾਰ ਚੋਰ ਚੁਨਿ ਮਾਰਾ ॥
626.t: jeh teh yaar chor chun maaraa ||

626.g: ਏਕ ਦੇਸਿ ਕਹੂੰ ਰਹੈ ਨ ਪਾਰਾ ॥੧੭੦॥
626.t: ek dhes kahoo(n) rahai na paaraa ||170||
626.e: He had picked up and killed all the thieves and Thugs and had established one-canopy kingdom.170.

626.g: ਸਾਧ ਓਰਿ ਕੋਈ ਦਿਸਟਿ ਨ ਪੇਖਾ ॥
626.t: saadh or koiee dhisaT na pekhaa ||

626.e: The kingdom of king Raghu was such that the differentiation of a saint and a thief did not exist there and all were saits
His discus fluttered in all the four directions, which returned only on cutting the heads of the sinners.171.
The cow caused the lion to drink milk and the lion supervised the cow while grazing

626.g: ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਮਾਰਿ ਕੋਈ ਹਾਥੁ ਨ ਡਾਰਾ ॥੧੭੨॥
626.t: traas maar koiee haath na ddaaraa ||172||
626.e: The persons considered to be thieves now protected the wealth and none committed any wrong act because of the fear of punishment.172.
The men and women slept peacefully in their beds and none begged for anything from others

626.g: ਰਾਜ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਤੇ ਢਰੈ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥੧੭੩॥
626.t: raaj traas te ddarai na paae ||173||
626.e: The ghee and fire lived at the same places, and did not damage each other because of the fear of the king.173.

626.g: ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਤ੍ਰਸਤ ਕਰੁ ਕੋਈ ਨ ਡਾਰੈ ॥
626.t: traas trasat kar koiee na ddaarai ||
626.e: The thief and saints moved together and none frightened any fear because of the fear of the administration
The cow and the lion moved freely in the same field and no power could harm them.174.

627.g: ਇਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਰਾਜੁ ਕਰ੍ਯੋ ਰਘੁ ਰਾਜਾ ॥
627.t: eeh bidh raaj karayo ragh raajaa ||

627.e: The king Raghu ruled in this way and the fame of his charity spread in all the four directions
The mighty and elegant warriors protected him in all the four directions.175.
That king, skilful in fourteen sciences, ruled for twenty thousand years

627.g: ਔਰ ਨ ਸਕੈ ਐਸ ਕਰ ਕਰਮਾ ॥੧੭੬॥
627.t: aauar na sakai aais kar karamaa ||176||
627.e: He always performed the religious acts of this kind, which none other could perform.176.
PAADHARI STANZA
The king Raghu ruled in this way and gave in charity the elephants and horses to the poor
He conquered many kings and shattered many forts.177.
End of “The Rule of king Raghu.”

627.g: ਅਥ ਅਜ ਰਾਜਾ ਕੋ ਰਾਜ ਕਥਨੰ ॥
627.t: ath aj raajaa ko raaj kathana(n) ||
627.e: Now begins the description of the rule of king Aj
PAADHARI STANZA
Then there ruled the great and powerful king Aj, who destroyed several clans after conquering many heroes
He also conquered the rebellious kings.1.
He conquered many invincible kings and shattered the pride of many egoistic kings
The great king Aj was the ocean of fourteen sciences.2.
That king was a powerful warrior and expert in the study of Shrutis (Vedas) and Shastras
That great king was full of self-pride and had a very charming face, seeing which all the kings felt shy.3.
That Sovereign was king of kings and in his kingdom, all the houses were full of wealth
The women were allured on seeing his beauty and he was the knower of the mysteries of the Vedas he was a great donor, skilful in sciences and a very gentle king.4.
If I relate the whole story, I fear the Granth to become voluminous
Therefore, O friend! listen this story only in brief there was a king named Subahu in Vidrabha country, the name of whose queen was Champavati.5.
She gave birth to a daughter, whose name was Indumati

627.g: ਜਬ ਭਈ ਜੋਗ ਬਰ ਕੇ ਕੁਮਾਰਿ ॥
627.t: jab bhiee jog bar ke kumaar ||

627.e: When she attained the marriageable age, the king then consulted his ministers.6.
The king invited the kings of all the countries, who came to the kingdom of Subahu with their armies

627.g: ਜਿਹਿ ਜਪਤ ਲੋਗ ਮਿਲਿ ਸਰਬ ਜਾਪੁ ॥੭॥
627.t: jeh japat log mil sarab jaap ||7||
627.e: The adorable goddess Sarasvati came to reside in the mouths of all them and all of them with the desire of marrying that girl, offered prayers alongwith

627.g: ਤਬ ਦੇਸ ਦੇਸ ਕੇ ਭੂਪ ਆਨਿ ॥
627.t: tab dhes dhes ke bhoop aan ||

627.e: All the kings of various countries came and bowed before that king Subahu nad sat in the assembly

627.g: ਜਨ ਦੇਵ ਮੰਡਲੀ ਸਮ ਨ ਤੈਸੁ ॥੮॥
627.t: jan dhev ma(n)ddalee sam na tais ||8||
627.e: , Where their glory excelled that of the assembly of gods.8.

628.e: The small and big drums were resounding
The glory of that place is indescribable all of them appeared to be like Indra.9.
That royal assembly was such that seeing it, Indra shrunk his nose, who should describe its glory?
The Gandharvas and Yakshas kept silent on seeing it.10.
ARDH PAADHARI STANZA
The warriors looked splendid, seeing whom the heavenly damsels got allured
There were innumerable heavenly damsels.11.
They were singing fascinating songs, in which they were blessing together for their long like till the end of four ages.12.
The knocking on the instruments were being heard and many heavenly damsels were being seen.13.
The songs were being sung according to Vedic rites and the kings of unique glory looked magnificent.14.
The stringed instruments were being played and the women, being pleased, were happily singing songs.15.
UCHHAAL STANZA
The women were singing with the clapping of their hands and the kings with the decoration of gods, were looking at them.16.
The singing of songs continued with happy mind and seeing the glory of that place, even the mind of greed was becoming greedy.17.
They were talking with the signs of their eyes and all the weapon wielders were looking splendid.18.
The elephants were thundering and the companions were bedecked
The horses were jumping and dancing.19.
The young damsels were dancing and were singing happily while clapping their hands.20.
These women of the voice of a nightingale and having beautiful eyes, were alluring the mind by singing the song.21.
These women having beautiful hair, charming eyes and in the garb of heavenly damsels had the voice of a nightingale.22.
These women had marvelous figures, full of desires, with bewitching smiles and long nostrils.23.
Seeing the beauty of the queens, the wife of Indra also felt shy
These heavenly maidens were like the rosary of musical modes.24.
MOHINI STANZA

628.g: ਦੇਖਤ ਸੁਰ ਨਰ ਕੋ ਮਨ ਮੋਹਤ ॥
628.t: dhekhat sur nar ko man mohat ||
628.e: These whit-complexioned elegant women were fascinating the mind of gods and men
Seeing them, the great kings got pleased what more description can be given of their glory?.25.

629.e: Seeing the embellishment of these women, many men of taste were getting pleased
The women were dancing in many emotional postures, seeing which all the gods and men were delighted.26.
The horses were neighing
The elephants were trumpeting and the people of the town were dancing the gods, men and women were all getting pleased and the kings were busy in bestowing charities.27.
The heavenly damsels were dancing while singing, seeing whom, the kings got pleased and their queens were also getting angry
The pretty lyre of Narada was being played, seeing which the gods seemed radiant like fire.28.
All of them had put antimony in their eyes and had bedecked their limbs, having worn handsome garments
The kings were getting pleased and were trying to wed them.29.

629.g: ਰੁਣ ਝੁਣ ਬਾਜੈ ਰੰਗ ਅੰਗ ਮਾਲਾ ॥
629.t: run jhun baajai ra(n)g a(n)g maalaa ||
629.e: The women of gods were dancing and the jingling of the rosaries of their limbs was being heard

629.g: ਬਨਿ ਬਨਿ ਬੈਠੇ ਜਹ ਤਹ ਰਾਜਾ ॥
629.t: ban ban baiThe jeh teh raajaa ||

629.g: ਦੈ ਦੈ ਡਾਰੈ ਤਨ ਮਨ ਸਾਜਾ ॥੩੦॥
629.t: dhai dhai ddaarai tan man saajaa ||30||
629.e: The kings were sitting with pomp and show at various places.30.

629.g: ਜਿਹ ਜਿਹ ਦੇਖਾ ਸੋ ਸੋ ਰੀਝਾ ॥
629.t: jeh jeh dhekhaa so so reejhaa ||

629.g: ਜਿਨ ਨਹੀ ਦੇਖਾ ਤਿਹ ਮਨ ਖੀਝਾ ॥
629.t: jin nahee dhekhaa teh man kheejhaa ||
629.e: Whosoever saw this, he was pleased and he who did not see this, he got angry in his mind

629.g: ਕਰਿ ਕਰਿ ਭਾਯੰ ਤ੍ਰੀਅ ਬਰ ਨਾਚੈ ॥
629.t: kar kar bhaaya(n) treea bar naachai ||

629.e: The women were dancing, exhibiting various kinds of emotions and there was wonderful emotional play from every limb of theirs.31.

629.g: ਤਿਨ ਅਤਿਭੁਤਿ ਗਤਿ ਤਹ ਜਹ ਠਾਨੀ ॥
629.t: tin atibhut gat teh jeh Thaanee ||

629.g: ਜਹ ਤਹ ਸੋਹੈ ਮੁਨਿ ਮਨਿ ਮਾਨੀ ॥
629.t: jeh teh sohai mun man maanee ||
629.e: Those women also decided to do something marvelous at that place, because there were sitting there some persistent sages

629.g: ਤਜਿ ਤਜਿ ਜੋਗੰ ਭਜਿ ਭਜਿ ਆਵੈ ॥
629.t: taj taj joga(n) bhaj bhaj aavai ||

629.g: ਲਖਿ ਅਤਿ ਆਭਾ ਜੀਅ ਸੁਖ ਪਾਵੈ ॥੩੨॥
629.t: lakh at aabhaa jeea sukh paavai ||32||
629.e: The Yogis leaving their meditation came running and seeing the glory of this function, they were pleased.32.

629.g: ਬਨਿ ਬਨਿ ਬੈਠੇ ਜਹ ਤਹ ਰਾਜਾ ॥
629.t: ban ban baiThe jeh teh raajaa ||

629.g: ਜਹ ਤਹ ਸੋਭੈ ਸਭ ਸੁਭ ਸਾਜਾ ॥
629.t: jeh teh sobhai sabh subh saajaa ||
629.e: Wherever the kings were sitting well-bedecked, the atmosphere of that place seemed extremely splendid

629.g: ਜਹ ਤਹ ਦੇਖੈ ਗੁਨਿ ਗਨ ਫੂਲੇ ॥
629.t: jeh teh dhekhai gun gan foole ||

629.g: ਮੁਨਿ ਮਨਿ ਛਬਿ ਲਖਿ ਤਨ ਮਨ ਭੂਲੇ ॥੩੩॥
629.t: mun man chhab lakh tan man bhoole ||33||
629.e: The kings were filled with pleasure here and there, accomplished with their qualities and servants and the sages seeing their magnificence, had forgotten the consciousness of their mind and body.33.

629.g: ਤਤ ਬਿਤ ਘਨ ਮੁਖਰਸ ਸਬ ਬਾਜੈ ॥
629.t: tat bit ghan mukharas sab baajai ||

629.g: ਸੁਨਿ ਮਨ ਰਾਗੰ ਗੁਨਿ ਗਨ ਲਾਜੈ ॥
629.t: sun man raaga(n) gun gan laajai ||
629.e: The stringed musical instruments were being played there and hearing their pleasing musical modes, the experts of musicology were feeling shy

629.g: ਜਹ ਤਹ ਗਿਰ ਗੇ ਰਿਝਿ ਰਿਝਿ ਐਸੇ ॥
629.t: jeh teh gir ge rijh rijh aaise ||

629.g: ਜਨੁ ਭਟ ਜੂਝੇ ਰਣ ਬ੍ਰਿਣ ਕੈਸੇ ॥੩੪॥
629.t: jan bhaT joojhe ran biran kaise ||34||
629.e: Hearing the tunes of the musical instruments, the kings fell down here and there like the warriors lying wounded in the battlefield.34.

629.g: ਬਨਿ ਬਨਿ ਫੂਲੇ ਜਨੁ ਬਰ ਫੂਲੰ ॥
629.t: ban ban foole jan bar foola(n) ||

629.g: ਤਨੁ ਬਰੁ ਸੋਭੇ ਜਨੁ ਧਰ ਮੂਲੰ ॥
629.t: tan bar sobhe jan dhar moola(n) ||
629.e: They seemed to have blossomed like the flowers of the forest and their bodies were exhibiting the fundamental emotion of the earthly comfort

629.g: ਜਹੰ ਤਹੰ ਝੂਲੇ ਮਦ ਮਤ ਰਾਜਾ ॥
629.t: jaha(n) taha(n) jhoole madh mat raajaa ||

629.g: ਜਨੁ ਮੁਰਿ ਬੋਲੈ ਸੁਨ ਘਨ ਗਾਜਾ ॥੩੫॥
629.t: jan mur bolai sun ghan gaajaa ||35||
629.e: The intoxicated kings were swinging here and there like the peacocks getting intoxicated hearing the thundering of clouds.35.
PAADHARI STANZA
Seeing the splendour here and there, the kings sat down

629.g: ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਕਹੈ ਨਹੀ ਪਰਤ ਬੈਨ ॥
629.t: eeh bhaat kahai nahee parat bain ||

629.e: Their glory cannot be described and seeing their figures, the eyes were getting pleased.36.
Seeing the colourful dance of this kind, the god of love was pulling his bow and discharging his arrows on the kings
The great glory of the atmosphere is indescribable and all were getting pleased on seeing it.37.

630.e: It seemed that this was the first day of spring

630.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਸਮਾਨ ਨਹੀ ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਹੈਸ ॥੩੮॥
630.t: tin ke samaan nahee i(n)dhr hais ||38||
630.e: In this way, seeing the whole assembly, all the kings sat down there in their glory as if they excelled even Indra.38.

630.g: ਇਕ ਮਾਸ ਲਾਗ ਤਹ ਭਇਓ ਨਾਚ ॥
630.t: eik maas laag teh bhio naach ||

630.g: ਬਿਨ ਪੀਐ ਕੈਫ ਕੋਊ ਨ ਬਾਚ ॥
630.t: bin peeaai kaif kouoo na baach ||
630.e: In this, way, the dancing continued there for one month and no one could save himself from drinking the wine of that dance

630.g: ਤਹ ਤਹ ਸੁ ਰਾਜ ਰਾਜਨ ਕੁਮਾਰ ॥੩੯॥
630.t: teh teh su raaj raajan kumaar ||39||
630.e: Here, there and everywhere the beauty of the kings and princes was seen.39.

630.g: ਜਿਹ ਕੋ ਜਪੰਤ ਸਭ ਜਗਤ ਜਾਪ ॥
630.t: jeh ko japa(n)t sabh jagat jaap ||
630.e: Sarasvati, the goddess worshipped by the world, said to the princess,

630.g: ਜਾ ਕੀ ਸਮਾਨ ਨਹੀ ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਸਾਜ ॥੪੦॥
630.t: jaa kee samaan nahee i(n)dhr saaj ||40||
630.e: “O princess! Look at these princes, who even excel Indra.”40.
The princess looked towards the group of princes and did not even like the prince of Sindhu-kingdom

630.g: ਜਨੁ ਸਰਬ ਸੋਭ ਕਹੁ ਲੀਲ ਲੀਸੁ ॥੪੧॥
630.t: jan sarab sobh kahu leel lees ||41||
630.e: Leaving him, absorbing all the glory within herself, she moved further.41.
Sarasvati said to her again, “Here is a king of the West, you may see him
The princess saw his natural features, but she did not like him also.42.
MADHUBHAAR STANZA
“O princess! Look towards these elegantly dressed warrior-kings of the countery.”43.
The princess saw towards the natural features of many kings thoughtfully and that supremely immaculate damsel even did not like the king of the West.44.
Then that girl moved forward and began to smile like the flash of lightning amongst the clouds.45.
The kings were getting allured on seeing her and the heavenly damsels were getting angry
They were enraged because they found the princess more beautiful than themselves.46.
The kings of charming forms and apparently beauty-incarnate and of supreme glory were there.47.
The princess saw the kings standing there and also saw amongst them the sovereign of Mulatan.48.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

630.g: ਚਲੀ ਛੋਡਿ ਤਾ ਕੌ ਤ੍ਰੀਆ ਰਾਜ ਐਸੇ ॥
630.t: chalee chhodd taa kau treeaa raaj aaise ||

630.g: ਮਨੋ ਪਾਡੁ ਪੁਤ੍ਰੰ ਸਿਰੀ ਰਾਜ ਜੈਸੇ ॥
630.t: mano paadd putra(n) siree raaj jaise ||
630.e: Leaving all of them, the princess moved forward like the Pandavas, the sons of Pandu, moving away after leaving their kingdom etc.

630.g: ਮਨੋ ਜ੍ਵਾਲ ਮਾਲਾ ਮਹਾ ਮੋਨਿ ਮੋਹੈ ॥੪੯॥
630.t: mano javaiaal maalaa mahaa mon mohai ||49||
630.e: Standing in the royal court, she appeared like the fascinating fire-flame.49.
Standing in the royal court she appeared like the portrait of painter

630.g: ਬਧੇ ਸ੍ਵਰਣ ਕੀ ਕਿੰਕਣੀ ਲਾਲ ਮਾਲੰ ॥
630.t: badhe savairan kee ki(n)kanee laal maala(n) ||

630.g: ਸਿਖਾ ਜਾਨ ਸੋਭੇ ਨ੍ਰਿਪੰ ਜਗਿ ਜ੍ਵਾਲੰ ॥੫੦॥
630.t: sikhaa jaan sobhe nirapa(n) jag javaiaala(n) ||50||
630.e: She was wearing a golden ornament (Kinkini) fitted with wreath of gems the pigtail of her hair was apparently like fire for the kings.50.

630.g: ਲਖੋ ਨੈਨਿ ਠਾਢੇ ਸਭੈ ਭੂਪ ਆਲਾ ॥
630.t: lakho nain Thaadde sabhai bhoop aalaa ||
630.e: Sarasvati, seeing the damsel said to her again, “O princess! See these superb kings

630.g: ਰੁਚੈ ਚਿਤ ਜਉਨੈ ਸੁਈ ਨਾਥ ਕੀਜੈ ॥
630.t: ruchai chit jaunai suiee naath keejai ||

630.g: ਸੁਨੋ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਪਿਆਰੀ ਇਹੈ ਮਾਨਿ ਲੀਜੈ ॥੫੧॥
630.t: suno praan piaaree ihai maan leejai ||51||
630.e: O my beloved! Obey my saying wed him, whom you consider worthy in your mind.51.

630.g: ਬਡੀ ਬਾਹਨੀ ਸੰਗਿ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਬਿਰਾਜੈ ॥
630.t: baddee baahanee sa(n)g jaa ke biraajai ||

630.g: ਘੁਰੈ ਸੰਗ ਭੇਰੀ ਮਹਾ ਨਾਦ ਬਾਜੈ ॥
630.t: ghurai sa(n)g bheree mahaa naadh baajai ||
630.e: “He, with whom there is a large army and the conches, battledrums and the war-horns are being played, see this great king
Whose thousand arms make the day appear as night.52.

630.g: ਧੁਜਾ ਮਧਿ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਬਡੋ ਸਿੰਘ ਰਾਜੈ ॥
630.t: dhujaa madh jaa ke baddo si(n)gh raajai ||

630.g: ਸੁਨੇ ਨਾਦ ਤਾ ਕੋ ਮਹਾ ਪਾਪ ਭਾਜੈ ॥
630.t: sune naadh taa ko mahaa paap bhaajai ||
630.e: “In whose banner, there is seated a huge lion and hearing whose voice, the great sins are eliminated

630.g: ਸੁਨੋ ਬੈਨ ਬਾਲਾ ਸੁਰੂਪੰ ਸੁ ਭਾਨੰ ॥੫੩॥
630.t: suno bain baalaa suroopa(n) su bhaana(n) ||53||
630.e: O princess! See that sun-faced great king of the East.53.
“Here the kettledrums, conches and drums are being played
The tones and tunes of many other instruments are being heard also the drums, anklets etc. are being played.54.

630.g: ਬਧੇ ਹੀਰ ਚੀਰੰ ਸੁ ਬੀਰੰ ਸੁਬਾਹੰ ॥
630.t: badhe heer cheera(n) su beera(n) subaaha(n) ||

630.e: The warriors are wearing beautiful garments

631.g: ਨਹੇ ਪਿੰਗ ਬਾਜੀ ਰਥੰ ਜੇਣਿ ਜਾਨੋ ॥
631.t: nahe pi(n)g baajee ratha(n) jen jaano ||

631.g: ਤਿਸੈ ਦਛਨੇਸੰ ਹੀਐ ਬਾਲ ਮਾਨੋ ॥੫੫॥
631.t: tisai dhachhanesa(n) heeaai baal maano ||55||
631.e: And the canopied king is looking splendid alongwith his army he, whose chariot and its horses destroy large and mountain-sized warriors O princess! He is the king of the South.55.

631.g: ਮਹਾ ਬਾਹਨੀਸੰ ਨਗੀਸੰ ਨਰੇਸੰ ॥
631.t: mahaa baahaneesa(n) nageesa(n) naresa(n) ||

631.g: ਕਈ ਕੋਟਿ ਪਾਤੰ ਸੁਭੈ ਪਤ੍ਰ ਭੇਸੰ ॥
631.t: kiee koT paata(n) subhai patr bhesa(n) ||

631.g: ਧੁਜਾ ਬਧ ਉਧੰ ਗਜੰ ਗੂੜ ਬਾਕੋ ॥
631.t: dhujaa badh udha(n) gaja(n) gooR baako ||

631.g: ਲਖੋ ਉਤਰੀ ਰਾਜ ਕੈ ਨਾਮ ਤਾ ਕੋ ॥੫੬॥
631.t: lakho utaree raaj kai naam taa ko ||56||
631.e: “The king who has a great army and in which there are millions of soldiers on foot in green uniforms, and whose beautiful elephants tied with banners, are roaming, O princess! He is the king of the North.56.

631.g: ਫਰੀ ਧੋਪ ਪਾਇਕ ਸੁ ਆਗੇ ਉਮੰਗੈ ॥
631.t: faree dhop paik su aage uma(n)gai ||

631.g: ਜਿਣੈ ਕੋਟਿ ਬੰਕੈ ਮੁਰੇ ਨਾਹਿ ਅੰਗੈ ॥
631.t: jinai koT ba(n)kai mure naeh a(n)gai ||

631.g: ਹਰੇ ਬਾਜ ਰਾਜੰ ਕਪੋਤੰ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਨੰ ॥
631.t: hare baaj raaja(n) kapota(n) pramaana(n) ||

631.g: ਨਹੇ ਸ੍ਰਯੰਦਨੀ ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਬਾਜੀ ਸਮਾਣੰ ॥੫੭॥
631.t: nahe sraya(n)dhanee i(n)dhr baajee samaana(n) ||57||
631.e: “He, before whom the army on foot is moving enthusiastically, and who after conquering millions, has not turned away from the war, whose horses are like pigeons and who has such chariots which are not even with Indra.57.

631.g: ਬਡੇ ਸ੍ਰਿੰਗ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਧਰੇ ਸੂਰ ਸੋਭੈ ॥
631.t: badde sira(n)g jaa ke dhare soor sobhai ||

631.g: ਲਖੇ ਦੈਤ ਕੰਨ੍ਯਾ ਜਿਨੈ ਚਿਤ ਲੋਭੈ ॥
631.t: lakhe dhait ka(n)nayaa jinai chit lobhai ||

631.g: ਕਢੇ ਦੰਤ ਪਤੰ ਸਿਰੰ ਕੇਸ ਉਚੰ ॥
631.t: kadde dha(n)t pata(n) sira(n) kes ucha(n) ||

631.g: ਲਖੇ ਗਰਭਣੀ ਆਣਿ ਕੇ ਗਰਭ ਮੁਚੰ ॥੫੮॥
631.t: lakhe garabhanee aan ke garabh mucha(n) ||58||
631.e: “He, with whom there are warriors of the size of the peaks of the mountains and seeing whom, the damsels of the demons get fascinated, smile and wave the hair of their heads and in whose fear the pregnant women lose their pregnancies.58.

631.g: ਲਖੋ ਲੰਕ ਏਸੰ ਨਰੇਸੰ ਸੁ ਬਾਲੰ ॥
631.t: lakho la(n)k esa(n) naresa(n) su baala(n) ||

631.g: ਸਬੈ ਸੰਗ ਜਾ ਕੈ ਸਬੈ ਲੋਕ ਪਾਲੰ ॥
631.t: sabai sa(n)g jaa kai sabai lok paala(n) ||
631.e: “That mighty one is the king of Lanka (Ceylon), in whose company there are also Lokpals

631.g: ਲੁਟਿਓ ਏਕ ਬੇਰੰ ਕੁਬੇਰੰ ਭੰਡਾਰੀ ॥
631.t: luTio ek bera(n) kubera(n) bha(n)ddaaree ||

631.g: ਜਿਣਿਓ ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਰਾਜਾ ਬਡੋ ਛਤ੍ਰਧਾਰੀ ॥੫੯॥
631.t: jinio i(n)dhr raajaa baddo chhatradhaaree ||59||
631.e: He had once looted the store of Kuber and had also defeated the mighty Indra.59.

631.g: ਕਹੇ ਜਉਨ ਬਾਲੀ ਨ ਤੇ ਚਿਤ ਆਨੇ ॥
631.t: kahe jaun baalee na te chit aane ||

631.g: ਜਿਤੇ ਭੂਪ ਭਾਰੀ ਸੁ ਪਾਛੇ ਬਖਾਨੇ ॥
631.t: jite bhoop bhaaree su paachhe bakhaane ||
631.e: “O princess! Tell me what is in your mind? The mention of the great kings has already been made

631.g: ਚਹੂੰ ਓਰ ਰਾਜਾ ਕਹੋ ਨਾਮ ਸੋ ਭੀ ॥
631.t: chahoo(n) or raajaa kaho naam so bhee ||

631.g: ਤਜੇ ਭਾਤਿ ਜੈਸੀ ਸਬੈ ਰਾਜ ਓ ਭੀ ॥੬੦॥
631.t: taje bhaat jaisee sabai raaj o bhee ||60||
631.e: There are kings and kings on all the four sides, but you have equally abandoned them all.60.

631.g: ਲਖੋ ਦਈਤ ਸੈਨਾ ਬਡੀ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਾ ਕੇ ॥
631.t: lakho dhieet sainaa baddee sa(n)g taa ke ||

631.g: ਸੁਭੈ ਛਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰੀ ਬਡੇ ਸੰਗ ਜਾ ਕੇ ॥
631.t: subhai chhatr dhaaree badde sa(n)g jaa ke ||
631.e: “See that one who has a great army of demons with him

631.g: ਧੁਜਾ ਗਿਧ ਉਧੰ ਲਸੈ ਕਾਕ ਪੂਰੰ ॥
631.t: dhujaa gidh udha(n) lasai kaak poora(n) ||

631.g: ਤਿਸੈ ਪਿਆਲ ਰਾਜਾ ਬਲੀ ਬ੍ਰਿਧ ਨੂਰੰ ॥੬੧॥
631.t: tisai piaal raajaa balee biradh noora(n) ||61||
631.e: And with whom there are many canopied kings on whose banner the vultures and crows are sitting you may love that mighty king.61.

631.g: ਰਥੰ ਬੇਸਟੰ ਹੀਰ ਚੀਰੰ ਅਪਾਰੰ ॥
631.t: ratha(n) besaTa(n) heer cheera(n) apaara(n) ||

631.g: ਸੁਭੈ ਸੰਗ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਸਭੇ ਲੋਕ ਪਾਰੰ ॥
631.t: subhai sa(n)g jaa ke sabhe lok paara(n) ||
631.e: “He, who has charming garments and chariots and with whom there are all the Lokpals

631.g: ਇਹੈ ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਰਾਜਾ ਦੁਰੰ ਦਾਨਵਾਰੰ ॥
631.t: eihai i(n)dhr raajaa dhura(n) dhaanavaara(n) ||

631.g: ਤ੍ਰੀਆ ਤਾਸ ਚੀਨੋ ਅਦਿਤਿਆ ਕੁਮਾਰੰ ॥੬੨॥
631.t: treeaa taas cheeno adhitiaa kumaara(n) ||62||
631.e: Even the king Indra conceals himself in fear because of his fame as a Donor O friend! He is the same Aditya Kumar.62.

631.g: ਨਹੇ ਸਪਤ ਬਾਜੀ ਰਥੰ ਏਕ ਚਕ੍ਰੰ ॥
631.t: nahe sapat baajee ratha(n) ek chakra(n) ||

631.g: ਮਹਾ ਨਾਗ ਬਧੰ ਤਪੈ ਤੇਜ ਬਕ੍ਰੰ ॥
631.t: mahaa naag badha(n) tapai tej bakra(n) ||
631.e: “He, in whose chariot, there are seven horses and who can even destroy Sheshnaga with his glory

631.g: ਮਹਾ ਉਗ੍ਰ ਧੰਨ੍ਵਾ ਸੁ ਆਜਾਨ ਬਾਹੰ ॥
631.t: mahaa ugr dha(n)navaiaa su aajaan baaha(n) ||

631.g: ਸਹੀ ਚਿਤ ਚੀਨੋ ਤਿਸੈ ਦਿਉਸ ਨਾਹੰ ॥੬੩॥
631.t: sahee chit cheeno tisai dhiaus naaha(n) ||63||
631.e: Who has long arms and dreadful bow, recognize him as dinkar of Surya.63.

631.g: ਚੜਿਓ ਏਣ ਰਾਜੰ ਧਰੇ ਬਾਣ ਪਾਣੰ ॥
631.t: chaRio en raaja(n) dhare baan paana(n) ||

631.g: ਨਿਸਾ ਰਾਜ ਤਾ ਕੋ ਲਖੋ ਤੇਜ ਮਾਣੰ ॥
631.t: nisaa raaj taa ko lakho tej maana(n) ||

631.g: ਕਰੈ ਰਸਮਿ ਮਾਲਾ ਉਜਾਲਾ ਪਰਾਨੰ ॥
631.t: karai rasam maalaa ujaalaa paraana(n) ||

631.g: ਜਪੈ ਰਾਤ੍ਰ ਦਿਉਸੰ ਸਹੰਸ੍ਰੀ ਭੁਜਾਨੰ ॥੬੪॥
631.t: japai raatr dhiausa(n) saha(n)sree bhujaana(n) ||64||
631.e: “He, whom you see coming with his bow and arrow, he is the king of the night, the brilliant Chandra, who lightens up for all the creatures and whom thousands of people remember day and night.64.

631.g: ਚੜੇ ਮਹਿਖੀਸੰ ਸੁਮੇਰੰ ਜੁ ਦੀਸੰ ॥
631.t: chaRe mahikheesa(n) sumera(n) ju dheesa(n) ||

631.g: ਮਹਾ ਕ੍ਰੂਰ ਕਰਮੰ ਜਿਣਿਓ ਬਾਹ ਬੀਸੰ ॥
631.t: mahaa kraoor karama(n) jinio baeh beesa(n) ||
631.e: “This one, who while going for war, seems like a mountain and who has conquered greatly tyrannical, multi-armed kings

631.g: ਧੁਜਾ ਦੰਡ ਜਾ ਕੀ ਪ੍ਰਚੰਡੰ ਬਿਰਾਜੈ ॥
631.t: dhujaa dha(n)dd jaa kee pracha(n)dda(n) biraajai ||

631.g: ਲਖੇ ਜਾਸ ਗਰਬੀਨ ਕੋ ਗਰਬ ਭਾਜੈ ॥੬੫॥
631.t: lakhe jaas garabeen ko garab bhaajai ||65||
631.e: His banner is powerfully exhibiting its glory, seeing which, the pride of many egoists is shattered.65.

631.g: ਕਹਾ ਲੌ ਬਖਾਨੋ ਬਡੇ ਗਰਬਧਾਰੀ ॥
631.t: kahaa lau bakhaano badde garabadhaaree ||

631.g: ਸਬੈ ਘੇਰਿ ਠਾਢੇ ਜੁਰੀ ਭੀਰ ਭਾਰੀ ॥
631.t: sabai gher Thaadde juree bheer bhaaree ||
631.e: “To what extent should I describe these great egoists? All of them are standing in groups and surrounding others

631.g: ਨਚੈ ਪਾਤਰਾ ਚਾਤੁਰਾ ਨਿਰਤਕਾਰੀ ॥
631.t: nachai paataraa chaaturaa niratakaaree ||

631.g: ਉਠੈ ਝਾਝ ਸਬਦੰ ਸੁਨੈ ਲੋਗ ਧਾਰੀ ॥੬੬॥
631.t: auThai jhaajh sabadha(n) sunai log dhaaree ||66||
631.e: The comely and clever prositiutes are dancing and the voice of the musical instruments is being heard.66.

631.g: ਬਡੋ ਦਿਰਬ ਧਾਰੀ ਬਡੀ ਸੈਨ ਲੀਨੇ ॥
631.t: baddo dhirab dhaaree baddee sain leene ||

631.g: ਬਡੋ ਦਿਰਬ ਕੋ ਚਿਤ ਮੈ ਗਰਬ ਕੀਨੇ ॥
631.t: baddo dhirab ko chit mai garab keene ||
631.e: “The great wealthy kings taking their armies with themselves and taking pride in their riche, are seated here

632.g: ਚਿਤੰ ਤਾਸ ਚੀਨੋ ਸਹੀ ਦਿਰਬ ਪਾਲੰ ॥
632.t: chita(n) taas cheeno sahee dhirab paala(n) ||

632.g: ਉਠੈ ਜਉਨ ਕੇ ਰੂਪ ਕੀ ਜ੍ਵਾਲ ਮਾਲੰ ॥੬੭॥
632.t: auThai jaun ke roop kee javaiaal maala(n) ||67||
632.e: O princess! see that king, the master of riches, from whose body the fires of beauty are arising.”67.

632.g: ਸਭੈ ਭੂਪ ਠਾਢੇ ਜਹਾ ਰਾਜ ਕੰਨਿਆ ॥
632.t: sabhai bhoop Thaadde jahaa raaj ka(n)niaa ||

632.g: ਬਿਖੈ ਭੂ ਤਲੰ ਰੂਪ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਨ ਅੰਨਿਆ ॥
632.t: bikhai bhoo tala(n) roop jaa ke na a(n)niaa ||
632.e: Where there was the princess, all the kings were standing there

632.g: ਬਡੇ ਛਤ੍ਰਧਾਰੀ ਬਡੇ ਗਰਬ ਕੀਨੇ ॥
632.t: badde chhatradhaaree badde garab keene ||

632.g: ਤਹਾ ਆਨਿ ਠਾਢੇ ਬਡੀ ਸੈਨ ਲੀਨੇ ॥੬੮॥
632.t: tahaa aan Thaadde baddee sain leene ||68||
632.e: There was none other so beautiful on the earth many egoistic canopied kings, taking their armies with them, came and stood there.68.

632.g: ਨਦੀ ਸੰਗ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਸਬੈ ਰੂਪ ਧਾਰੇ ॥
632.t: nadhee sa(n)g jaa ke sabai roop dhaare ||

632.g: ਸਬੈ ਸਿੰਧ ਸੰਗੰ ਚੜੇ ਤੇਜ ਵਾਰੇ ॥
632.t: sabai si(n)dh sa(n)ga(n) chaRe tej vaare ||
632.e: “He, form whom the streams adopt the glory of their comeliness and from whom the oceans also spring up, not enduring His brilliance

632.g: ਬਡੀ ਕਾਇ ਜਾ ਕੀ ਮਹਾ ਰੂਪ ਸੋਹੈ ॥
632.t: baddee kai jaa kee mahaa roop sohai ||

632.g: ਲਖੇ ਦੇਵ ਕੰਨਿਆਨ ਕੇ ਮਾਨ ਮੋਹੈ ॥੬੯॥
632.t: lakhe dhev ka(n)niaan ke maan mohai ||69||
632.e: He, whose body is very big and whose beauty is magnificent and seeing whom, the heavenly maidens get allured.69.

632.g: ਕਹੋ ਨਾਰ ਤੋ ਕੌ ਇਹੈ ਬਰੁਨ ਰਾਜਾ ॥
632.t: kaho naar to kau ihai barun raajaa ||

632.g: ਜਿਸੈ ਪੇਖਿ ਰਾਜਾਨ ਕੋ ਮਾਨ ਭਾਜਾ ॥
632.t: jisai pekh raajaan ko maan bhaajaa ||
632.e: “O princess! All those different kings have come here seeing whom the pride of the kings is shattered

632.g: ਕਹਾ ਲੌ ਬਖਾਨੋ ਜਿਤੇ ਭੂਪ ਆਏ ॥
632.t: kahaa lau bakhaano jite bhoop aae ||

632.g: ਸਬੈ ਬਾਲ ਕੌ ਲੈ ਭਵਾਨੀ ਬਤਾਏ ॥੭੦॥
632.t: sabai baal kau lai bhavaanee bataae ||70||
632.e: To what extent should I describe those kings who have come here?” That goddess showed the princess all those kings.70.

632.g: ਸਵੈਯਾ ॥
632.t: savaiyaa ||
632.e: SWAYYA

632.g: ਆਨਿ ਜੁਰੇ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਮੰਡਲ ਜੇਤਿ ਤੇਤ ਸਬੈ ਤਿਨ ਤਾਸ ਦਿਖਾਏ ॥
632.t: aan jure nirap ma(n)ddal jet tet sabai tin taas dhikhaae ||
632.e: All those kings who had come there, they were all shown to the princess

632.g: ਦੇਖ ਫਿਰੀ ਚਹੂੰ ਚਕ੍ਰਨ ਕੋ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਰਾਜ ਕੁਮਾਰਿ ਹ੍ਰਿਦੈ ਨਹੀ ਲਿਆਏ ॥
632.t: dhekh firee chahoo(n) chakran ko nirap raaj kumaar hiradhai nahee liaae ||
632.e: She saw the kings in all the four directions, but did not like anyone

632.g: ਹਾਰਿ ਪਰਿਓ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਭਟ ਮੰਡਲ ਭੂਪਤਿ ਹੇਰਿ ਦਸਾ ਮੁਰਝਾਏ ॥
632.t: haar pario sabh hee bhaT ma(n)ddal bhoopat her dhasaa murajhaae ||
632.e: The whole sphere of heroes was defeated and seeing such a situation, the kings also became dejected

632.g: ਫੂਕ ਭਏ ਮੁਖ ਸੂਕ ਗਏ ਸਬ ਰਾਜ ਕੁਮਾਰਿ ਫਿਰੇ ਘਰਿ ਆਏ ॥੭੧॥
632.t: fook bhe mukh sook ge sab raaj kumaar fire ghar aae ||71||
632.e: The faces of all of them shrank and all the princes returned to their homes.71.

632.g: ਤਉ ਲਗਿ ਆਨ ਗਏ ਅਜਿਰਾਜ ਸੁ ਰਾਜਨ ਰਾਜ ਬਡੋ ਦਲ ਲੀਨੇ ॥
632.t: tau lag aan ge ajiraaj su raajan raaj baddo dhal leene ||

632.g: ਅੰਬਰ ਅਨੂਪ ਧਰੇ ਪਸਮੰਬਰ ਸੰਬਰ ਕੇ ਅਰਿ ਕੀ ਛਬਿ ਛੀਨੇ ॥
632.t: a(n)bar anoop dhare pasama(n)bar sa(n)bar ke ar kee chhab chheene ||
632.e: At that time, the king Aj, taking alongwith him him his big army, reached there, his unique silken garments were making the god of love feel shy

632.g: ਬੇਖਨ ਬੇਖ ਚੜੇ ਸੰਗ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਹਾਨ ਸਬੈ ਸੁਖ ਧਾਮ ਨਵੀਨੇ ॥
632.t: bekhan bekh chaRe sa(n)g havai nirap haan sabai sukh dhaam naveene ||
632.e: There were also many well-dressed other kings affording pleasure

632.g: ਆਨਿ ਗਏ ਜਰਿਕੰਬਰ ਸੇ ਅੰਬਰ ਸੇ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਕੰਬਰ ਕੀਨੇ ॥੭੨॥
632.t: aan ge jarika(n)bar se a(n)bar se nirap ka(n)bar keene ||72||
632.e: The king Aj, wearing handsome garments reached there.72.

632.g: ਪਾਤਿ ਹੀ ਪਾਤਿ ਬਨਾਇ ਬਡੋ ਦਲ ਢੋਲ ਮ੍ਰਿਦੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਬਜਾਇ ॥
632.t: paat hee paat banai baddo dhal ddol miradha(n)g sura(n)g bajai ||
632.e: His army made queues and his forces began to play on the small and big durms

632.g: ਭੂਖਨ ਚਾਰੁ ਦਿਪੈ ਸਬ ਅੰਗ ਬਿਲੋਕਿ ਅਨੰਗ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ਮੁਰਛਾਏ ॥
632.t: bhookhan chaar dhipai sab a(n)g bilok ana(n)g prabhaa murachhaae ||
632.e: On the bodies of al, the handsome ornaments were shining and the god of love also seeting their comeliness, was becoming unconscious

632.g: ਬਾਜਤ ਚੰਗ ਮ੍ਰਿਦੰਗ ਉਪੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਸੁ ਨਾਦ ਸਬੈ ਸੁਨਿ ਪਾਏ ॥
632.t: baajat cha(n)g miradha(n)g upa(n)g sura(n)g su naadh sabai sun paae ||

632.g: ਰੀਝ ਰਹੇ ਰਿਝਵਾਰ ਸਬੈ ਲਖਿ ਰੂਪ ਅਨੂਪ ਸਰਾਹਤ ਆਏ ॥੭੩॥
632.t: reejh rahe rijhavaar sabai lakh roop anoop saraahat aae ||73||
632.e: All were listening to the sounds of the musical instruments and all seeing their unique beauty, were getting pleased.73.

632.g: ਜੈਸ ਸਰੂਪ ਲਖਿਓ ਅਜਿ ਕੋ ਹਮ ਤੈਸ ਸਰੂਪ ਨ ਅਉਰ ਬਿਚਾਰੇ ॥
632.t: jais saroop lakhio aj ko ham tais saroop na aaur bichaare ||
632.e: The beauty of king Aj that we saw, had not seen the same beauty of anyone else before

632.g: ਚੰਦਿ ਚਪਿਓ ਲਖਿ ਕੈ ਮੁਖ ਕੀ ਛਬਿ ਛੇਦ ਪਰੇ ਉਰ ਮੈ ਰਿਸ ਮਾਰੇ ॥
632.t: cha(n)dh chapio lakh kai mukh kee chhab chhedh pare ur mai ris maare ||
632.e: The moon seeing his comeliness, hid himself and his heart burnt with jealousy

632.g: ਤੇਜ ਸਰੂਪ ਬਿਲੋਕਿ ਕੈ ਪਾਵਕ ਚਿਤਿ ਚਿਰੀ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਅਉਰਨ ਜਾਰੇ ॥
632.t: tej saroop bilok kai paavak chit chiree gireh aauran jaare ||
632.e: The fire seeing his elegance, was irritated and he abandoned his burning activity

632.g: ਜੈਸ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ਲਖਿਓ ਅਜਿ ਕੋ ਹਮ ਤੈਸ ਸਰੂਪ ਨ ਭੂਪ ਨਿਹਾਰੇ ॥੭੪॥
632.t: jais prabhaa lakhio aj ko ham tais saroop na bhoop nihaare ||74||
632.e: The kind of beauty that the king Aj has, the same beauty we have never seen before.74.

632.g: ਸੁੰਦਰ ਜੁਆਨ ਸਰੂਪ ਮਹਾਨ ਪ੍ਰਧਾਨ ਚਹੁੰ ਚਕ ਮੈ ਹਮ ਜਾਨਿਓ ॥
632.t: su(n)dhar juaan saroop mahaan pradhaan chahu(n) chak mai ham jaanio ||
632.e: He was winsome youth and had a shapely figure, which was considered foremost in all the four directions

632.g: ਭਾਨੁ ਸਮਾਨ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ਨ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਨ ਕਿ ਰਾਵ ਕਿ ਰਾਨ ਮਹਾਨ ਬਖਾਨਿਓ ॥
632.t: bhaan samaan prabhaa na pramaan k raav k raan mahaan bakhaanio ||
632.e: He was radiant like the sun and was a great sovereign amongst kings

632.g: ਦੇਵ ਅਦੇਵ ਚਕੇ ਅਪਨੇ ਚਿਤਿ ਚੰਦ ਸਰੂਪ ਨਿਸਾ ਪਹਿਚਾਨਿਓ ॥
632.t: dhev adhev chake apane chit cha(n)dh saroop nisaa pahichaanio ||
632.e: The gods and others were all wonder-struck to see him and the night considered him as moon

632.g: ਦਿਉਸ ਕੈ ਭਾਨੁ ਮੁਨਿਓ ਭਗਵਾਨ ਪਛਾਨ ਮਨੈ ਘਨ ਮੋਰਨ ਮਾਨਿਓ ॥੭੫॥
632.t: dhiaus kai bhaan munio bhagavaan pachhaan manai ghan moran maanio ||75||
632.e: The day imagined him as the sun and the peacocks thought of him as the cloud.75.

632.g: ਬੋਲਿ ਉਠੇ ਪਿਕ ਜਾਨ ਬਸੰਤ ਚਕੋਰਨ ਚੰਦ ਸਰੂਪ ਬਖਾਨਿਓ ॥
632.t: bol uThe pik jaan basa(n)t chakoran cha(n)dh saroop bakhaanio ||
632.e: The rain-birds raised their voice considering him as spring and the partridges thought of his as moon

632.g: ਸਾਤਿ ਸੁਭਾਵ ਲਖਿਓ ਸਭ ਸਾਧਨ ਜੋਧਨ ਕ੍ਰੋਧ ਪ੍ਰਤਛ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਨਿਓ ॥
632.t: saat subhaav lakhio sabh saadhan jodhan krodh pratachh pramaanio ||
632.e: The saints thought of him as peace and the warriors apparently as anger

632.g: ਬਾਲਨ ਬਾਲ ਸੁਭਾਵ ਲਖਿਓ ਤਿਹ ਸਤ੍ਰਨ ਕਾਲ ਸਰੂਪ ਪਛਾਨਿਓ ॥
632.t: baalan baal subhaav lakhio teh satran kaal saroop pachhaanio ||
632.e: The children considered him as a good-natured child and the enemies as KAL (death)

632.g: ਦੇਵਲ ਦੇਵ ਅਦੇਵਨ ਕੈ ਸਿਵ ਰਾਜਨ ਰਾਜਿ ਬਡੋ ਜੀਅ ਜਾਨਿਓ ॥੭੬॥
632.t: dheval dhev adhevan kai siv raajan raaj baddo jeea jaanio ||76||
632.e: The gods thought of him as god, the ghosts and fiends as Shiva and the kings as the Sovereign.76.

632.g: ਸਾਧਨ ਸਿਧ ਸਰੂਪ ਲਖਿਓ ਤਿਹ ਸਤ੍ਰਨ ਸਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਨ ਬਸੇਖਿਓ ॥
632.t: saadhan sidh saroop lakhio teh satran satr samaan basekhio ||
632.e: The saints saw him as a Siddha (adept) and the enemies as enemy

632.g: ਚੋਰਨ ਭੋਰ ਕਰੋਰਨ ਮੋਰਨ ਤਾਸੁ ਸਹੀ ਘਨ ਕੈ ਅਵਿਰੇਖਿਓ ॥
632.t: choran bhor karoran moran taas sahee ghan kai avirekhio ||
632.e: The thieves saw him s early morn and the peacocks as cloud

632.g: ਕਾਮ ਸਰੂਪ ਸਭੈ ਪੁਰ ਨਾਰਨ ਸੰਭੂ ਸਮਾਨ ਸਬੂ ਗਨ ਦੇਖਿਓ ॥
632.t: kaam saroop sabhai pur naaran sa(n)bhoo samaan saboo gan dhekhio ||
632.e: All the women considered him as god of love and all the ganas as Shiva

632.g: ਸੀਪ ਸ੍ਵਾਤਿ ਕੀ ਬੂੰਦ ਤਿਸੈ ਕਰਿ ਰਾਜਨ ਰਾਜ ਬਡੋ ਤਿਹ ਪੇਖਿਓ ॥੭੭॥
632.t: seep savaiaat kee boo(n)dh tisai kar raajan raaj baddo teh pekhio ||77||
632.e: The shell saw him as the rain-drop and the kings as the Sovereing.77.

632.g: ਕੰਬਰ ਜਿਉ ਜਰਿਕੰਬਰ ਕੀ ਢਿਗ ਤਿਉ ਅਵਿਨੰਬਰ ਤੀਰ ਸੁਹਾਏ ॥
632.t: ka(n)bar jiau jarika(n)bar kee ddig tiau avina(n)bar teer suhaae ||
632.e: The king Aj looked splendid on the earth just as the clouds in the sky

632.g: ਨਾਕ ਲਖੇ ਰਿਸ ਮਾਨ ਸੂਆ ਮਨ ਨੈਨ ਦੋਊ ਲਖਿ ਏਣ ਲਜਾਏ ॥
632.t: naak lakhe ris maan sooaa man nain dhouoo lakh en lajaae ||
632.e: Seeing his comely nose, the parrot got jealous and seeing both of his eyes, the wagtail felt shy

632.g: ਪੇਖਿ ਗੁਲਾਬ ਸਰਾਬ ਪੀਐ ਜਨੁ ਪੇਖਤ ਅੰਗ ਅਨੰਗ ਰਿਸਾਏ ॥
632.t: pekh gulaab saraab peeaai jan pekhat a(n)g ana(n)g risaae ||
632.e: Seeing his limbs, the rose got dead-drunks and the god of love got angry seeing his handsome neck

632.g: ਕੰਠ ਕਪੋਤ ਕਟੂ ਪਰ ਕੇਹਰ ਰੋਸ ਰਸੇ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਭੂਲਿ ਨ ਆਏ ॥੭੮॥
632.t: ka(n)Th kapot kaToo par kehar ros rase gireh bhool na aae ||78||
632.e: And the lions seeing his waist forgot themselves and were not able to reach their homes.78.

632.g: ਪੇਖਿ ਸਰੂਪ ਸਿਰਾਤ ਨ ਲੋਚਨ ਘੂਟਤ ਹੈ ਜਨੁ ਘੂਟ ਅਮੀ ਕੇ ॥
632.t: pekh saroop siraat na lochan ghooTat hai jan ghooT amee ke ||
632.e: Seeing his lake-like eyes, it seemed that they became intoxicated after drinking a draught of ambrosia

632.g: ਗਾਵਤ ਗੀਤ ਬਜਾਵਤ ਤਾਲ ਬਤਾਵਤ ਹੈ ਜਨੋ ਆਛਰ ਹੀ ਕੇ ॥
632.t: gaavat geet bajaavat taal bataavat hai jano aachhar hee ke ||
632.e: The songs were being sung and the musical instruments were being played

632.g: ਭਾਵਤ ਨਾਰਿ ਸੁਹਾਵਤ ਗਾਰ ਦਿਵਾਵਤ ਹੈ ਭਰਿ ਆਨੰਦ ਜੀ ਕੇ ॥
632.t: bhaavat naar suhaavat gaar dhivaavat hai bhar aana(n)dh jee ke ||

632.g: ਤੂ ਸੁ ਕੁਮਾਰ ਰਚੀ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਕਹੈ ਅਬਿਚਾਰ ਤ੍ਰੀਆ ਬਰ ਨੀਕੇ ॥੭੯॥
632.t: too su kumaar rachee karataar kahai abichaar treeaa bar neeke ||79||
632.e: The women in their pleasure were singing abusive songs and saying, “O prince! the Lord has created this princess for you, you may wed her.”79.

632.g: ਦੇਖਤ ਰੂਪ ਸਿਰਾਤ ਨ ਲੋਚਨ ਪੇਖਿ ਛਕੀ ਪੀਅ ਕੀ ਛਬਿ ਨਾਰੀ ॥
632.t: dhekhat roop siraat na lochan pekh chhakee peea kee chhab naaree ||

632.g: ਗਾਵਤ ਗੀਤ ਬਜਾਵਤ ਢੋਲ ਮ੍ਰਿਦੰਗ ਮੁਚੰਗਨ ਕੀ ਧੁਨਿ ਭਾਰੀ ॥
632.t: gaavat geet bajaavat ddol miradha(n)g mucha(n)gan kee dhun bhaaree ||
632.e: Seeing the glory of his eyes, the women were absorbed in love and were singing songs while playing on the drums

632.g: ਆਵਤ ਜਾਤ ਜਿਤੀ ਪੁਰ ਨਾਗਰ ਗਾਗਰਿ ਡਾਰਿ ਲਖੈ ਦੁਤਿ ਭਾਰੀ ॥
632.t: aavat jaat jitee pur naagar gaagar ddaar lakhai dhut bhaaree ||
632.e: All the women who were coming from outside the town, seeing he beauty of the king, they threw away their gowns and were only looking at his charming face

632.g: ਰਾਜ ਕਰੋ ਤਬ ਲੌ ਜਬ ਲੌ ਮਹਿ ਜਉ ਲਗ ਗੰਗ ਬਹੈ ਜਮੁਨਾ ਰੀ ॥੮੦॥
632.t: raaj karo tab lau jab lau meh jau lag ga(n)g bahai jamunaa ree ||80||
632.e: Seeing the king they all desired, “O king! let it be the God’s will that you may rule as long as th

632.g: ਜਉਨ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ਅਜਿ ਰਾਜ ਕੀ ਰਾਜਤ ਸੋ ਕਹਿ ਕੈ ਕਿਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਗਨਾਊ ॥
632.t: jaun prabhaa aj raaj kee raajat so keh kai keh bhaat ganaauoo ||
632.e: While describing the glory of king Aj. I accept that whatever similes the poets generally give,

632.g: ਜਉਨ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ਕਬਿ ਦੇਤ ਸਬੈ ਜੌ ਪੈ ਤਾਸ ਕਹੋ ਜੀਅ ਬੀਚ ਲਜਾਊ ॥
632.t: jaun prabhaa kab dhet sabai jau pai taas kaho jeea beech lajaauoo ||
632.e: They are all discourteous and I feel shy while uttering them

632.g: ਹਉ ਚਹੂੰ ਓਰ ਫਿਰਿਓ ਬਸੁਧਾ ਛਬਿ ਅੰਗਨ ਕੀਨ ਕਹੂੰ ਕੋਈ ਪਾਊ ॥
632.t: hau chahoo(n) or firio basudhaa chhab a(n)gan keen kahoo(n) koiee paauoo ||
632.e: I have searched on all the earth in order to find someone so beautiful as you, but I was not successful

632.g: ਲੇਖਨ ਊਖ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਜਾਤ ਲਿਖੋ ਛਬਿ ਆਨਨ ਤੇ ਕਿਮਿ ਭਾਖਿ ਸੁਨਾਊ ॥੮੧॥
632.t: lekhan uookh havai jaat likho chhab aanan te kim bhaakh sunaauoo ||81||
632.e: Writing about your beauty, my pen is pulled down and how should I describe it from my mouth ? 81.

632.g: ਨੈਨਨ ਬਾਨ ਚਹੂੰ ਦਿਸ ਮਾਰਤ ਘਾਇਲ ਕੈ ਪੁਰ ਬਾਸਨ ਡਾਰੀ ॥
632.t: nainan baan chahoo(n) dhis maarat ghail kai pur baasan ddaaree ||
632.e: The king with the arrows of his eyes, wounded all the townfolk

632.g: ਸਾਰਸ੍ਵਤੀ ਨ ਸਕੈ ਕਹਿ ਰੂਪ ਸਿੰਗਾਰ ਕਹੈ ਮਤਿ ਕਉਨ ਬਿਚਾਰੀ ॥
632.t: saarasavaitee na sakai keh roop si(n)gaar kahai mat kaun bichaaree ||
632.e: Even Saravati is uncable to describe the charm of his beauty

632.g: ਕੋਕਿਲ ਕੰਠਿ ਹਰਿਓ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਨਾਇਕ ਛੀਨ ਕਪੋਤ ਕੀ ਗ੍ਰੀਵ ਅਨਿਆਰੀ ॥
632.t: kokil ka(n)Th hario nirap naik chheen kapot kee greev aniaaree ||
632.e: The throat of the king is sweet like the nightingale and the neck like the pigeon

632.g: ਰੀਝ ਗਿਰੇ ਨਰ ਨਾਰਿ ਧਰਾ ਪਰ ਘੂਮਤਿ ਹੈ ਜਨੁ ਘਾਇਲ ਭਾਰੀ ॥੮੨॥
632.t: reejh gire nar naar dharaa par ghoomat hai jan ghail bhaaree ||82||
632.e: Seeing his beauty, all are falling down on earth and getting wounded.82.

632.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
632.t: dhoharaa ||
632.e: DOHRA

632.g: ਨਿਰਖਿ ਰੂਪ ਅਜਿ ਰਾਜ ਕੋ ਰੀਝ ਰਹੇ ਨਰ ਨਾਰਿ ॥
632.t: nirakh roop aj raaj ko reejh rahe nar naar ||

632.g: ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਕਿ ਚੰਦ੍ਰ ਕਿ ਸੂਰ ਇਹਿ ਇਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਕਰਤ ਬਿਚਾਰ ॥੮੩॥
632.t: ei(n)dhr k cha(n)dhr k soor ieh ieh bidh karat bichaar ||83||
632.e: The men and women are getting pleased on seeing the comeliness of form of king Aj and have not been able to decide whether he is Indra, Chandra of Surya.83.

632.g: ਕਬਿਤੁ ॥
632.t: kabit ||
632.e: KABIT

632.g: ਨਾਗਨ ਕੇ ਛਉਨਾ ਹੈਂ ਕਿ ਕੀਨੇ ਕਾਹੂੰ ਟਉਨਾ ਹੈਂ ਕਿ ਕਾਮ ਕੇ ਖਿਲਉਨਾ ਹੈਂ ਬਨਾਏ ਹੈਂ ਸੁਧਾਰ ਕੇ ॥
632.t: naagan ke chhaunaa hai(n) k keene kaahoo(n) Taunaa hai(n) k kaam ke khilaunaa hai(n) banaae hai(n) sudhaar ke ||
632.e: Either he is mercurial like the young ones of serpents or someone has seen him like the one, who casts spells on the king Aj, has been specially created like the toy of the god of love

632.g: ਇਸਤ੍ਰਿਨ ਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਹੈਂ ਕਿ ਸੁੰਦਰਤਾ ਕੀ ਖਾਨ ਹੈਂ ਕਿ ਕਾਮ ਕੇ ਕਲਾਨ ਬਿਧਿ ਕੀਨੇ ਹੈਂ ਬਿਚਾਰ ਕੇ ॥
632.t: eisatiran ke praan hai(n) k su(n)dharataa kee khaan hai(n) k kaam ke kalaan bidh keene hai(n) bichaar ke ||
632.e: The king Aj is the breath of like for women, he is the mine of beauty and is skilful in the sexual sports

632.g: ਚਾਤੁਰਤਾ ਕੇ ਭੇਸ ਹੈਂ ਕਿ ਰੂਪ ਕੇ ਨਰੇਸ ਹੈਂ ਕਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੁ ਦੇਸ ਏਸ ਕੀਨੇ ਚੰਦ੍ਰ ਸਾਰ ਕੇ ॥
632.t: chaaturataa ke bhes hai(n) k roop ke nares hai(n) k su(n)dhar su dhes es keene cha(n)dhr saar ke ||
632.e: He is the apparent manifestation of wisdom and amongst the kings he is charming like the moon

632.g: ਤੇਗ ਹੈਂ ਕਿ ਤੀਰ ਹੈਂ ਕਿ ਬਾਨਾ ਬਾਧੇ ਬੀਰ ਹੈਂ ਸੁ ਐਸੇ ਨੇਤ੍ਰ ਅਜਿ ਕੇ ਬਿਲੋਕੀਐ ਸੰਭਾਰ ਕੇ ॥੮੪॥
632.t: teg hai(n) k teer hai(n) k baanaa baadhe beer hai(n) su aaise netr aj ke bilokeeaai sa(n)bhaar ke ||84||
632.e: It is not clear whether he is the sword or the arrow or a bedecked warrior such a brave king Aj is being seen with great caution.84.

632.g: ਸਵੈਯਾ ॥
632.t: savaiyaa ||
632.e: SWAYYA

633.g: ਤੀਰਨ ਤੇ ਤਰਵਾਰਨ ਸੇ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਬਾਰਨ ਸੇ ਅਵਿਲੋਕਹੁ ਜਾਈ ॥
633.t: teeran te taravaaran se mirag baaran se avilokahu jaiee ||

633.g: ਰੀਝ ਰਹੀ ਰਿਝਵਾਰ ਲਖੇ ਦੁਤਿ ਭਾਖਿ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ਨਹੀ ਜਾਤ ਬਤਾਈ ॥
633.t: reejh rahee rijhavaar lakhe dhut bhaakh prabhaa nahee jaat bataiee ||
633.e: He is impressive like a sword or an arrow his simple beauty like the young one of a deer is worth seeing all are getting pleased on seeing him and his glory is indescribable

633.g: ਸੰਗਿ ਚਲੀ ਉਠਿ ਬਾਲ ਬਿਲੋਕਨ ਮੋਰ ਚਕੋਰ ਰਹੇ ਉਰਝਾਈ ॥
633.t: sa(n)g chalee uTh baal bilokan mor chakor rahe urajhaiee ||

633.g: ਡੀਠਿ ਪਰੈ ਅਜਿ ਰਾਜ ਜਬੈ ਚਿਤ ਦੇਖਤ ਹੀ ਤ੍ਰੀਅ ਲੀਨ ਚੁਰਾਈ ॥੮੫॥
633.t: ddeeTh parai aj raaj jabai chit dhekhat hee treea leen churaiee ||85||
633.e: The princess is moving forward to see him and seeing him, the peacocks and partridges have fallen in confusion the heart of that princess was fascinated, the moment she saw the king Aj.85.
TOMAR STANZA
When the princess saw the king, the treasure of beauty, she held her wreath of flowers with smile.86.
The charming damsel caught the garland in her hand and put it around the neck of the king, expert in eighteen sciences.87.
The goddess said to that princess, who was expert in all sciences, “O beautiful maiden like moonlight having charming eyes! listen to what I say.88.
“O princess full of charm and shyness! the king Aj is worthy match for you
You see him and listen to my speech”89.
The princess caught the wreath of flowers and put it around the neck of the king and
At that time many musical instruments including the lyre were played.90.
The tabor, drum, kettledrum and many other musical instruments of various tunes and tones were played
The flutes were played and there were many beautiful ladies of charming eyes seated there.91.
The king Aj wedded that damsel and taking various types of dowry and
Causing the tabor and lyre to be played, he retuned home with great happiness.92.
The king expert in eighteen sciences, was the ocean of pleasure and store of gentleness
He had conquered even Shiva in the war.93.
In this waay, he ruled and caused the canopy to be swung over his head and in the whole world,
The ceremonies regarding he divine kingship of that victorious king were performed.94.
The king Aj, after conquering all the four directions, gave charities of materials as a generous king
Being expert in all sciences, that king was extremely benevolent.95.
His eyes and body were so charming, hat even the god of love felt jealous

634.e: Hundreds of kings evaded him, seeing the moonlike beauty of his face.96.
In this way, the king ruled like a great sovereign in the world doing religious and social services and performing Yajnas
If I narrate all the things associated with him, the story will be greatly increased.97.
Therefore, I say in brief, O brothers! listen to it
The king Aj ruled in this way in various ways in religions and society.98.
He abandoned the idea of considering the whole world as his own and did not care for anyone
Then the great Death, in great rage, reduced king Aj to ashes in his fire.99.
Seeing the king Aj merging in the supreme Light, all the people became fearful like the passengers of a boat without the sailor
The people became weak like the individual becoming helpless with the loss of physical strength.100.
Just as a village becomes helpless without a headman, the earth becomes meaningless without fertility,
The treasure loses charm without wealth and the trader becomes in low spirit without the trade.101.
Without the king, the people became like poetry without meaning, friend without love,
The country without the king and as the army becomes helpless without the general.102.
That state becomes like a Yogi without knowledge, a king without kingdom,
The idea without the meaning and the donor without the material.103.
The people became like an elephant without a goad, the king without the army,
The warrior without weapons and the ideas without wiseom.104.
They are just like the wife without husband, the woman without beloved,
The poetry without wisdom and the friend without love.105.
They are just like the country becoming desolate, the women losing their husbands,
The Brahmins without learning or the men without wealth.106.
In this way, the kings, who ruled over this country, how can they be described?
Vyas, the store of Vedic learning, composed eighteen Puranas.107.
He composed eighteen parvas (parts of Mahabharata), listening which th whole world was pleased
In this way Vyas was the fifth incarnation of Brahma.108.

634.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਪੰਚਮੋਵਤਾਰ ਬ੍ਰਹਮਾ ਬਿਆਸ ਰਾਜਾ ਅਜ ਕੋ ਰਾਜ ਸਮਾਪਤੰ ॥੧੦॥੫॥
634.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the pa(n)chamovataar brahamaa biaas raajaa aj ko raaj samaapata(n) ||10||5||
634.e: End of the description of Vyas the fifth incarnation of Brahma and the rule of king Aj in Bachittar Natak.5.
Now begins the description of six sages, the sixth incarnation of Brahma
TOMAR STANZA
In this next Age, Vyas composed Puranas in the world and in doing this his prie was also increased
He also did not considered anyone equal to him.1.
Then the dreadful KAL (death) in his rage divided him into six parts with his great fires
Then they ware considered lowly.2.
His life-force was not terminated and form his six parts emerged six sages,
Who were the wupreme scholars of Shastras and they compsed six Shastras in their names.3.
These six sages of the lustre of Brahma and Yyas, brought to light six Shastras and in this way,
Brahma assumed the sixth incarnation made ideological improvements over the earth through six Shastras.4.

634.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਖਸਟਮੋ ਅਵਤਾਰ ਬ੍ਰਹਮਾ ਖਸਟ ਰਿਖ ਸਮਾਪਤੰ ॥੬॥
634.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the khasaTamo avataar brahamaa khasaT rikh samaapata(n) ||6||
634.e: End of the description about six sages, the sixth incarnation of Brahma in Bhachittar Natak.6.
Now begins the description of Kalidas Incarnation
TOMAR STANZA

635.e: This Brahma, the ocean of Vedas, who was the authentic knower of eighteen Puranas and Shastras, began to scan the whole world in his incarnation named Kalidas in the Iron Age.1.
The king Vikramaditya, who himself was glorious, unconquerable, scholar, full of virtues with auspicious brightness and charming eyes, remained pleased on seeing kalidas.2.
After his manifestation, Kalidas composed in chastened form his poem ‘Raghuvansh’
To what extent I should describe the number of poems that he composed?3.
He was the seventh incarnation of Brahma and when he was redeemed, then he assumed the form of fourheaded Brahma i.e. merged himself in Brahma.4.

635.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਸਪਤਮੋ ਅਵਤਾਰ ਬ੍ਰਹਮਾ ਕਾਲਿਦਾਸ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ॥੭॥
635.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the sapatamo avataar brahamaa kaalidhaas samaapatam ||7||
635.e: End of the description of Kalidas, the seventh incarnation of Brahma in a Bachittar Natak.7.
Rudra Avatar
The Lord is One and He can be realized through the Grace of the True Guru.
The Lord is One and He can be realized through the Grace of the True Guru.
Now begins the description of Rudra Incarnation
TOMAR STANZA
Now I describe in chastened form those incarnations, which were assumed by Rudra
Performing extreme austerities Rudra became egoistic.1.
He did not consider anyone equal to him in all place and countries, then Mahakal (the great death) in ire said to him thus
“Those who become proud, they deliberately perform the action of falling into a well
O Rudra! Listen to me attentively that my name is also the destroyer of ego.3.
“Brahma had also become egoistic in his mind and the evil notions arose there, but when he took birth for seven times, he was then redeemed.4.
“O the king of sages! listen to what I say and in the same way, you may go and take birth on the earth
Otherwise, O Rudra! You will not be redeemed in any other way.”5.
Hearing this, Shiva, considering the Lord as the destroyer of ego, and leaving his persistence, incarnated on earth.6.
PAADHARI STANZA

635.g: ਤਿਮ ਕਹੇ ਰਿਖਿਨ ਸਬ ਹੀ ਸਮਾਜ ॥
635.t: tim kahe rikhin sab hee samaaj ||

635.g: ਜਿਹ ਜਿਹ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਰ ਤਿਹ ਕਰਮ ਕੀਨ ॥
635.t: jeh jeh prakaar teh karam keen ||

635.g: ਜਿਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਜੇਮਿ ਦਿਜ ਬਰਨ ਲੀਨ ॥੭॥
635.t: jeh bhaat jem dhij baran leen ||7||
635.e: The way, in which all the kings have been described, in the same way, the actions done by all the sages have been narrated as to how Rudra manifested himself in the castes of dvijas (twice born).7.

635.g: ਤੇ ਤੇ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਭਾਖੋ ਸੁ ਬਾਸ ॥
635.t: te te charitr bhaakho su baas ||
635.e: Whatever deeds they brought to light, I relate them here

635.g: ਰਿਖਿ ਪੁਤ੍ਰ ਏਸ ਭਏ ਰੁਦ੍ਰ ਦੇਵ ॥
635.t: rikh putr es bhe rudhr dhev ||

635.e: In this way, rudra became the sons of the sages, who adopted silence and attained recognition.8.

635.g: ਪੁਨਿ ਭਏ ਅਤ੍ਰਿ ਰਿਖਿ ਮੁਨਿ ਮਹਾਨ ॥
635.t: pun bhe atr rikh mun mahaan ||

635.e: Then he incarnated himself as sage Atrl, who the store of eighteen sciences

635.g: ਲਿਨੇ ਸੁ ਜੋਗ ਤਜਿ ਰਾਜ ਆਨਿ ॥
635.t: line su jog taj raaj aan ||

635.e: He abandoned everything else and adopted Yoga as his way of life and served Rudra, the store of all wealth.9.

635.g: ਕਿਨੋ ਸੁ ਯੋਗ ਬਹੁ ਦਿਨ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਨ ॥
635.t: kino su yog bahu dhin pramaan ||

635.g: ਬਰੁ ਮਾਗ ਪੁਤ੍ਰ ਜੋ ਰੁਚੈ ਤੋਹਿ ॥
635.t: bar maag putr jo ruchai toh ||

635.g: ਬਰੁ ਦਾਨੁ ਤਉਨ ਮੈ ਦੇਉ ਤੋਹਿ ॥੧੦॥
635.t: bar dhaan taun mai dheau toh ||10||
635.e: He performed austerities for a long time, on which, Rudra got pleased and said, “You may ask for any boon which you like, I shall grant it to you.”10.

635.g: ਕਰਿ ਜੋਰਿ ਅਤ੍ਰਿ ਤਬ ਭਯੋ ਠਾਢ ॥
635.t: kar jor atr tab bhayo Thaadd ||

635.e: Then the sage Atri stood up with folded hands and his love for Rudra was further increased in his mind

635.g: ਗਦ ਗਦ ਸੁ ਬੈਣ ਭਭਕੰਤ ਨੈਣ ॥
635.t: gadh gadh su bain bhabhaka(n)t nain ||

635.e: He became very happy the tears flowed form his eyes and his hair showed signs of jubilation, when he said11

635.g: ਜੋ ਦੇਤ ਰੁਦ੍ਰ ਬਰੁ ਰੀਝ ਮੋਹਿ ॥
635.t: jo dhet rudhr bar reejh moh ||

635.g: ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਹੋਇ ਪੁਤ੍ਰ ਸਮ ਤੁਲਿ ਤੋਹਿ ॥
635.t: gireh hoi putr sam tul toh ||
635.e: “O Rudra! if you want to grant me a boon, then give me a son like you

635.g: ਕਹਿ ਕੈ ਤਥਾਸਤੁ ਭਏ ਅੰਤ੍ਰ ਧਿਆਨ ॥
635.t: keh kai tathaasat bhe a(n)tr dhiaan ||

635.g: ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਗਯੋ ਅਤ੍ਰਿ ਮੁਨਿ ਮਨਿ ਮਹਾਨ ॥੧੨॥
635.t: gireh gayo atr mun man mahaan ||12||
635.e: ” Rudra saying “let it be”, disappeared and the sage came back to his home.12.

635.g: ਜਨੁ ਪਠਿਓ ਤਤੁ ਨਿਜ ਸਿਵ ਨਿਕਾਰਿ ॥
635.t: jan paThio tat nij siv nikaar ||

636.g: ਬ੍ਰਹਮਾ ਰੁ ਬਿਸਨ ਨਿਜ ਤੇਜ ਕਾਢਿ ॥
636.t: brahamaa r bisan nij tej kaadd ||

636.e: On returning, he married Ansuya, who had been blessed by Shiva, Brahma and Vishnu by their Lustre.13.

636.g: ਭਈ ਕਰਤ ਜੋਗ ਬਹੁ ਦਿਨ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਨ ॥
636.t: bhiee karat jog bahu dhin pramaan ||

636.e: Ansuya also, in consonance with her name, inspection being a charming lady, performed austerities
She was extremely lustrous and glorious and it appeared that she was the second manifestation of the goddess of love (Rati).14.
That pretty and married fortunate woman was glorious in various ways on seeing whom, the personification of beauty also got allured her glory is indescribable.15.

636.g: ਜਲਿ ਜਾਇ ਨੈਨ ਲਹਿ ਰੋਸ ਮਾਨ ॥
636.t: jal jai nain leh ros maan ||
636.e: Seeing her face, the moon was filled with jealousy and wept in affection

636.g: ਤਮ ਨਿਰਖਿ ਕੇਸ ਕੀਅ ਨੀਚ ਡੀਠ ॥
636.t: tam nirakh kes keea neech ddeeTh ||

636.g: ਛਪਿ ਰਹਾ ਜਾਨੁ ਗਿਰ ਹੇਮ ਪੀਠ ॥੧੬॥
636.t: chhap rahaa jaan gir hem peeTh ||16||
636.e: Seeing her hair, he bowed down her looks and even the Sumeru mountain, seeing her beauty, concealed himself.16.
Seeing her neck, the female pigeon got enraged and the parrot seeing her nostril hid himself in the forest
Seeing her hair, even Yamuna was filled with anger and seeing her serenity, the ocean felt shy.17.
Seeing her arms, the lotus-stalk felt she and the swans, seeing her gait got angry

636.g: ਨਿਸ ਰਾਟ ਆਪ ਘਟਿ ਰੂਪ ਮਾਨ ॥੧੮॥
636.t: nis raaT aap ghaT roop maan ||18||
636.e: Seeing her legs, the Kadli trees became shyful and the moon considered his beauty inferior to her.18.
In this way, the charm of her beauty is described, and no poet can utter her greatness

636.g: ਜਨੁ ਲੀਨ ਰੂਪ ਕੋ ਛੀਨ ਛਤ੍ਰ ॥੧੯॥
636.t: jan leen roop ko chheen chhatr ||19||
636.e: Seeing such a beauteous lady, the sage Atri believed that he had obtained canopied kingdom of beauty.19.

636.g: ਮੈ ਬਰੌ ਤਾਸੁ ਰੁਚਿ ਮਾਨਿ ਚਿਤ ॥
636.t: mai barau taas ruch maan chit ||

636.e: That lady had vowed that she would not marry her husband for sexual enjoyment, and would wed that person, who would have the strength to endure the sacred tribulations of austrerities.20.

636.g: ਰਿਖਿ ਮਾਨਿ ਬੈਨ ਤਬ ਬਰ੍ਰਯੋ ਵਾਹਿ ॥
636.t: rikh maan bain tab barrayo vaeh ||

636.e: The sage (Arti) had agreed with her vow and married her and sacrificed himself on her charm of beauty

636.g: ਲੈ ਗਯੋ ਧਾਮਿ ਕਰਿ ਨਾਰਿ ਤਉਨ ॥
636.t: lai gayo dhaam kar naar taun ||

636.g: ਪਿਤ ਦਤ ਦੇਵ ਮੁਨਿ ਅਤ੍ਰਿ ਜਉਨ ॥੨੧॥
636.t: pit dhat dhev mun atr jaun ||21||
636.e: He, the sage Atri, who was the father of Dattatreya, making her his wife, brought her home.21.
TOMAR STANZA

636.g: ਕਿਨੀ ਸੁ ਸੇਵ ਤ੍ਰੀਯ ਬਹੁ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ॥੨੨॥
636.t: kinee su sev treey bahu prasaadh ||22||
636.e: Several years passed after marriage and once an opportunity arose when Brahma and other gods went to the home of that sage the women of the hermitage of the sage performed great service to them.22.

636.g: ਬਹੁ ਧੂਪ ਦੀਪ ਅਰੁ ਅਰਘ ਦਾਨ ॥
636.t: bahu dhoop dheep ar aragh dhaan ||

636.e: The incense was burnt, the lamps were lighted, there were libations and salutations
Seeing Indra, Vishnu and Shiva, all the devotees eulogized them.23.
Seeing the devotion of the sage, all were pleased and all blessed him
Then Brahma said, “O Kumar! You will be blessed with a son.”24.

637.e: When Brahma said this that the save would be blessed with a son, then listening to it, her eyes showed signs of anxiety.25.
The body of that young lady became agitated and the tears flowed form her eyes
She was filled with anxiety on hearing these words and she felt that the day had changed into night.26.
Her body was agitated with anxiety and she getting enraged, became impatient, lips and eyes quivered and she lamented.27.
Hearing these words that doe-eyed and extremely beautiful lady (felt agitated).28.
Her mind, which was immaculate, was filled with extreme rage alongwith other women of the sages.29.
The wife of the sage plucked her hair at that place and her comely limbs were filled with extreme ire.30.
Breaking her necklaces, she plucked her hair and began to put dust hr head.31.
Seeing the wife of the sage in anger, getting fearful and forsaking his pride, and taking Shiva and other sages with him, Brahma fled.32.
Then the wife of the sage, uprooting one of the matted lock of ther head in anger, strumck it on her hand, at that time Dattatreya was born.33.
Considering Ansuya as his mother and keeping her on his right, he circumambulated around her and then saluted her
In this way, thinking about the experience of sexual pleasure, Dutt Kumar was born.34.
His body was charming and he was reciting seven Smrities
The great Dutt was reciting all the four Vedas.35.

638.e: Shiva, remembering the earlier curse assumed himself the body of Dutt and
Took birth in the home of Ansuya this was his first incarnation.36.
PAADHARI STANZA
The loving Dutt, the store of eighteen sciences was born
He was the knower of Shastras and had a charming figure he was Yogi king of all the ganas.37.
He spread the cults of Sannyas and Yoga and he was totally spotless and servitor of all

638.g: ਜਨ ਧਰਿਓ ਆਨਿ ਬਪੁ ਸਰਬ ਜੋਗ ॥
638.t: jan dhario aan bap sarab jog ||

638.g: ਤਜਿ ਰਾਜ ਸਾਜ ਅਰੁ ਤਿਆਗ ਭੋਗ ॥੩੮॥
638.t: taj raaj saaj ar tiaag bhog ||38||
638.e: He was the apparent manifestation of Yoga, who abandoned the path of royal pleasure.38.
He was greatly praiseworthy, had a charming personality and also the store-house of Grace

638.g: ਰਵਿ ਅਨਿਲ ਤੇਜ ਜਲ ਸੋ ਸੁਭਾਵ ॥
638.t: rav anil tej jal so subhaav ||

638.e: His disposition was radiant like sun and fire and had cool temperament like water he manifested himself as the king of Yogis in the world.39.
Dutt Dev was superior to all in Sannyas Ashrama (monastic order) and was becoming incarnation of Rudra
His radiance was like fire and power of Rudra his radiance was like fire and power endurance like earth.40.
Dutt was a person of purity, indestructible splendour and pure intellect
Even the gold feel shy before him and the waves of the Ganges seemed to surge over his head.41.
He had long arms and charming body and was a detached supreme Yogi
When he applied the ashes to his limbs, he fragranced everyone around him and he brought to light Sannyas and Yoga in the world.42.
The praise of his limbs seemed boundless and he manifested himself as a generous king of the Yogis
The brilliance of his body was infinite and from his great personality, he appeared to be a silence-observing ascetic and eminently glorious.43.
That king of the Yogis spread his infinite greatness and glory and on his manifestation, the fraudulent tendencies trembled and he made them stingless in an instant.44.
Seeing his indestructible greatness and unique body, the mother remained wonder-struck

638.g: ਸੁਨਿ ਸਰਬ ਰਿਖਿਨ ਤਜਿ ਦੀਨ ਗਰਬ ॥੪੫॥
638.t: sun sarab rikhin taj dheen garab ||45||
638.e: All the people in counties far and near also marveled to see him and all of them abandoned their pride on listening to his greatness.45.

638.g: ਚਲ ਚਾਲ ਚਿਤੁ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੁ ਬਾਸ ॥
638.t: chal chaal chit su(n)dhar su baas ||
638.e: The whole nether-world and sky had the feeling about his comeliness which made all the creatures full of joy
Because of him, the whole earth became blissful.46.

638.g: ਜਹ ਤਹ ਰਿਖੀਨ ਤਜਿ ਦੀਨ ਗਰਬ ॥
638.t: jeh teh rikheen taj dheen garab ||
638.e: The sky and the earth all quivered and the sages here and there abandoned their pride

638.g: ਦਸ ਦਿਉਸ ਪਾਇ ਦਿਖੀ ਨ ਰੈਣ ॥੪੭॥
638.t: dhas dhiaus pai dhikhee na rain ||47||
638.e: On his manifestation, many instruments (musical) were played in the sky and for ten days, the presence o f night was not felt.47.

639.e: Many musical instruments were played here and there and it appeared that the discriminating intellect had assumed a body itself
His glory is indescribable and he manifested himself as the king of ‘Sannyas’.48.
Even on taking birth, he absorbed himself in actions of Yogs
And he, destroying sins, propagated Dharma the great Sovereign fell at his feet and getting up, they practiced Sannyas and Yoga.49.

639.g: ਉਠਿ ਲਗੇ ਪਾਇ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਸਰਬ ਆਇ ॥
639.t: auTh lage pai nirap sarab aai ||
639.e: Seeing the unique king Dutt, all the king bowed respectfully at his feet
Seeing the greatness of Dutt, it appeared that he was the store of eighteen sciences.50.

639.g: ਨਖ ਨੇਮ ਕੇ ਸੁ ਬਢਏ ਮਹਾਨ ॥
639.t: nakh nem ke su badde mahaan ||
639.e: On his head, there were the matted locks of his celibacy and on his hands grew the nails of observances

639.g: ਦਿਜ ਚਰਜ ਤੁਲਿ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਚਰਮ ਅਰੋਹ ॥੫੧॥
639.t: dhij charaj tul mirag charam aroh ||51||
639.e: The white ashes on his body were indicative of his state devoid of illusions his character like Brahm (Brahman) was his deer skin.51.
Having white ashes on his face and wearing loin-cloth, he was the possessor of Sannyas and conduct and relinquisher of deceit
He remained absorbed in abstract meditation and his limbs were extremely charming his radiance was indestructible.52.

639.g: ਇਕ ਆਸ ਚਿਤ ਤਜਿ ਸਰਬ ਆਸ ॥
639.t: eik aas chit taj sarab aas ||

639.e: In his mind there was only one desire of Sannyas and Yoga and for this desire he had abandoned all other desires

639.g: ਮੁਨਿ ਚਰਜ ਲੀਨ ਤਜਿ ਸਰਬ ਕਾਮ ॥
639.t: mun charaj leen taj sarab kaam ||

639.e: His body was unique and during day and night, he remained detached from the deceits of the world leaving the desires of all kinds, he had adopted the character of sages his eyes were red and were the store of Dharma.53.
He had a pure mind, devoid of vices, and he meditated with his non-mercurial eyes
His praise was infinite having only one desire in his mind of adopting Sannyas from all sides he was the greatest among the immaculate Sannyasis.54.
He had a body of Yogis, whose greatness was infinite and he was the store of the knowledge of Shrutis (Vedas) and extremely generous

639.g: ਮੁਨਿ ਮਨਿ ਪ੍ਰਬੀਨ ਗੁਨਿ ਗਨ ਮਹਾਨ ॥
639.t: mun man prabeen gun gan mahaan ||

639.e: Amongst the sages, he was most skilful and great and was supremely learned.55.

639.g: ਕਬਹੂੰ ਨ ਪਾਪ ਜਿਹ ਛੁਹਾ ਅੰਗ ॥
639.t: kabahoo(n) na paap jeh chhuhaa a(n)g ||

639.e: The sin had not even touched him and he was elegant in virtues
The Yogi Dutt wore loin-cloth and seeing him, mother was wonder-struck.56.
Seeing the greatest Sannyasi Dutt, having comely limbs, even the god of love felt shy
The sage Dutt was the king of Sannyasis and he had practiced all kinds of the activities of Sannyas.57.
His body was immaculate, which had never been troubled by lust
On his head there was a tuft of matted locks such a form was adopted by Dutt, the incarnation of Rudra.58.
Who can describe his fine glory ? And listening to his appreciation, the Yakshas and Gandharvas become silent
Brahma was also wonder-struck to see his glory and even the god of love felt shy on seeing his beauty.59.

640.g: ਅਨ ਆਸ ਗਾਤ ਹਰਿ ਕੋ ਅਧੀਨ ॥
640.t: an aas gaat har ko adheen ||
640.e: He was extremely learned, expert in actions, beyond the desires and obedient to the Lord
His elegance was like the crores of suns and the moon was also wonder-struck on seeing him.60.
He had manifested as the apparent form of yoga and then had been absorbed in the practice of Yoga

640.g: ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਪ੍ਰਿਥਮ ਛਾਡਿ ਉਠਿ ਚਲਾ ਦਤ ॥
640.t: gireh piratham chhaadd uTh chalaa dhat ||

640.e: That immaculate Dutt of pure intellect did the first thing of leaving his home.61.

640.g: ਜਬ ਕੀਨ ਜੋਗ ਬਹੁ ਦਿਨ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਨ ॥
640.t: jab keen jog bahu dhin pramaan ||

640.e: When he practiced Yoga for a long time, Kaldev (the Lord) was pleased with him
At that time, there was a heavenly voice “O king of Yogis! Listen to what I say.”62.
Voice from heaven addressed to Dutt :
PAADHARI STANZA

640.g: ਗੁਰ ਹੀਣ ਮੁਕਤਿ ਨਹੀ ਹੋਤ ਦਤ ॥
640.t: gur heen mukat nahee hot dhat ||

640.g: ਤੁਹਿ ਕਹੋ ਬਾਤ ਸੁਨਿ ਬਿਮਲ ਮਤ ॥
640.t: tuh kaho baat sun bimal mat ||
640.e: “O Dutt! Listen to me with pure intellect

640.g: ਗੁਰ ਕਰਹਿ ਪ੍ਰਿਥਮ ਤਬ ਹੋਗਿ ਮੁਕਤਿ ॥
640.t: gur kareh piratham tab hog mukat ||

640.g: ਕਹਿ ਦੀਨ ਕਾਲ ਤਿਹ ਜੋਗ ਜੁਗਤ ॥੬੩॥
640.t: keh dheen kaal teh jog jugat ||63||
640.e: I say unto you that there can be no salvation without the Guru first of all, adopt a Guru, then you will be redeemed, in this way, KAL told the method of Yoga to Dutt.63.
Obedient to the Lord and abiding beyond the desires, Dutt prostrated before the Lord in various ways
He practiced Yoga in different ways and spread the exaltation of Yoga.64.
Then Dutt, bowing before the Lord, eulogized the Unmanifested Brahman who is the Sovereign of Sovereigns,
The supreme Yogi and with unique limbs pervades everywhere.65

640.g: ਜਲ ਥਲ ਬਿਯਾਪ ਜਿਹ ਤੇਜ ਏਕ ॥
640.t: jal thal biyaap jeh tej ek ||

640.e: The splendour of that Lord Pervades in after an on plain and many sages sing His Praises
He, whom the Vedas etc. call “Neti, neti” (not this, not this), that Lord is eternal and Pervades in beginning, in the middle and at the end.66.
He who created many beings from one and with His Power of wisdom, created the earth and the sky

640.g: ਜਲ ਬਾ ਥਲੇਸ ਸਬ ਠੌਰ ਜਾਨ ॥
640.t: jal baa thales sab Thauar jaan ||

640.e: That fearless, birthless and beyond desires is there at all the places in water and on plain.67.
He is supremely immaculate, sacred, pure, long-armed, fearless and unconquerable
He is the supremely eminent Purusha, the Sovereign of Sovereign and the great enjoyer.68.
That Lord has indestructible Lustre, Light-incarnation, Dagger-wielder and is eminent glorious

640.g: ਫਿਰ ਫਿਰੇ ਸਰਬ ਮਤਿ ਕੋ ਚਲਾਇ ॥੬੯॥
640.t: fir fire sarab mat ko chalai ||69||
640.e: His infinite glory is indescribable He Pervades in all the religions.69.
Whom all call “Neti, neti” (not this, not this), the powers of all kinds abide at the feet of that Blemishless and Beauty-incarnate Lord

640.g: ਜਿਹ ਨਾਮ ਲੇਤ ਸਬ ਪਾਪ ਭਾਗ ॥੭੦॥
640.t: jeh naam let sab paap bhaag ||70||
640.e: And all the sins fly away with the remembrance of His Name.70.

640.g: ਗੁਨ ਸੀਲ ਸਾਧੁ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਸੁਭਾਇ ॥
640.t: gun seel saadh taa ke subhai ||

640.g: ਬਿਨੁ ਤਾਸ ਸਰਨਿ ਨਹੀ ਕੋਊ ਉਪਾਇ ॥
640.t: bin taas saran nahee kouoo upai ||
640.e: He has the temperament, qualities and gentleness like the saints and there is no other measure of achieving salvation without going under His shelter

641.e: He acts for the redemption of the lowly and if anyone calls Him with any motive, He accepts his saying.7
The enemies and friends all are allured to see Him, Who is blemishless, Who is eternally glorious, Who is seated on a stable seat and Who has infinite qualities.72.

641.g: ਲਖਿ ਸਤ੍ਰ ਮਿਤ੍ਰ ਜਿਹ ਰਹਤ ਲੋਭ ॥੭੨॥
641.t: lakh satr mitr jeh rahat lobh ||72||

641.g: ਜਿਹ ਸਤ੍ਰ ਮਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮ ਏਕ ਜਾਨ ॥
641.t: jeh satr mitr sam ek jaan ||

641.e: He considers enemies and friends alike, and also comprehends the praise and slander alike
He is seated on a stable seat He is supremely Beauty-incranate and also immaculate He is the Sovereign of sovereigns.73.
His tongue showers ambrosia
All the gods and demons are fascinated by Himp He is devoid of enmity and Light-incarnate His body is indestructible and is impartial all the time.74.
His Glory remains the same in the beginning and at the end and is accomplished with all kinds of powers

641.g: ਸੋਭਾ ਸੁ ਬਹੁਤ ਤਨ ਜਾਸੁ ਸੋਭ ॥
641.t: sobhaa su bahut tan jaas sobh ||

641.e: All the beauties are there in his body and seing his comeliness the Yakshas and Gandharvas are allured.75.
His limbs are indestructible

641.g: ਕਿਨੇ ਸੁ ਜੀਵ ਜਲਿ ਥਲਿ ਅਨੇਕ ॥
641.t: kine su jeev jal thal anek ||

641.e: That Lord is the manifestation of cognition because of His Grave, the beings are scattered over the whole world He had created many beings in water and on plain and He ultimately merges everyone in His Form.76.

641.g: ਜਿਹ ਛੂਆ ਨੈਕੁ ਨਹੀ ਕਾਲ ਜਾਲੁ ॥
641.t: jeh chhooaa naik nahee kaal jaal ||

641.g: ਛ੍ਵੈ ਸਕਾ ਪਾਪ ਨਹੀ ਕਉਨ ਕਾਲ ॥
641.t: chhavai sakaa paap nahee kaun kaal ||
641.e: The death and sin have not been able to touch Him at any time
The Lord of that indestructible Lustre and body remains the same at all times.77.

641.g: ਮੁਖ ਪੜਤ ਅਛ੍ਰ ਗਯੋ ਪਾਪ ਨਾਠ ॥
641.t: mukh paRat achhr gayo paap naaTh ||
641.e: In this way, Dutt recited the eulogy and by this recitation, all the sins fled away
Who can describe his infinite greatness?, therefore I have said it in brief.78.

641.g: ਲਿਖੇ ਗਣੇਸ ਕਰਿ ਕੈ ਸੁ ਗਰਬ ॥
641.t: likhe ganes kar kai su garab ||
641.e: If the whole earth becomes the paper and Ganesha is the proud writer

641.g: ਨਹੀ ਤਦਿਪ ਅੰਤਿ ਕਹਿ ਸਕੈ ਸੇਸੁ ॥੭੯॥
641.t: nahee tadhip a(n)t keh sakai ses ||79||
641.e: All the oceans become the ink and all the forests become the pens and Sheshnaga makes a description of the Lord from his thousand mouths, then also he mystery of the Lord cannot be comprehended.79.
If Brahma also utters His Glory, then also His effulgence cannot be comprehended

641.g: ਮੁਖ ਸਹੰਸ ਨਾਮ ਫਣ ਪਤਿ ਰੜੰਤ ॥
641.t: mukh saha(n)s naam fan pat raRa(n)t ||

641.e: If Sheshnaga also utters His Names from his thousand mouths, then also His end cannot be known.80.
If Sanak, Sunandan etc. remember Him continuously night and day, then also Hi Glory cannot be described
Brahma crated all the four Vedas, but on reflecting about Him, he also talks of Him as “Neti, Neti” (no this, not this.)81.

641.g: ਸਿਵ ਸਹੰਸ੍ਰ ਬਰਖ ਲੌ ਜੋਗ ਕੀਨ ॥
641.t: siv saha(n)sr barakh lau jog keen ||

641.g: ਤਜਿ ਨੇਹ ਗੇਹ ਬਨ ਬਾਸ ਲੀਨ ॥
641.t: taj neh geh ban baas leen ||
641.e: Shiva practiced Yoga for thousands of years

641.g: ਬਹੁ ਕੀਨ ਜੋਗ ਤਹ ਬਹੁ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਰ ॥
641.t: bahu keen jog teh bahu prakaar ||

641.g: ਨਹੀ ਤਦਿਪ ਤਾਸੁ ਲਹਿ ਸਕਾ ਪਾਰ ॥੮੨॥
641.t: nahee tadhip taas leh sakaa paar ||82||
641.e: He left his home and all attachment and resided in the forest he also practiced Yoga in various ways, but still he could not know His end.82.
Many worlds are manifested from His one form and the Lustre of that Lord, who remains unattached throughout night and day, cannot be described

642.e: His seat is permanent and He is praiseworthy, Lustrous and Glorrious.83.
The enemies and friends are alike for Him and His invisible Lustre and Praise are Supreme
He has the same form in the beginning and at the end and He is the Creator of this fascinating world.84.

642.g: ਜਿਹ ਰਾਗ ਰੰਗ ਨਹੀ ਰੂਪ ਰੇਖ ॥
642.t: jeh raag ra(n)g nahee roop rekh ||

642.e: He has no form or line, no attachment or detachment
That Guiseless Lord had no special Name or Place that Long-armed and omnipotent Lord is the manifestation of cognition and His Comeliness and Greatness are infinite.85.

642.g: ਕਈ ਕਲਪ ਜੋਗ ਜਿਨਿ ਕਰਤ ਬੀਤ ॥
642.t: kiee kalap jog jin karat beet ||

642.g: ਨਹੀ ਤਦਿਪ ਤਉਨ ਧਰਿ ਗਏ ਚੀਤ ॥
642.t: nahee tadhip taun dhar ge cheet ||
642.e: Even those who practiced Yoga for various Kalpas (ages) ccouldnot please His mind

642.g: ਮੁਨਿ ਮਨ ਅਨੇਕ ਗੁਨਿ ਗਨ ਮਹਾਨ ॥
642.t: mun man anek gun gan mahaan ||

642.g: ਬਹੁ ਕਸਟ ਕਰਤ ਨਹੀ ਧਰਤ ਧਿਆਨ ॥੮੬॥
642.t: bahu kasaT karat nahee dharat dhiaan ||86||
642.e: Many sags and virtuous people remember Him by the performance of many agonizing austerities, but that Lord does not even think of them.86.
He is the only One, and creates many and ultimately merges the many created forms in His oneness
He is the life-force of millions of beings and ultimately He merges all within Him.87.

642.g: ਜਿਹ ਜਗਤ ਜੀਵ ਸਬ ਪਰੇ ਸਰਨਿ ॥
642.t: jeh jagat jeev sab pare saran ||

642.g: ਮੁਨ ਮਨਿ ਅਨੇਕ ਜਿਹ ਜਪਤ ਚਰਨ ॥
642.t: mun man anek jeh japat charan ||
642.e: All the beings of the world are under His shelter and many sages meditate on His feet
That all-pervading Lord does not even scan those who mediate on Him fore many kalpas (ages).88.

642.g: ਮੁਨ ਮਨਿ ਮਹਾਨ ਅਤ ਹੀ ਉਦਾਰ ॥
642.t: mun man mahaan at hee udhaar ||
642.e: His Greatness and Glory are infinite

642.g: ਨਹੀ ਸਕਤ ਬੁਧ ਕਰਿ ਕੈ ਬਿਚਾਰ ॥੮੯॥
642.t: nahee sakat budh kar kai bichaar ||89||
642.e: He is the Greatest amongst the sages and is extremely Generous His effulgence is eternal and form Most Beautiful the human intellect cannot reflect on Him.89.
He, the Lord of Unique Greatness and Glory, remains the same in the beginning and at the end
He, who has instilled His Light in all the beings, He has also smashed the pride of the egoists.90.

642.g: ਫਿਰਿ ਕਹੋ ਬੈਣ ਨਹੀ ਬੈਣ ਭਾਖ ॥
642.t: fir kaho bain nahee bain bhaakh ||
642.e: He, who has not left untouched even one egoist, He cannot be described in words

642.g: ਇਕ ਬਾਰ ਮਾਰਿ ਮਾਰ੍ਯੋ ਨ ਸਤ੍ਰੁ ॥
642.t: eik baar maar maarayo na satr ||

642.g: ਇਕ ਬਾਰ ਡਾਰਿ ਡਾਰਿਓ ਨ ਅਤ੍ਰ ॥੯੧॥
642.t: eik baar ddaar ddaario na atr ||91||
642.e: He kills the enemy with a single blow.91.

642.g: ਲਖਿ ਭਈ ਭੂਲ ਮੁਖਿ ਬਿਹਸ ਦੀਨ ॥
642.t: lakh bhiee bhool mukh bihas dheen ||
642.e: He never keep His devotees away from Him and just smiles even on his erratic doings

642.g: ਤ੍ਰੀਯਾ ਏਕ ਬ੍ਯਾਹਿ ਨਹੀ ਕੀਨ ਬ੍ਯਾਹ ॥੯੨॥
642.t: treeyaa ek bayaeh nahee keen bayaeh ||92||
642.e: He, who comes under His Grace, his objectives are fulfilled by Him ultimately through He has not married, even then maya is His spouse.92.
Millions are getting pleased with Him and some are getting pleased only by remembering His name
He is devoid of deceit and is the manifestation o of cognition He is Omnipotent and ever remains without desires.93.
He is Immaculate, Perfect, Store of Eternal Glory, Indestructible, Praiseworthy, Holy Illustrious, Omnipotent, Fearless and Unconquerable.94.
Millions of Indras, Chandras, Suryas and Krishans serve Him

642.g: ਬਿਨੁ ਭਗਤਿ ਯੌ ਨ ਕੋਈ ਕਬੂਲ ॥੯੫॥
642.t: bin bhagat yau na koiee kabool ||95||
642.e: Many Vishnus, Rudras, Rams, Muhammadas etc. mediate on Him, but He accepts none without true devotion.95.
There are many truthful persons like Dutt, many Yogis like Gorakh, Machhindar and other sages, but none has been able to comprehend His mystery

642.g: ਬਹੁ ਭਾਤਿ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਮਤ ਕੈ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ ॥
642.t: bahu bhaat ma(n)tr mat kai prakaas ||

642.g: ਬਿਨੁ ਏਕ ਆਸ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਨਿਰਾਸ ॥੯੬॥
642.t: bin ek aas sabh hee niraas ||96||
642.e: Various types of Mantras in various religions the faith of One Lord.96.
Vedas speak of Him as “Neti, Neti” (not this, not this) and that creator is the cause of all cause and unapproachable

642.g: ਜਿਹ ਲਖਤ ਕੋਈ ਨਹੀ ਕਉਨ ਜਾਤਿ ॥
642.t: jeh lakhat koiee nahee kaun jaat ||

642.g: ਜਿਹ ਨਾਹਿ ਪਿਤਾ ਭ੍ਰਿਤ ਤਾਤ ਮਾਤ ॥੯੭॥
642.t: jeh naeh pitaa bhirat taat maat ||97||
642.e: He is casteless and without father, mother and servents.97.

642.g: ਜਾਨੀ ਨ ਜਾਤ ਜਿਹ ਰੰਗ ਰੂਪ ॥
642.t: jaanee na jaat jeh ra(n)g roop ||
642.e: His form and colour cannot be known
He is the king of kings and Sovereign of sovereigns

642.g: ਜਿਹ ਬਰਣ ਜਾਤਿ ਨਹੀ ਕ੍ਰਿਤ ਅਨੰਤ ॥
642.t: jeh baran jaat nahee kirat ana(n)t ||
642.e: He is the king of kings and Sovereign of sovereigns
He is the Primal cause of the world and is Infinite.98.

642.g: ਬਰਣੀ ਨ ਜਾਤਿ ਜਿਹ ਰੰਗ ਰੇਖ ॥
642.t: baranee na jaat jeh ra(n)g rekh ||

642.e: His colour and Line are indescribable and the power of that Guiseless Lord is endless
He is Vice-less, indivisible, God of gods and unique.99.
The praise and slander are alike for Him and the beauty of that Great Praiseworthy Lord is perfect

642.g: ਘਟਿ ਘਟਿ ਬਿਯਾਪ ਨਿਸ ਦਿਨ ਉਦਾਸ ॥੧੦੦॥
642.t: ghaT ghaT biyaap nis dhin udhaas ||100||
642.e: That Lord, the manifestation of cognition, is vice-less, All-pervading and continuously unattached.100.
In this way, Dutt, the son of Atri eulogised the Lord and prostrated in devotion

643.g: ਅਰੁ ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਉਠਿ ਪਰਤ ਚਰਨਿ ॥
643.t: ar bhaat bhaat uTh parat charan ||

643.g: ਜਾਨੀ ਨ ਜਾਇ ਜਿਹ ਜਾਤਿ ਬਰਨ ॥੧੦੧॥
643.t: jaanee na jai jeh jaat baran ||101||
643.e: Then he touched the feet of that castless and colorless lord in in various ways.101.

643.g: ਜਉ ਕਰੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਤ ਕਈ ਜੁਗ ਉਚਾਰ ॥
643.t: jau karai kirat kiee jug uchaar ||

643.g: ਨਹੀ ਤਦਿਪ ਤਾਸੁ ਲਹਿ ਜਾਤ ਪਾਰ ॥
643.t: nahee tadhip taas leh jaat paar ||
643.e: If one utter His praises for several ages, even then he cannot understand His mystery

643.g: ਮਮ ਅਲਪ ਬੁਧਿ ਤਵ ਗੁਨ ਅਨੰਤ ॥
643.t: mam alap budh tav gun ana(n)t ||

643.g: ਬਰਨਾ ਨ ਜਾਤ ਤੁਮ ਅਤਿ ਬਿਅੰਤ ॥੧੦੨॥
643.t: baranaa na jaat tum at bia(n)t ||102||
643.e: "O Lord! My intellect is very low and I cannot describe Thy Vastness.102.

643.g: ਤਵ ਗੁਣ ਅਤਿ ਊਚ ਅੰਬਰ ਸਮਾਨ ॥
643.t: tav gun at uooch a(n)bar samaan ||

643.g: ਮਮ ਅਲਪ ਬੁਧਿ ਬਾਲਕ ਅਜਾਨ ॥
643.t: mam alap budh baalak ajaan ||
643.e: “Thy attributes are Great like the sky and my wisdom is very low like that of a child

643.g: ਕਿਮ ਸਕੌ ਬਰਨ ਤੁਮਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭਾਵ ॥
643.t: kim sakau baran tumare prabhaav ||

643.g: ਤਵ ਪਰਾ ਸਰਣਿ ਤਜਿ ਸਭ ਉਪਾਵ ॥੧੦੩॥
643.t: tav paraa saran taj sabh upaav ||103||
643.e: How can I describe the Glory? Therefore leaving all the measures, I have come under Thy Refuge.”103.

643.g: ਜਿਹ ਲਖਤ ਚਤ੍ਰ ਨਹਿ ਭੇਦ ਬੇਦ ॥
643.t: jeh lakhat chatr neh bhedh bedh ||

643.g: ਆਭਾ ਅਨੰਤ ਮਹਿਮਾ ਅਛੇਦ ॥
643.t: aabhaa ana(n)t mahimaa achhedh ||
643.e: His mystery cannot be known to all the four Vedas His Glory is infinite and supreme

643.g: ਗੁਨ ਗਨਤ ਚਤ੍ਰਮੁਖ ਪਰਾ ਹਾਰ ॥
643.t: gun ganat chatramukh paraa haar ||

643.g: ਤਬ ਨੇਤਿ ਨੇਤਿ ਕਿਨੋ ਉਚਾਰ ॥੧੦੪॥
643.t: tab net net kino uchaar ||104||
643.e: Brahma also got tired in praising Him and is uttering Him Greatness only by the words “Neti, Neti” (not this, not this).104.

643.g: ਥਕਿ ਗਿਰਿਓ ਬ੍ਰਿਧ ਸਿਰ ਲਿਖਤ ਕਿਤ ॥
643.t: thak girio biradh sir likhat kit ||

643.g: ਚਕਿ ਰਹੇ ਬਾਲਿਖਿਲਾਦਿ ਚਿਤ ॥
643.t: chak rahe baalikhilaadh chit ||
643.e: Ganesha also gets tired in writing His Praises and all of them, feeling His Omnipresence, get wonder-struck

643.g: ਗੁਨ ਗਨਤ ਚਤ੍ਰਮੁਖ ਹਾਰ ਮਾਨਿ ॥
643.t: gun ganat chatramukh haar maan ||

643.g: ਹਠਿ ਤਜਿ ਬਿਅੰਤਿ ਕਿਨੋ ਬਖਾਨ ॥੧੦੫॥
643.t: haTh taj bia(n)t kino bakhaan ||105||
643.e: Brahma also accepted defet, while singing His Praises and forsaking his persistence by describing Him only as infinite.105.

643.g: ਤਹ ਜਪਤ ਰੁਦ੍ਰ ਜੁਗ ਕੋਟਿ ਭੀਤ ॥
643.t: teh japat rudhr jug koT bheet ||

643.g: ਬਹਿ ਗਈ ਗੰਗ ਸਿਰ ਮੁਰਿ ਨ ਚੀਤ ॥
643.t: beh giee ga(n)g sir mur na cheet ||
643.e: Rudra is remembering Him for millions of ages the Ganges is flowing from the head of that Rudra

643.g: ਕਈ ਕਲਪ ਬੀਤ ਜਿਹ ਧਰਤਿ ਧਿਆਨ ॥
643.t: kiee kalap beet jeh dharat dhiaan ||

643.g: ਨਹੀ ਤਦਿਪ ਧਿਆਨ ਆਏ ਸੁਜਾਨ ॥੧੦੬॥
643.t: nahee tadhip dhiaan aae sujaan ||106||
643.e: He is not bound down within the meditation of sagacious individuals, even on meditating Him for many Kalpas (ages).106.

643.g: ਜਬ ਕੀਨ ਨਾਲਿ ਬ੍ਰਹਮਾ ਪ੍ਰਵੇਸ ॥
643.t: jab keen naal brahamaa praves ||

643.g: ਮੁਨ ਮਨਿ ਮਹਾਨ ਦਿਜਬਰ ਦਿਜੇਸ ॥
643.t: mun man mahaan dhijabar dhijes ||

643.g: ਨਹੀ ਕਮਲ ਨਾਲ ਕੋ ਲਖਾ ਪਾਰ ॥
643.t: nahee kamal naal ko lakhaa paar ||

643.g: ਕਹੋ ਤਾਸੁ ਕੈਸ ਪਾਵੈ ਬਿਚਾਰ ॥੧੦੭॥
643.t: kaho taas kais paavai bichaar ||107||
643.e: When Brahma, who is superb amongst the great sages, entered the lotus-stalk, he could not even know the end of that lotus-stalk, then how can our power of reflection and wisdom realise Him?107.

643.g: ਬਰਨੀ ਨ ਜਾਤਿ ਜਿਹ ਛਬਿ ਸੁਰੰਗ ॥
643.t: baranee na jaat jeh chhab sura(n)g ||

643.g: ਆਭਾ ਆਪਾਰ ਮਹਿਮਾ ਅਭੰਗ ॥
643.t: aabhaa aapaar mahimaa abha(n)g ||
643.e: He, whose elegant comeliness cannot be described, His Greatness and Glory is infinite

643.g: ਜਿਹ ਏਕ ਰੂਪ ਕਿਨੋ ਅਨੇਕ ॥
643.t: jeh ek roop kino anek ||

643.g: ਪਗ ਛੋਰਿ ਆਨ ਤਿਹ ਧਰੋ ਟੇਕ ॥੧੦੮॥
643.t: pag chhor aan teh dharo Tek ||108||
643.e: He, was has manifested Himself in more than one forms meditate only on His Feet.108.

643.g: ਰੂਆਲ ਛੰਦ ॥
643.t: rooaal chha(n)dh ||
643.e: ROOAAL STANZA

643.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਬਿਅੰਤਿ ਦੇਸ ਭਵੰਤ ਕਿਰਤ ਉਚਾਰ ॥
643.t: bhaat bhaat bia(n)t dhes bhava(n)t kirat uchaar ||

643.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਪਗੋ ਲਗਾ ਤਜਿ ਗਰਬ ਅਤ੍ਰਿ ਕੁਮਾਰ ॥
643.t: bhaat bhaat pago lagaa taj garab atr kumaar ||
643.e: Touching the feet of various sages and forsaking his pride, Dutt, the son of Atri, began to wander in various countries

643.g: ਕੋਟਿ ਬਰਖ ਕਰੀ ਜਬੈ ਹਰਿ ਸੇਵਿ ਵਾ ਚਿਤੁ ਲਾਇ ॥
643.t: koT barakh karee jabai har sev vaa chit lai ||

643.g: ਅਕਸਮਾਤ ਭਈ ਤਬੈ ਤਿਹ ਬਿਓਮ ਬਾਨ ਬਨਾਇ ॥੧੦੯॥
643.t: akasamaat bhiee tabai teh biom baan banai ||109||
643.e: When, for lakhs of years, he served the Lord single-mindedly, then suddenly, a voice came from heaven.109.

643.g: ਬ੍ਯੋਮ ਬਾਨੀ ਬਾਚ ਦਤ ਪ੍ਰਤਿ ॥
643.t: bayom baanee baach dhat prat ||
643.e: (Now begins the description of adopting the Immortal Lord as the First Guru) Speech of heavenly voice addressed to Dutt :

643.g: ਦਤ ਸਤਿ ਕਹੋ ਤੁਝੈ ਗੁਰ ਹੀਣ ਮੁਕਤਿ ਨ ਹੋਇ ॥
643.t: dhat sat kaho tujhai gur heen mukat na hoi ||

643.g: ਰਾਵ ਰੰਕ ਪ੍ਰਜਾ ਵਜਾ ਇਮ ਭਾਖਈ ਸਭ ਕੋਇ ॥
643.t: raav ra(n)k prajaa vajaa im bhaakhiee sabh koi ||
643.e: “O Dutt! I am telling you the truth that none out of the people, the king, the poor and others, gets salvation without the Guru

643.g: ਕੋਟਿ ਕਸਟ ਨ ਕਿਉ ਕਰੋ ਨਹੀ ਐਸ ਦੇਹਿ ਉਧਾਰ ॥
643.t: koT kasaT na kiau karo nahee aais dheh udhaar ||

643.g: ਜਾਇ ਕੈ ਗੁਰ ਕੀਜੀਐ ਸੁਨਿ ਸਤਿ ਅਤ੍ਰਿ ਕੁਮਾਰ ॥੧੧੦॥
643.t: jai kai gur keejeeaai sun sat atr kumaar ||110||
643.e: “You may suffer millions of tribulations, but this body will not be redeemed, therefore, O the son of Atri, you may adopt a Guru.”110.

643.g: ਦਤ ਬਾਚ ॥
643.t: dhat baach ||
643.e: Speech of Dutt :

643.g: ਰੂਆਲ ਛੰਦ ॥
643.t: rooaal chha(n)dh ||
643.e: ROOAAL STANZA

643.g: ਐਸ ਬਾਕ ਭਏ ਜਬੈ ਤਬ ਦਤ ਸਤ ਸਰੂਪ ॥
643.t: aais baak bhe jabai tab dhat sat saroop ||

643.g: ਸਿੰਧੁ ਸੀਲ ਸੁਬ੍ਰਿਤ ਕੋ ਨਦ ਗ੍ਯਾਨ ਕੋ ਜਨੁ ਕੂਪ ॥
