643.t: si(n)dh seel subirat ko nadh gayaan ko jan koop ||
643.e: When this voice of heaven was heard, then Dutt, store of good qualities and knowledge and ocean of gentleness prostrating on the feet of the Lord, said,

643.g: ਪਾਨ ਲਾਗ ਡੰਡੌਤਿ ਕੈ ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਕੀਨ ਉਚਾਰ ॥
643.t: paan laag dda(n)ddauat kai ieh bhaat keen uchaar ||

643.g: ਕਉਨ ਸੋ ਗੁਰ ਕੀਜੀਐ ਕਹਿ ਮੋਹਿ ਤਤ ਬਿਚਾਰ ॥੧੧੧॥
643.t: kaun so gur keejeeaai keh moh tat bichaar ||111||
643.e: “O Lord! kindly give me the crux of the matter as to whom I should adopt my Guru?”111.

643.g: ਬ੍ਯੋਮ ਬਾਨੀ ਬਾਚ ॥
643.t: bayom baanee baach ||
643.e: Speech of the heavenly voice :

643.g: ਜਉਨ ਚਿਤ ਬਿਖੈ ਰੁਚੈ ਸੋਈ ਕੀਜੀਐ ਗੁਰਦੇਵ ॥
643.t: jaun chit bikhai ruchai soiee keejeeaai gurdhev ||

644.g: ਤਿਆਗ ਕਰਿ ਕੈ ਕਪਟ ਕਉ ਚਿਤ ਲਾਇ ਕੀਜੈ ਸੇਵ ॥
644.t: tiaag kar kai kapaT kau chit lai keejai sev ||
644.e: “Whomsoever you like in your mind, accept him as your Guru and forsaking deceit, serve him with the singleness of mind

644.g: ਰੀਝ ਹੈ ਗੁਰਦੇਵ ਤਉ ਤੁਮ ਪਾਇ ਹੋ ਬਰੁ ਦਾਨ ॥
644.t: reejh hai gurdhev tau tum pai ho bar dhaan ||

644.g: ਯੌ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਉਧਾਰ ਪੈ ਸੁਨਿ ਲੇਹੁ ਦਤ ਸੁਜਾਨ ॥੧੧੨॥
644.t: yau na hoi udhaar pai sun leh dhat sujaan ||112||
644.e: When the Guru is pleased, he will grant you a boon, otherwise O wise an sagacious Dutt! you will not be able to achieve redemption.”112.

644.g: ਪ੍ਰਿਥਮ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਦਯੋ ਜਿਨੈ ਸੋਈ ਜਾਨਿ ਕੈ ਗੁਰਦੇਵ ॥
644.t: piratham ma(n)tr dhayo jinai soiee jaan kai gurdhev ||

644.g: ਜੋਗ ਕਾਰਣ ਕੋ ਚਲਾ ਜੀਅ ਜਾਨਿ ਕੈ ਅਨਭੇਵ ॥
644.t: jog kaaran ko chalaa jeea jaan kai anabhev ||
644.e: He, who in the first place gave this mantra, feeling about that Lord in his mind and accepting Him as the Guru, Dutt proceeded for getting instructions in Yoga

644.g: ਤਾਤ ਮਾਤ ਰਹੇ ਮਨੈ ਕਰਿ ਮਾਨ ਬੈਨ ਨ ਏਕ ॥
644.t: taat maat rahe manai kar maan bain na ek ||

644.g: ਘੋਰ ਕਾਨਿਨ ਕੌ ਚਲਾ ਧਰਿ ਜੋਗਿ ਨ੍ਯਾਸ ਅਨੇਕ ॥੧੧੩॥
644.t: ghor kaanin kau chalaa dhar jog nayaas anek ||113||
644.e: Though the parents dissuaded him, he did not accept the saying of anyone he assumed the garb of a Yogi and went towards a dense forest.113.

644.g: ਘੋਰ ਕਾਨਨਿ ਮੈ ਕਰੀ ਤਪਸਾ ਅਨੇਕ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਰ ॥
644.t: ghor kaanan mai karee tapasaa anek prakaar ||

644.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਕਰੇ ਇਕ ਚਿਤ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਉਚਾਰ ॥
644.t: bhaat bhaatin ke kare ik chit ma(n)tr uchaar ||
644.e: In the forest, he performed austerities in many ways and concentrating his mind, he recited various kinds of mantras

644.g: ਕਸਟ ਕੈ ਜਬ ਹੀ ਕੀਆ ਤਪ ਘੋਰ ਬਰਖ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਨ ॥
644.t: kasaT kai jab hee keeaa tap ghor barakh pramaan ||

644.g: ਬੁਧਿ ਕੋ ਬਰੁ ਦੇਤ ਭੇ ਤਬ ਆਨਿ ਬੁਧਿ ਨਿਧਾਨ ॥੧੧੪॥
644.t: budh ko bar dhet bhe tab aan budh nidhaan ||114||
644.e: When he, enduring tribulations for many years, performed great austerities, then the Lord, the treasure of wisdom, gave him the boon of ‘wisdom’.114.

644.g: ਬੁਧਿ ਕੌ ਬਰੁ ਜਉ ਦਯੋ ਤਿਨ ਆਨ ਬੁਧ ਅਨੰਤ ॥
644.t: budh kau bar jau dhayo tin aan budh ana(n)t ||

644.g: ਪਰਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਪਵਿਤ੍ਰ ਕੈ ਗਏ ਦਤ ਦੇਵ ਮਹੰਤ ॥
644.t: param purakh pavitr kai ge dhat dhev maha(n)t ||
644.e: When this boon was bestowed upon him, then infinite wisdom penetrated within him and that great Dutt, reached the abode of that supreme Purusha (Lord)

644.g: ਅਕਸਮਾਤ੍ਰ ਬਢੀ ਤਬੈ ਬੁਧਿ ਜਤ੍ਰ ਤਤ੍ਰ ਦਿਸਾਨ ॥
644.t: akasamaatr baddee tabai budh jatr tatr dhisaan ||

644.g: ਧਰਮ ਪ੍ਰਚੁਰ ਕੀਆ ਜਹੀ ਤਹ ਪਰਮ ਪਾਪ ਖਿਸਾਨ ॥੧੧੫॥
644.t: dharam prachur keeaa jahee teh param paap khisaan ||115||
644.e: This wisdom suddenly extended on various sides and he propagated Dharma, which destroyed the sins.115.

644.g: ਪ੍ਰਿਥਮ ਅਕਾਲ ਗੁਰੂ ਕੀਆ ਜਿਹ ਕੋ ਕਬੈ ਨਹੀ ਨਾਸ ॥
644.t: piratham akaal guroo keeaa jeh ko kabai nahee naas ||

644.g: ਜਤ੍ਰ ਤਤ੍ਰ ਦਿਸਾ ਵਿਸਾ ਜਿਹ ਠਉਰ ਸਰਬ ਨਿਵਾਸ ॥
644.t: jatr tatr dhisaa visaa jeh Thaur sarab nivaas ||
644.e: In this way, he adopted the eternal unmanifested Brahman as His first Guru, who pervades in all directions He who has spread the four major divisions of creation viz.,

644.g: ਅੰਡ ਜੇਰਜ ਸੇਤ ਉਤਭੁਜ ਕੀਨ ਜਾਸ ਪਸਾਰ ॥
644.t: a(n)dd jeraj set utabhuj keen jaas pasaar ||

644.g: ਤਾਹਿ ਜਾਨ ਗੁਰੂ ਕੀਯੋ ਮੁਨਿ ਸਤਿ ਦਤ ਸੁ ਧਾਰ ॥੧੧੬॥
644.t: taeh jaan guroo keeyo mun sat dhat su dhaar ||116||
644.e: Andaja (oviparous) Jeraj (viviparous), Svetaja (generated by heat and moisture) and Utbhija (germinating), the sage Dutt accepted that Lord as his first Guru.116.

644.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਦਤ ਮਹਾਤਮੇ ਪ੍ਰਥਮ ਗੁਰੂ ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਸਮਾਪਤੰ ॥੧॥
644.t: eit sree dhat mahaatame pratham guroo akaal purakh samaapata(n) ||1||
644.e: End of the description about the adoption of the Unmanifested Brahman as the first Guru.

644.g: ਰੂਆਲ ਛੰਦ ॥
644.t: rooaal chha(n)dh ||
644.e: (Now begins the description of the second Guru) ROOAAL STANZA

644.g: ਪਰਮ ਰੂਪ ਪਵਿਤ੍ਰ ਮੁਨਿ ਮਨ ਜੋਗ ਕਰਮ ਨਿਧਾਨ ॥
644.t: param roop pavitr mun man jog karam nidhaan ||

644.g: ਦੂਸਰੇ ਗੁਰ ਕਉ ਕਰਾ ਮਨ ਈ ਮਨੈ ਮੁਨਿ ਮਾਨਿ ॥
644.t: dhoosare gur kau karaa man iee manai mun maan ||
644.e: The sage Dutt, supremely immaculate and the ocean of Yoga, then meditated in his mind on the second Guru sand made the mind his guru

644.g: ਨਾਥ ਤਉ ਹੀ ਪਛਾਨ ਜੋ ਮਨ ਮਾਨਈ ਜਿਹ ਕਾਲ ॥
644.t: naath tau hee pachhaan jo man maaniee jeh kaal ||

644.g: ਸਿਧ ਤਉ ਮਨ ਕਾਮਨਾ ਸੁਧ ਹੋਤ ਹੈ ਸੁਨਿ ਲਾਲ ॥੧੧੭॥
644.t: sidh tau man kaamanaa sudh hot hai sun laal ||117||
644.e: When the mind becomes stable, that supreme Lord is recognized and the heart’s desires are fulfilled.117.

644.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਦਤ ਮਹਾਤਮੇ ਦੁਤੀਆ ਗੁਰੂ ਮਨ ਬਰਨਨੰ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤੰ ॥੨॥
644.t: eit sree dhat mahaatame dhuteeaa guroo man baranana(n) dhiaai samaapata(n) ||2||
644.e: End of the chapter entitled “Description of the second Guru.”

644.g: ਭੁਜੰਗ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਤ ਛੰਦ ॥
644.t: bhuja(n)g prayaat chha(n)dh ||
644.e: (Now begins the description of Dashaam) BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

644.g: ਜਬੈ ਦ੍ਵੈ ਸੁ ਕੀਨੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਦਤ ਦੇਵੰ ॥
644.t: jabai dhavai su keene guroo dhat dheva(n) ||

644.g: ਸਦਾ ਏਕ ਚਿਤੰ ਕਰੈ ਨਿਤ ਸੇਵੰ ॥
644.t: sadhaa ek chita(n) karai nit seva(n) ||
644.e: When Dutt adopted two Guru and he always served them single-mindedly

644.g: ਜਟਾ ਜੂਟ ਸੀਸੰ ਸੁ ਗੰਗਾ ਤਰੰਗੰ ॥
644.t: jaTaa jooT seesa(n) su ga(n)gaa tara(n)ga(n) ||

644.g: ਕਬੈ ਛ੍ਵੈ ਸਕਾ ਅੰਗ ਕੋ ਨ ਅਨੰਗੰ ॥੧੧੮॥
644.t: kabai chhavai sakaa a(n)g ko na ana(n)ga(n) ||118||
644.e: The waves of the Ganges and the matted locks were auspiciously seated on his head and the god of love could never touch his body.118.

644.g: ਮਹਾ ਉਜਲੀ ਅੰਗ ਬਿਭੂਤ ਸੋਹੈ ॥
644.t: mahaa ujalee a(n)g bibhoot sohai ||

644.g: ਲਖੈ ਮੋਨ ਮਾਨੀ ਮਹਾ ਮਾਨ ਮੋਹੈ ॥
644.t: lakhai mon maanee mahaa maan mohai ||
644.e: There were white ashes smeared on his body and he was alluring the mind of very honoured persons

644.g: ਜਟਾ ਜੂਟ ਗੰਗਾ ਤਰੰਗੰ ਮਹਾਨੰ ॥
644.t: jaTaa jooT ga(n)gaa tara(n)ga(n) mahaana(n) ||

644.g: ਮਹਾ ਬੁਧਿ ਉਦਾਰ ਬਿਦਿਆ ਨਿਧਾਨੰ ॥੧੧੯॥
644.t: mahaa budh udhaar bidhiaa nidhaana(n) ||119||
644.e: The sage appeared very great with the waves of the Ganges and matted locks he was the treasure of generous wisdom and learning.119.

644.g: ਭਗਉਹੇ ਲਸੈ ਬਸਤ੍ਰ ਲੰਗੋਟ ਬੰਦੰ ॥
644.t: bhagauhe lasai basatr la(n)goT ba(n)dha(n) ||
644.e: He wore ochre-coloured clothes and also the loin-cloth

644.g: ਤਜੇ ਸਰਬ ਆਸਾ ਰਟੈ ਏਕ ਛੰਦੰ ॥
644.t: taje sarab aasaa raTai ek chha(n)dha(n) ||
644.e: He had forsaken all the expectations and recited only one mantra

644.g: ਮਹਾ ਮੋਨ ਮਾਨੀ ਮਹਾ ਮੋਨ ਬਾਧੇ ॥
644.t: mahaa mon maanee mahaa mon baadhe ||

644.g: ਮਹਾ ਜੋਗ ਕਰਮੰ ਸਭੈ ਨ੍ਯਾਸ ਸਾਧੇ ॥੧੨੦॥
644.t: mahaa jog karama(n) sabhai nayaas saadhe ||120||
644.e: He was a great silence-observer and practiced of all the practices of that actions of Yoga.120.

644.g: ਦਯਾ ਸਿੰਧੁ ਸਰਬੰ ਸੁਭੰ ਕਰਮ ਕਰਤਾ ॥
644.t: dhayaa si(n)dh saraba(n) subha(n) karam karataa ||

644.g: ਹਰੇ ਸਰਬ ਗਰਬੰ ਮਹਾ ਤੇਜ ਧਰਤਾ ॥
644.t: hare sarab garaba(n) mahaa tej dharataa ||
644.e: He was greatly glorious as the ocean of mercy, the doer of good actions and the smasher of the pride of all

644.g: ਮਹਾ ਜੋਗ ਕੀ ਸਾਧਨਾ ਸਰਬ ਸਾਧੀ ॥
644.t: mahaa jog kee saadhanaa sarab saadhee ||

644.g: ਮਹਾ ਮੋਨ ਮਾਨੀ ਮਹਾ ਸਿਧ ਲਾਧੀ ॥੧੨੧॥
644.t: mahaa mon maanee mahaa sidh laadhee ||121||
644.e: He was the practiser of all the practices of great Yoga and was a purusha of silence observation and the discoverer of the great powers.121.

644.g: ਉਠੈ ਪ੍ਰਾਤਿ ਸੰਧਿਆ ਕਰੈ ਨਾਨ ਜਾਵੈ ॥
644.t: auThai praat sa(n)dhiaa karai naan jaavai ||

644.g: ਕਰੈ ਸਾਧਨਾ ਜੋਗ ਕੀ ਜੋਗ ਭਾਵੈ ॥
644.t: karai saadhanaa jog kee jog bhaavai ||
644.e: He used to go for a bath in the mornings and evenings and practiced Yoga

644.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਕਾਲਗ ਦਰਸੀ ਮਹਾ ਪਰਮ ਤਤੰ ॥
644.t: tirakaalag dharasee mahaa param tata(n) ||

644.g: ਸੁ ਸੰਨ੍ਰਯਾਸੁ ਦੇਵੰ ਮਹਾ ਸੁਧ ਮਤੰ ॥੧੨੨॥
644.t: s sa(n)nrayaas dheva(n) mahaa sudh mata(n) ||122||
644.e: He could observe the past, present and future and was divinely-incarnate saint of pure intellect amongst all the Sannyasis.122.

644.g: ਪਿਯਾਸਾ ਛੁਧਾ ਆਨ ਕੈ ਜੋ ਸੰਤਾਵੈ ॥
644.t: piyaasaa chhudhaa aan kai jo sa(n)taavai ||

645.g: ਰਹੇ ਏਕ ਚਿਤੰ ਨ ਚਿਤੰ ਚਲਾਵੈ ॥
645.t: rahe ek chita(n) na chita(n) chalaavai ||
645.e: He did not allow his mind to become mercurial even on being afflicted by hunger and thirst
He, remaining supremely unattached, and wearing the patched cloak, practiced Yoga, for the realization of the light of the Supreme Essence.123.

645.g: ਮਹਾ ਆਤਮ ਦਰਸੀ ਮਹਾ ਤਤ ਬੇਤਾ ॥
645.t: mahaa aatam dharasee mahaa tat betaa ||

645.e: He was a great self-knowing, essence-knowing, stable Yogi performing austerities in upside down posture
He was the destroyer of evil actions through good actions and was ever and unattached ascetic of stable mind.124.
He used to live in the forest, studying all Shastras, destroying evil actions as a worthy traveler on the path of detachment

645.g: ਤਜ੍ਯੋ ਕਾਮ ਕਰੋਧੰ ਸਬੈ ਲੋਭ ਮੋਹੰ ॥
645.t: tajayo kaam karodha(n) sabai lobh moha(n) ||

645.g: ਮਹਾ ਜੋਗ ਜ੍ਵਾਲਾ ਮਹਾ ਮੋਨਿ ਸੋਹੰ ॥੧੨੫॥
645.t: mahaa jog javaiaalaa mahaa mon soha(n) ||125||
645.e: He had forsaken lust, anger, greed and attachment and was a supreme silence-observer and the adopter of the fire of Yoga.125.
He was the practiser of various kinds, a great celibate and an authority on Dharma

645.g: ਮਹਾ ਤਤ ਬੇਤਾ ਸੁ ਸੰਨ੍ਯਾਸ ਜੋਗੰ ॥
645.t: mahaa tat betaa su sa(n)nayaas joga(n) ||
645.e: He was a great knower of essence, knower of the secrets of Yoga and Sannyas and
A detached ascetic he always remained in good health.126.
He was without expectations, practiser of austerities in upside-down posture, a great knower of essence and an unattached Sannyasi

645.g: ਸਬੈ ਜੋਗ ਸਾਧੈ ਰਹੈ ਏਕ ਚਿਤੰ ॥
645.t: sabai jog saadhai rahai ek chita(n) ||
645.e: He practiced all kinds of Yogic postures with concentration

645.g: ਤਜੈ ਅਉਰ ਸਰਬੰ ਗਹ੍ਰਯੋ ਏਕ ਹਿਤੰ ॥੧੨੭॥
645.t: tajai aaur saraba(n) gahrayo ek hita(n) ||127||
645.e: Forsaking all other desire, he meditated only on the one Lord.127.

645.g: ਤਰੇ ਤਾਪ ਧੂਮੰ ਕਰੈ ਪਾਨ ਉਚੰ ॥
645.t: tare taap dhooma(n) karai paan ucha(n) ||

645.g: ਝੁਲੈ ਮਧਿ ਅਗਨੰ ਤਉ ਧਿਆਨ ਮੁਚੰ ॥
645.t: jhulai madh agana(n) tau dhiaan mucha(n) ||
645.e: While seated near the fire and smoke, he had raised his hand and while meditating, burning the fires in all the four directions, he was internally scorching it

645.g: ਭਏ ਦਤ ਕੇ ਰੁਦ੍ਰ ਪੂਰਣ ਵਤਾਰੀ ॥੧੨੮॥
645.t: bhe dhat ke rudhr pooran vataaree ||128||
645.e: He was the celibate adopting a great religion and also the perfect incarnation of Rudra.128.
He was persistent silence-observer performing austerities, a great knower of mantras and the treasure of generosity

645.g: ਕਰੈ ਜੋਗ ਨ੍ਯਾਸੰ ਤਜੇ ਰਾਜ ਭੋਗੰ ॥
645.t: karai jog nayaasa(n) taje raaj bhoga(n) ||

645.g: ਚਕੇ ਸਰਬ ਦੇਵੰ ਜਕੇ ਸਰਬ ਲੋਗੰ ॥੧੨੯॥
645.t: chake sarab dheva(n) jake sarab loga(n) ||129||
645.e: While abandoning the royal enjoyments, he was practising Yoga and seeing him, all the men and hods were wonder-struck.129.
Seeing him, the Gandharvas, who were the treasure of science, and Chandra, Surya, the king of gods and other gods full of astonishment

645.g: ਛਕੇ ਜੀਵ ਜੰਤ੍ਰੰ ਲਖੇ ਪਰਮ ਰੂਪੰ ॥
645.t: chhake jeev ja(n)tra(n) lakhe param roopa(n) ||

645.g: ਤਜ੍ਯੋ ਗਰਬ ਸਰਬੰ ਲਗੇ ਪਾਨ ਭੂਪੰ ॥੧੩੦॥
645.t: tajayo garab saraba(n) lage paan bhoopa(n) ||130||
645.e: All the creatures were pleased to see his comely figure and all the kings, abandoning their pride, had fallen on his feet.130.
There were also there mighty warriors living on mountains and other countries
The mighty ones of Balkh, Bengal, Russia and Ruhekhand were also there, in his shelter.131.

The saints with matted locks, the deceptors, deceiving people through Yantras and Mantras, the residents of Aj Pradesh and Aabhir Desh and the Yogis performing Neoli Karma (purging of intestines) were also there
All Atev Agnihotris, controlling the world and the perfect celibates adopting celibacy at all levels were also in his refuge.132.

645.g: ਸਬੈ ਪਾਨ ਲਗੇ ਤਜ੍ਯੋ ਗਰਬ ਭਾਰੀ ॥
645.t: sabai paan lage tajayo garab bhaaree ||
645.e: All the canopied kings of far and near, they all fell at his feet, leaving their pride

645.g: ਕਰੈ ਲਾਗ ਸਰਬੰ ਸੁ ਸੰਨ੍ਯਾਸ ਜੋਗੰ ॥
645.t: karai laag saraba(n) su sa(n)nayaas joga(n) ||

645.g: ਇਹੀ ਪੰਥ ਲਾਗੇ ਸੁਭੰ ਸਰਬ ਲੋਗੰ ॥੧੩੩॥
645.t: eihee pa(n)th laage subha(n) sarab loga(n) ||133||
645.e: They all practiced Sannyas and Yoga and al of them became followers of this path.133.

645.g: ਸਬੇ ਦੇਸ ਦੇਸਾਨ ਤੇ ਲੋਗ ਆਏ ॥
645.t: sabe dhes dhesaan te log aae ||

645.g: ਕਰੰ ਦਤ ਕੇ ਆਨਿ ਮੂੰਡੰ ਮੁੰਡਾਏ ॥
645.t: kara(n) dhat ke aan moo(n)dda(n) mu(n)ddaae ||
645.e: The people of various countries from far and near, came and got performed the tonsure ceremony from the hands of Dutt,

645.g: ਧਰੇ ਸੀਸ ਪੈ ਪਰਮ ਜੂਟੇ ਜਟਾਨੰ ॥
645.t: dhare sees pai param jooTe jaTaana(n) ||

645.e: And many people wearing matted locks on their head, practiced Yoga and Sannyas.134.
ROOAAL STANZA

646.g: ਦੇਸ ਦੇਸਨ ਕੇ ਸਬੈ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਆਨਿ ਕੈ ਤਹਿ ਠਉਰ ॥
646.t: dhes dhesan ke sabai nirap aan kai teh Thaur ||

646.g: ਜਾਨਿ ਪਾਨ ਪਰੈ ਸਬੈ ਗੁਰੁ ਦਤ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਸਰਮਉਰ ॥
646.t: jaan paan parai sabai gur dhat sree saramaur ||
646.e: The kings of various countries from far and near fell at the feet of the supreme Guru Dutt at that place

646.g: ਤਿਆਗਿ ਅਉਰ ਨਏ ਮਤਿ ਏਕ ਹੀ ਮਤਿ ਠਾਨ ॥
646.t: tiaag aaur ne mat ek hee mat Thaan ||
646.e: They all abandoned the new sects and joined the one sect of Yoga

646.g: ਆਨਿ ਮੂੰਡ ਮੁੰਡਾਤ ਭੇ ਸਭ ਰਾਜ ਪਾਟ ਨਿਧਾਨ ॥੧੩੫॥
646.t: aan moo(n)dd mu(n)ddaat bhe sabh raaj paaT nidhaan ||135||
646.e: They abandoned their royal responsibilities and came to get done their tonsure ceremony.135.

646.g: ਆਨਿ ਆਨਿ ਲਗੇ ਸਬੈ ਪਗ ਜਾਨਿ ਕੈ ਗੁਰਦੇਵ ॥
646.t: aan aan lage sabai pag jaan kai gurdhev ||

646.g: ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਸਾਸਤ੍ਰ ਸਬੈ ਭ੍ਰਿਤਾਬਰ ਅਨੰਤ ਰੂਪ ਅਭੇਵ ॥
646.t: sasatr saasatr sabai bhirataabar ana(n)t roop abhev ||
646.e: All of them, considering him as the Supreme Guru, came to bow at his feet and Dutt was also the great purusha comprehending the secret of weapons and Shastras

646.g: ਅਛਿਦ ਗਾਤ ਅਛਿਜ ਰੂਪ ਅਭਿਦ ਜੋਗ ਦੁਰੰਤ ॥
646.t: achhidh gaat achhij roop abhidh jog dhura(n)t ||
646.e: His body was invincible, the form indestructible and he had achieved oneness in Yoga

646.g: ਅਮਿਤ ਉਜਲ ਅਜਿਤ ਪਰਮ ਉਪਜਿਓ ਸੁ ਦਤ ਮਹੰਤ ॥੧੩੬॥
646.t: amit ujal ajit param upajio su dhat maha(n)t ||136||
646.e: He has manifested himself in the form of unlimited, lustrous and unconquerable power.136.

646.g: ਪੇਖਿ ਰੂਪ ਚਕੇ ਚਰਾਚਰ ਸਰਬ ਬ੍ਯੋਮ ਬਿਮਾਨ ॥
646.t: pekh roop chake charaachar sarab bayom bimaan ||
646.e: The animate and inanimate creation and the gods of heaven, were wonder-struck on seeing his figure and

646.g: ਜਤ੍ਰ ਤਤ੍ਰ ਰਹੇ ਨਰਾਧਪ ਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਰੂਪ ਸਮਾਨ ॥
646.t: jatr tatr rahe naraadhap chitr roop samaan ||
646.e: The kings looked splendid like the pretty portraits here and there

646.g: ਅਤ੍ਰ ਛਤ੍ਰ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤ ਕੋ ਤਜਿ ਜੋਗ ਲੈ ਸੰਨ੍ਯਾਸ ॥
646.t: atr chhatr nirapat ko taj jog lai sa(n)nayaas ||
646.e: They all had forsaken their arms and canopies, had been initiated into Sannyas and Yoga and

646.g: ਆਨਿ ਆਨਿ ਕਰੈ ਲਗੇ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਜਤ੍ਰ ਤਤ੍ਰ ਉਦਾਸ ॥੧੩੭॥
646.t: aan aan karai lage havai jatr tatr udhaas ||137||
646.e: Had come to him as ascetics from all directions and were there at his feet.137.

646.g: ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਉਪਿੰਦ੍ਰ ਚਕੇ ਸਬੈ ਚਿਤ ਚਉਕਿਯੋ ਸਸਿ ਭਾਨੁ ॥
646.t: ei(n)dhr upi(n)dhr chake sabai chit chaukiyo sas bhaan ||
646.e: Indra, Upendra, Surya, Chandra etc. all marveled in their mind and

646.g: ਲੈ ਨ ਦਤ ਛਨਾਇ ਆਜ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤ ਮੋਰ ਮਹਾਨ ॥
646.t: lai na dhat chhanai aaj nirapat mor mahaan ||
646.e: Were thinking that the great Dutt may not seize their kingdom

646.g: ਰੀਝ ਰੀਝ ਰਹੇ ਜਹਾ ਤਹਾ ਸਰਬ ਬ੍ਯੋਮ ਬਿਮਾਨ ॥
646.t: reejh reejh rahe jahaa tahaa sarab bayom bimaan ||
646.e: All were getting pleased in the sky, sitting in their vehicles and

646.g: ਜਾਨ ਜਾਨ ਸਬੈ ਪਰੇ ਗੁਰਦੇਵ ਦਤ ਮਹਾਨ ॥੧੩੮॥
646.t: jaan jaan sabai pare gurdhev dhat mahaan ||138||
646.e: Were considering Dutt as the great Guru.138.

646.g: ਜਤ੍ਰ ਤਤ੍ਰ ਦਿਸਾ ਵਿਸਾ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਰਾਜ ਸਾਜ ਬਿਸਾਰ ॥
646.t: jatr tatr dhisaa visaa nirap raaj saaj bisaar ||

646.g: ਆਨਿ ਆਨਿ ਸਬੋ ਗਹੇ ਪਗ ਦਤ ਦੇਵ ਉਦਾਰ ॥
646.t: aan aan sabo gahe pag dhat dhev udhaar ||
646.e: Here and there, in all the directions, the kings, forgetting their royal responsibilities, had caught the feet of the supremely generous Dutt

646.g: ਜਾਨਿ ਜਾਨਿ ਸੁ ਧਰਮ ਕੋ ਘਰ ਮਾਨਿ ਕੈ ਗੁਰਦੇਵ ॥
646.t: jaan jaan su dharam ko ghar maan kai gurdhev ||
646.e: Considering him as the treasure of dharma and the great Guru,

646.g: ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਮਾਨ ਸਬੈ ਲਗੇ ਮਨ ਛਾਡਿ ਕੈ ਅਹੰਮੇਵ ॥੧੩੯॥
646.t: preet maan sabai lage man chhaadd kai aha(n)mev ||139||
646.e: All had abandoned their ego and had dedicated themselves affectionately in his service.139.

646.g: ਰਾਜ ਸਾਜ ਸਬੈ ਤਜੇ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਭੇਸ ਕੈ ਸੰਨ੍ਯਾਸ ॥
646.t: raaj saaj sabai taje nirap bhes kai sa(n)nayaas ||
646.e: The kings had worn the garb of Sannyas and Yoga, leaving their royal responsibilities and

646.g: ਆਨਿ ਜੋਗ ਕਰੈ ਲਗੇ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਜਤ੍ਰ ਤਤ੍ਰ ਉਦਾਸ ॥
646.t: aan jog karai lage havai jatr tatr udhaas ||
646.e: Becoming unattached, they had begun the practice of Yoga

646.g: ਮੰਡਿ ਅੰਗਿ ਬਿਭੂਤ ਉਜਲ ਸੀਸ ਜੂਟ ਜਟਾਨ ॥
646.t: ma(n)dd a(n)g bibhoot ujal sees jooT jaTaan ||
646.e: Smearing their bodies with ashes and wearing matted locks on their heads,

646.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਨ ਸੌ ਸੁਭੇ ਸਭ ਰਾਜ ਪਾਟ ਨਿਧਾਨ ॥੧੪੦॥
646.t: bhaat bhaatan sau subhe sabh raaj paaT nidhaan ||140||
646.e: Various types of kings had gathered there.140.

646.g: ਜਤ੍ਰ ਤਤ੍ਰ ਬਿਸਾਰਿ ਸੰਪਤਿ ਪੁਤ੍ਰ ਮਿਤ੍ਰ ਕਲਤ੍ਰ ॥
646.t: jatr tatr bisaar sa(n)pat putr mitr kalatr ||
646.e: All the kings, leaving their property, wealth, son friends and the attachment of he queens,

646.g: ਭੇਸ ਲੈ ਸੰਨ੍ਯਾਸ ਕੋ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਛਾਡਿ ਕੈ ਜਯ ਪਤ੍ਰ ॥
646.t: bhes lai sa(n)nayaas ko nirap chhaadd kai jay patr ||
646.e: Their honours and victories, they adopted Sannyas and Yoga and have come there

646.g: ਬਾਜ ਰਾਜ ਸਮਾਜ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਛਾਡ ਕੇ ਗਜ ਰਾਜ ॥
646.t: baaj raaj samaaj su(n)dhar chhaadd ke gaj raaj ||
646.e: They came and sat there as ascetics here and there gathering together from all directions,

646.g: ਆਨਿ ਆਨਿ ਬਸੇ ਮਹਾ ਬਨਿ ਜਤ੍ਰ ਤਤ੍ਰ ਉਦਾਸ ॥੧੪੧॥
646.t: aan aan base mahaa ban jatr tatr udhaas ||141||
646.e: Leaving behind elephants and horses and their fine society.141.

646.g: ਪਾਧੜੀ ਛੰਦ ॥ ਤ੍ਵਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ॥
646.t: paadhaRee chha(n)dh || tavaiprasaadh ||
646.e: PAADHARI STANZA BY THY GRACE

646.g: ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਸਰਬ ਛਿਤ ਕੇ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਾਲ ॥
646.t: eeh bhaat sarab chhit ke nirapaal ||

646.g: ਸੰਨ੍ਯਾਸ ਜੋਗ ਲਾਗੇ ਉਤਾਲ ॥
646.t: sa(n)nayaas jog laage utaal ||
646.e: In this way, all the kings of the earth immediately joined the path of Sannyas and Yoga

646.g: ਇਕ ਕਰੈ ਲਾਗਿ ਨਿਵਲਿ ਆਦਿ ਕਰਮ ॥
646.t: eik karai laag nival aadh karam ||

646.g: ਇਕ ਧਰਤ ਧਿਆਨ ਲੈ ਬਸਤ੍ਰ ਚਰਮ ॥੧੪੨॥
646.t: eik dharat dhiaan lai basatr charam ||142||
646.e: Someone performed the Neoli Karma (purging of insestines) and someone wearing the garments of hide, was absorbed in meditation.142.

646.g: ਇਕ ਧਰਤ ਬਸਤ੍ਰ ਬਲਕਲਨ ਅੰਗਿ ॥
646.t: eik dharat basatr balakalan a(n)g ||

646.g: ਇਕ ਰਹਤ ਕਲਪ ਇਸਥਿਤ ਉਤੰਗ ॥
646.t: eik rahat kalap isathit uta(n)g ||
646.e: Someone is wearing the garments of a recluse and someone is standing straight with a special notion

646.g: ਇਕ ਕਰਤ ਅਲਪ ਦੁਗਧਾ ਅਹਾਰ ॥
646.t: eik karat alap dhugadhaa ahaar ||

646.g: ਇਕ ਰਹਤ ਬਰਖ ਬਹੁ ਨਿਰਾਹਾਰ ॥੧੪੩॥
646.t: eik rahat barakh bahu niraahaar ||143||
646.e: Someone subsists only on milk and someone abides without eating and srinking.143.

646.g: ਇਕ ਰਹਤ ਮੋਨ ਮੋਨੀ ਮਹਾਨ ॥
646.t: eik rahat mon monee mahaan ||

646.g: ਇਕ ਕਰਤ ਨ੍ਯਾਸ ਤਜਿ ਖਾਨ ਪਾਨ ॥
646.t: eik karat nayaas taj khaan paan ||
646.e: Those great saints observed silence and many practiced Yoga without eating and drinking

646.g: ਇਕ ਰਹਤ ਏਕ ਪਗ ਨਿਰਾਧਾਰ ॥
646.t: eik rahat ek pag niraadhaar ||

646.g: ਇਕ ਬਸਤ ਗ੍ਰਾਮ ਕਾਨਨ ਪਹਾਰ ॥੧੪੪॥
646.t: eik basat graam kaanan pahaar ||144||
646.e: Many stood on one foot without and support and many resided in villages, forests and mountains.144.

646.g: ਇਕ ਕਰਤ ਕਸਟ ਕਰ ਧੂਮ੍ਰ ਪਾਨ ॥
646.t: eik karat kasaT kar dhoomr paan ||

646.g: ਇਕ ਕਰਤ ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿਨ ਸਨਾਨ ॥
646.t: eik karat bhaat bhaatin sanaan ||
646.e: Many taking in smoke endured suffering and many took baths of different kinds

646.g: ਇਕ ਰਹਤ ਇਕ ਪਗ ਜੁਗ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਨ ॥
646.t: eik rahat ik pag jug pramaan ||

646.g: ਕਈ ਊਰਧ ਬਾਹ ਮੁਨਿ ਮਨ ਮਹਾਨ ॥੧੪੫॥
646.t: kiee uooradh baeh mun man mahaan ||145||
646.e: Many stood on their foot for ages and many great sages turned their arms upwards.145.

646.g: ਇਕ ਰਹਤ ਬੈਠਿ ਜਲਿ ਮਧਿ ਜਾਇ ॥
646.t: eik rahat baiTh jal madh jai ||

646.g: ਇਕ ਤਪਤ ਆਗਿ ਊਰਧ ਜਰਾਇ ॥
646.t: eik tapat aag uooradh jarai ||
646.e: Someone sat down in water and many made themselves warm by burning fire

646.g: ਇਕ ਕਰਤ ਨ੍ਯਾਸ ਬਹੁ ਬਿਧਿ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਰ ॥
646.t: eik karat nayaas bahu bidh prakaar ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਰਹਤ ਏਕ ਆਸਾ ਅਧਾਰ ॥੧੪੬॥
647.t: eik rahat ek aasaa adhaar ||146||
647.e: Someone practiced various postures and someone continued to live on the strength of one desire.146.

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਕਬਹੂੰ ਨੀਚ ਨਹੀ ਕਰਤ ਡੀਠ ॥
647.t: keiee kabahoo(n) neech nahee karat ddeeTh ||

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਤਪਤ ਆਗਿ ਪਰ ਜਾਰ ਪੀਠ ॥
647.t: keiee tapat aag par jaar peeTh ||
647.e: There are many who do not see below and many warm themselves by burning fire on their back

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਬੈਠ ਕਰਤ ਬ੍ਰਤ ਚਰਜ ਦਾਨ ॥
647.t: keiee baiTh karat brat charaj dhaan ||

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਧਰਤ ਚਿਤ ਏਕੈ ਨਿਧਾਨ ॥੧੪੭॥
647.t: keiee dharat chit ekai nidhaan ||147||
647.e: Some sit down and hold fasts and bestow charities and many are absorbed only in One Lord.147.

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਕਰਤ ਜਗਿ ਅਰੁ ਹੋਮ ਦਾਨ ॥
647.t: keiee karat jag ar hom dhaan ||

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਬਿਧਵਤਿ ਇਸਨਾਨ ॥
647.t: keiee bhaat bhaat bidhavat isanaan ||
647.e: Many take bath according to Shastric injuctions in various ways

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਧਰਤ ਜਾਇ ਲੈ ਪਿਸਟ ਪਾਨ ॥
647.t: keiee dharat jai lai pisaT paan ||

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਦੇਤ ਕਰਮ ਕੀ ਛਾਡਿ ਬਾਨ ॥੧੪੮॥
647.t: keiee dhet karam kee chhaadd baan ||148||
647.e: And many are busy in Yajnas charities and hom many are standing with their hands touching the earth at their back and many forsaking crores of rupees are donating whatever they have with th

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਕਰਤ ਬੈਠਿ ਪਰਮੰ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ ॥
647.t: keiee karat baiTh parama(n) prakaas ||

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਭ੍ਰਮਤ ਪਬ ਬਨਿ ਬਨਿ ਉਦਾਸ ॥
647.t: keiee bhramat pab ban ban udhaas ||
647.e: Many are sitting in Supreme Light and many are roaming unattached on mountain and in the forest

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਰਹਤ ਏਕ ਆਸਨ ਅਡੋਲ ॥
647.t: keiee rahat ek aasan addol ||

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਜਪਤ ਬੈਠਿ ਮੁਖ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਅਮੋਲ ॥੧੪੯॥
647.t: keiee japat baiTh mukh ma(n)tr amol ||149||
647.e: Many are sitting in one posture and many are reciting mantras.149.

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਕਰਤ ਬੈਠਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਉਚਾਰ ॥
647.t: keiee karat baiTh har har uchaar ||

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਕਰਤ ਪਾਠ ਮੁਨਿ ਮਨ ਉਦਾਰ ॥
647.t: keiee karat paaTh mun man udhaar ||
647.e: Some are uttering the Name of the Lord while sitting and some sages are reading the religious text with a generous heart

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਭਗਤਿ ਭਾਵ ਭਗਵਤ ਭਜੰਤ ॥
647.t: keiee bhagat bhaav bhagavat bhaja(n)t ||

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਰਿਚਾ ਬੇਦ ਸਿੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਟੰਤ ॥੧੫੦॥
647.t: keiee richaa bedh si(n)mirat raTa(n)t ||150||
647.e: Many are meditating on the Lord with devotion and many are repeating the Vedic verses and Smritis.150.

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਏਕ ਪਾਨ ਅਸਥਿਤ ਅਡੋਲ ॥
647.t: keiee ek paan asathit addol ||

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਜਪਤ ਜਾਪ ਮਨਿ ਚਿਤ ਖੋਲਿ ॥
647.t: keiee japat jaap man chit khol ||
647.e: Many are standing on one hand and many are reciting mantras with fullness of mind

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਰਹਤ ਏਕ ਮਨ ਨਿਰਾਹਾਰ ॥
647.t: keiee rahat ek man niraahaar ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਭਛਤ ਪਉਨ ਮੁਨਿ ਮਨ ਉਦਾਰ ॥੧੫੧॥
647.t: eik bhachhat paun mun man udhaar ||151||
647.e: Many go without food and many sages only subsist on air.151.

647.g: ਇਕ ਕਰਤ ਨਿਆਸ ਆਸਾ ਬਿਹੀਨ ॥
647.t: eik karat niaas aasaa biheen ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਰਹਤ ਏਕ ਭਗਵਤ ਅਧੀਨ ॥
647.t: eik rahat ek bhagavat adheen ||
647.e: Many are sitting in postures, abandoning their desires and expectations and many have resigned themselves to the support of the Lord

647.g: ਇਕ ਕਰਤ ਨੈਕੁ ਬਨ ਫਲ ਅਹਾਰ ॥
647.t: eik karat naik ban fal ahaar ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਰਟਤ ਨਾਮ ਸਿਆਮਾ ਅਪਾਰ ॥੧੫੨॥
647.t: eik raTat naam siaamaa apaar ||152||
647.e: Many are subsisting on small quantity of fruit in the forest and many are only repeating the Name of the Lord.152.

647.g: ਇਕ ਏਕ ਆਸ ਆਸਾ ਬਿਰਹਤ ॥
647.t: eik ek aas aasaa birahat ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਬਹੁਤ ਭਾਤਿ ਦੁਖ ਦੇਹ ਸਹਤ ॥
647.t: eik bahut bhaat dhukh dheh sahat ||
647.e: Many are abiding only with the hope of meeting the Lord and many are enduring many kinds of sufferings

647.g: ਇਕ ਕਹਤ ਏਕ ਹਰਿ ਕੋ ਕਥਾਨ ॥
647.t: eik kahat ek har ko kathaan ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਮੁਕਤ ਪਤ੍ਰ ਪਾਵਤ ਨਿਦਾਨ ॥੧੫੩॥
647.t: eik mukat patr paavat nidhaan ||153||
647.e: Many are busy in speaking a discourse of the Lord and many are ultimately obtaining salvation.153.

647.g: ਇਕ ਪਰੇ ਸਰਣਿ ਹਰਿ ਕੇ ਦੁਆਰ ॥
647.t: eik pare saran har ke dhuaar ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਰਹਤ ਤਾਸੁ ਨਾਮੈ ਅਧਾਰ ॥
647.t: eik rahat taas naamai adhaar ||
647.e: Many have come under the refuge of the Lord and their support is only the name of the Lord

647.g: ਇਕ ਜਪਤ ਨਾਮ ਤਾ ਕੋ ਦੁਰੰਤ ॥
647.t: eik japat naam taa ko dhura(n)t ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਅੰਤਿ ਮੁਕਤਿ ਪਾਵਤ ਬਿਅੰਤ ॥੧੫੪॥
647.t: eik a(n)t mukat paavat bia(n)t ||154||
647.e: Many are repeating His Name and are ultimately obtaining salvation.154.

647.g: ਇਕ ਕਰਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਸ ਦਿਨ ਉਚਾਰ ॥
647.t: eik karat naam nis dhin uchaar ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਅਗਨਿ ਹੋਤ੍ਰ ਬ੍ਰਹਮਾ ਬਿਚਾਰ ॥
647.t: eik agan hotr brahamaa bichaar ||
647.e: Many are uttering the Name of the Lord day and night and many adopting the thought of the Lord in their mind, are performing Agnihotra (the rite of fire-offering)

647.g: ਇਕ ਸਾਸਤ੍ਰ ਸਰਬ ਸਿਮ੍ਰਿਤਿ ਰਟੰਤ ॥
647.t: eik saasatr sarab simirat raTa(n)t ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਸਾਧ ਰੀਤਿ ਨਿਸ ਦਿਨ ਚਲੰਤ ॥੧੫੫॥
647.t: eik saadh reet nis dhin chala(n)t ||155||
647.e: Many are repeating for memory the Shastras and Smritis and many are continuously observing

647.g: ਇਕ ਹੋਮ ਦਾਨ ਅਰੁ ਬੇਦ ਰੀਤਿ ॥
647.t: eik hom dhaan ar bedh reet ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਰਟਤ ਬੈਠਿ ਖਟ ਸਾਸਤ੍ਰ ਮੀਤ ॥
647.t: eik raTat baiTh khaT saasatr meet ||
647.e: Many are performing the acts of hom and charity according to Vedic injunctions and many friends sitting together are cramming the six Shastras

647.g: ਇਕ ਕਰਤ ਬੇਦ ਚਾਰੋ ਉਚਾਰ ॥
647.t: eik karat bedh chaaro uchaar ||

647.g: ਇਕ ਗਿਆਨ ਗਾਥ ਮਹਿਮਾ ਅਪਾਰ ॥੧੫੬॥
647.t: eik giaan gaath mahimaa apaar ||156||
647.e: Many are reciting the four Vedas and are describing the infinite greatness of the discussion about knowledge.15

647.g: ਇਕ ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਮਿਸਟਾਨ ਭੋਜ ॥
647.t: eik bhaat bhaat misaTaan bhoj ||

647.g: ਬਹੁ ਦੀਨ ਬੋਲਿ ਭਛ ਦੇਤ ਰੋਜ ॥
647.t: bahu dheen bol bhachh dhet roj ||
647.e: Many are ever calling lowly and afflicted ones and serving them sweets and food

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਕਰਤ ਬੈਠਿ ਬਹੁ ਭਾਤਿ ਪਾਠ ॥
647.t: keiee karat baiTh bahu bhaat paaTh ||

647.g: ਕਈ ਅੰਨਿ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਚਾਬੰਤ ਕਾਠ ॥੧੫੭॥
647.t: kiee a(n)n tiaag chaaba(n)t kaaTh ||157||
647.e: Many are busy in reciting the religious texts in various ways and many forsaking the corn, are just chewing the wood.157.

647.g: ਪਾਧੜੀ ਛੰਦ ॥
647.t: paadhaRee chha(n)dh ||
647.e: PAADHARI STANZA

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਸੋ ਧਰਤ ਧਿਆਨ ॥
647.t: keiee bhaat bhaat so dharat dhiaan ||

647.g: ਕੇਈ ਕਰਤ ਬੈਠਿ ਹਰਿ ਕ੍ਰਿਤ ਕਾਨਿ ॥
647.t: keiee karat baiTh har kirat kaan ||
647.e: Many are meditating in various ways and many, while sitting, are elucidating about various works of the Lord

648.g: ਨਹੀ ਮੁਰਤ ਕਲਪ ਬਹੁਤ ਜਾਤ ਬੀਤ ॥੧੫੮॥
648.t: nahee murat kalap bahut jaat beet ||158||
648.e: Many are listening to the recitation of the holy religious texts, while sitting and many do not look back even for many Kalpas (ages).158.

648.g: ਕੇਈ ਬੈਠ ਕਰਤ ਜਲਿ ਕੋ ਅਹਾਰ ॥
648.t: keiee baiTh karat jal ko ahaar ||

648.e: Many, being seated, are drinking water and many are roaming on the mountains and countries far and near
Many are sitting in the caves and repeating the Name of the Lord and many celibates are moving in the streams.159.

648.g: ਕੇਈ ਰਹਤ ਬੈਠਿ ਮਧ ਨੀਰ ਜਾਇ ॥
648.t: keiee rahat baiTh madh neer jai ||

648.e: Many are sitting in water and many are warming themselves by burning the fire

648.g: ਕੇਈ ਰਹਤ ਸਿਧਿ ਮੁਖ ਮੋਨ ਠਾਨ ॥
648.t: keiee rahat sidh mukh mon Thaan ||

648.g: ਅਨਿ ਆਸ ਚਿਤ ਇਕ ਆਸ ਮਾਨ ॥੧੬੦॥
648.t: an aas chit ik aas maan ||160||
648.e: Many adepts observing silence, are remembering the Lord and many are absorbed in concentration on the sky in their mind.160.

Many are absorbed in meditation on that stable and vice less Lord, Who is Supreme and praiseworthy, Whose glory is Unique, Who is cognition-incarnate and Lightt-incarnate, Whose Splendour is unmanifested and Who is Unattached.161.

648.g: ਗੁਰ ਬਾਝ ਯੌ ਨ ਹੋਵੈ ਉਧਾਰ ॥
648.t: gur baajh yau na hovai udhaar ||
648.e: In this way, he practiced Yoga in various ways, but the salvation is not attained without the Guru

648.g: ਤਬ ਪਰੇ ਦਤ ਕੇ ਚਰਨਿ ਆਨਿ ॥
648.t: tab pare dhat ke charan aan ||

648.g: ਕਹਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਜੋਗ ਕੇ ਗੁਰ ਬਿਧਾਨ ॥੧੬੨॥
648.t: keh dheh jog ke gur bidhaan ||162||
648.e: Then they all fell at the feet of Dutt and requested him to instruct them in the method of Yoga.162.
Those who were subjected to tonsure ceremony in water, all those princes (boys) are under your refuge
Those who were initiated as disciples in the mountains, they were known by the name Girl.163.
He wandered in the cities and made Barat, Parath, Puri etc. as Sannyasis.164.

648.g: ਪਰਬਤਿ ਸੁ ਨਾਮ ਲੈ ਤਾਹਿ ਦੀਨ ॥
648.t: parabat su naam lai taeh dheen ||

648.g: ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਉਚਰਿ ਕਰਿ ਪੰਚ ਨਾਮ ॥
648.t: eeh bhaat uchar kar pa(n)ch naam ||

648.e: Those who were made disciples on the mountains, they were named ‘Parvat’ and in this way uttering the five names, Dutt took rest.165.

648.g: ਸਾਗਰਿ ਸੁ ਨਾਮ ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਬੀਨ ॥
648.t: saagar su naam tin ke prabeen ||
648.e: Those were initiated as disciples in the sea, they were named as ‘Sagar’ and
Those who were made disciples on the bank of river Sarasvati, they were named as ‘Sarasvati’.166.

648.g: ਤੀਰਥਿ ਸੁ ਨਾਮ ਤਿਨ ਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਬੀਨ ॥
648.t: teerath su naam tin ko prabeen ||
648.e: Those who were made were made disciples at pilgrim-stations, those skilful disciples were named as ‘Tirath’

648.g: ਜਿਨ ਚਰਨ ਦਤ ਕੇ ਗਹੇ ਆਨਿ ॥
648.t: jin charan dhat ke gahe aan ||

648.e: Those who came and caught the feet of Dutt, they all became the treasure of learning.167.

648.g: ਇਮਿ ਕਰਤ ਸਿਖ ਜਹ ਤਹ ਬਿਹਾਰਿ ॥
648.t: eim karat sikh jeh teh bihaar ||

648.e: In this way, wherever the disciples lived and wherever any disciple did anything,

648.g: ਤਹ ਤਹੀ ਸਿਖ ਜੋ ਕੀਨ ਜਾਇ ॥
648.t: teh tahee sikh jo keen jai ||

648.g: ਆਸ੍ਰਮਿ ਸੁ ਨਾਮ ਕੋ ਤਿਨ ਸੁਹਾਇ ॥੧੬੮॥
648.t: aasram su naam ko tin suhai ||168||
648.e: The hermitage was established there in his name.

648.g: ਤਹ ਤਹ ਸੁ ਕੀਨ ਜੇ ਸਿਖ ਜਾਇ ॥
648.t: teh teh su keen je sikh jai ||

648.e: That fearless Purusha Dutt made several disciples in the Aranyaks (forets), they were named `Aranayaks`.169.

648.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਦਤ ਮਹਾਤਮੇ ਅਨਭਉ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸੇ ਦਸ ਨਾਮ ਧ੍ਰਯਾਯ ਸੰਪੂਰਣ ॥
648.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the dhat mahaatame anabhau prakaase dhas naam dhrayaay sa(n)pooran ||
648.e: End of the chapter entitled "The ten names of Cognition-Incarnate disciples of th sage Dutt" in Bachittar Natak.
(Now begins the description of making mind as the Second Guru) PAADHARI STANZA
The glory of that king of Sannyasis was indescribable and the impact of his long arms was enormous

648.g: ਜਹ ਜਹ ਬਿਹਾਰ ਮੁਨਿ ਕਰਤ ਦਤ ॥
648.t: jeh jeh bihaar mun karat dhat ||

648.e: Wherever the sage Dutt went, there also the effulgence glistened and the pure intellect extended.170.

648.g: ਤਜਿ ਗਰਬ ਪਾਨ ਲਾਗੇ ਸੁ ਢਾਲ ॥
648.t: taj garab paan laage su ddaal ||
648.e: The kings of the countries far and near, forsaking their pride came and fell at his feet
They abandoned all the false measures and with determination, made Dutt, the king ofYogis, as their base.171.

648.g: ਤਜਿ ਸਰਬ ਆਸ ਇਕ ਆਸ ਚਿਤ ॥
648.t: taj sarab aas ik aas chit ||

648.e: Relinquishing all other desires, only one desire of meeting the Lord remained in their heart and
The mind of all of them was supremely pure and without any vice to whichever country Dutt went, the king of that place fell t his feet.172.
DOHRA

648.g: ਗਵਨ ਕਰਤ ਜਿਹਾਂ ਜਿਹਾਂ ਦਿਸਾ ਮੁਨਿ ਮਨ ਦਤ ਅਪਾਰ ॥
648.t: gavan karat jihaa(n) jihaa(n) dhisaa mun man dhat apaar ||

648.g: ਸੰਗਿ ਚਲਤ ਉਠਿ ਸਬ ਪ੍ਰਜਾ ਤਜ ਘਰ ਬਾਰ ਪਹਾਰ ॥੧੭੩॥
648.t: sa(n)g chalat uTh sab prajaa taj ghar baar pahaar ||173||
648.e: To whichever direction, Dutt went, the subjects of those places left their homes and accompanied him.173.
CHAUPAI

648.g: ਊਚ ਨੀਚ ਸਬ ਹੀ ਸੰਗਿ ਭਏ ॥
648.t: uooch neech sab hee sa(n)g bhe ||
648.e: To whichever country, the great sage Dutt went, all the elders and minors accompanied him
Whereas he was a Yogi, he was also extremely beautiful, then who would there be without allurement.174.
Wherever the impact of his Yoga and Sannyas reached, the people left all their paraphernalia and became unattached
No such place was visible, where there was not the impact of Yoga and Sannyas.175.

649.g: ਇਤਿ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੂਸਰ ਠਹਰਾਇਆ ਸਮਾਪਤੰ ॥੨॥
649.t: eit man noo(n) guroo dhoosar Thaharaiaa samaapata(n) ||2||
649.e: End of the adoption of Man (mind) as the second Guru.
Now begins the description of adopting Spider as the Third Guru
CHAUPAI

649.g: ਅਬ ਸੁਨ ਲੇਹੁ ਕਹੋ ਇਹ ਬਾਤਾ ॥
649.t: ab sun leh kaho ieh baataa ||
649.e: Listen not to the manner in which Dutt adopted twenty-four Gurus
He saw a spider and reflected in his mind.176.
Contemplating in his mind, he said this, “I consider it my third Guru
When the thread of love will extend, then only the Lord (Nath Niranjan-the unmanifested Brahman) will be realized.”177.

649.g: ਏਕ ਛਾਡਿ ਕੈ ਅਨਤ ਨ ਧਾਵੈ ॥
649.t: ek chhaadd kai anat na dhaavai ||

649.g: ਤਬ ਹੀ ਪਰਮ ਤਤੁ ਕੋ ਪਾਵੈ ॥੧੭੮॥
649.t: tab hee param tat ko paavai ||178||
649.e: When the self will be visualized and within oneself the soul-Guru will be touched and the mind will not go anywhere else, leaving the ONE, then only the Supreme Essence will be realized.178.

649.g: ਆਨ ਭਾਵ ਕੋ ਭਾਵ ਨੇ ਪੇਖੈ ॥
649.t: aan bhaav ko bhaav ne pekhai ||

649.g: ਏਕ ਆਸ ਤਜਿ ਅਨਤ ਨ ਧਾਵੈ ॥
649.t: ek aas taj anat na dhaavai ||

649.e: When the form of one will be considered and seen as One and no other thought will come into the mind and keeping one objective before oneself, the mind will not run anywhere else, then the Lord (Nath Niranjan---the unmanifested Brahman).179.

649.g: ਏਕ ਛਾਡਿ ਰਸ ਨੇਕ ਨ ਮਾਚੈ ॥
649.t: ek chhaadd ras nek na maachai ||

649.e: When the merger will be in only one and the mind will not be obsurbed in anyone else accept the ONE and meditate only on the supreme esselce, then it will realise the lord ( Nath Niranjan-the Unmanifasted brahman) 180
Accepting the spider as the third Guru, the glorious Dutt moved further

649.g: ਤਾ ਕਰ ਭਾਵ ਹ੍ਰਿਦੇ ਮਹਿ ਲੀਨਾ ॥
649.t: taa kar bhaav hiradhe meh leenaa ||

649.e: Getting greatly pleased, he moved forward, adopting their connotation in his heart.181.
End of the adoption of Spider as the third Guru.
Now begins the description of the fourth Guru Crane.
CHAUPAI
When Dutt moved forward, then after seeing the swarm of fish, he saw towards the meditating crane
His limbs were extremely white and seeing him all the silence-observing creatures felt shy.182.
The meditation that was being observed by the crane, made his name shameful because of his meditativeness for fish

649.g: ਭਾਵ ਤਾਸ ਕੋ ਮੁਨਿ ਮਨ ਭਾਵੈ ॥੧੮੩॥
649.t: bhaav taas ko mun man bhaavai ||183||
649.e: He was observing meditation very nicely and with his silence, he was pleasing the sages.183.

649.g: ਤਬ ਹੀ ਪਰਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਕਹੁ ਪਈਐ ॥
649.t: tab hee param purakh kahu pieeaai ||
649.e: If such a medittativeness is observed for the sake of that Lord, He is realized in that way
Seeing the crane, Dutt was allured towards him and he accepted him as his fourth Guru.184.
End of the description of the adoption of Crane as the fourth Guru.
Now begins the description of the fifth Guru Tom Cat
CHAUPAI
Dutt, the king of sages, having matted locks on his head, moved further

650.e: There he saw a Tom Cat, whom he continued ot scan attentively.185.
Seeing his miditativeness for the rats, even the great hermits felt shy
If such meditativeness is observed for the sake of the Lord, only then that unmanifested Brahman can be realized.186.
I shall consider him my fifth Guru, such a thought came to the mind of Dutt, the king of sages
He, who will meditate in such a way, he will assuredly realise the Lord.187.
End of the description of the adoption of Tom Cat as the fifth Guru.
Now begins the description of the Cotton Carder as the Guru
CHAUPAI
Leaving all other desires and keeping only one thought in his mind, Dutt, the king of Yogis moved further

650.g: ਐਸ ਭਾਤਿ ਮਨ ਸੌ ਮੁਨਿ ਕਹਾ ॥੧੮੮॥
650.t: aais bhaat man sau mun kahaa ||188||
650.e: There he saw a carder carding cotton and said thus in hiss mind188

650.g: ਭੂਪ ਸੈਨ ਇਹ ਜਾਤ ਨ ਲਹੀ ॥
650.t: bhoop sain ieh jaat na lahee ||

650.e: “This man has not seen all the army passing in front of him and his neck remained bowed

650.g: ਤਾ ਕੌ ਨੈਕੁ ਖਬਰ ਨਹੀ ਭਈ ॥੧੮੯॥
650.t: taa kau naik khabar nahee bhiee ||189||
650.e: The whole army went on this path, but he was not conscious of that.”189.
While carding the cotton, he did not look back and this lowly person kept his neck bowed
Seeing him, Dutt smiled in his mind and said, “I accept him as my sixth Guru.”190.

650.g: ਰੂਮ ਹੇਤ ਇਹ ਜਿਮ ਚਿਤੁ ਲਾਯੋ ॥
650.t: room het ieh jim chit laayo ||

650.g: ਸੈਨ ਗਈ ਪਰੁ ਸਿਰ ਨ ਉਚਾਯੋ ॥
650.t: sain giee par sir na uchaayo ||

650.e: The way in which he absorbed his mind in cotton and the army passed away and he did not raise his head, in the same way, when the Lord will be loved, then that ancient Purusha i.e. the Lord will be realized.191.

650.g: ਇਤਿ ਰੂਈ ਧੁਨਖਤਾ ਪੇਾਂਜਾ ਖਸਟਮੋ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਮਾਪਤੰ ॥੬॥
650.t: eit rooiee dhunakhataa peaa(n)jaa khasaTamo guroo samaapata(n) ||6||
650.e: End of the description of the adoption of Carder as the sixth Guru.
Now begins the description of Fisherman as the Seventh Guru
CHAUPI
That great ascetic Dutt, of the pure mind moved further

650.g: ਲਏ ਜਾਰ ਕਰਿ ਜਾਤ ਨ ਕਹਾ ॥੧੯੨॥
650.t: le jaar kar jaat na kahaa ||192||
650.e: There he saw a Fisherman going with his net.192.
He was holding his lance in one of his hands and was carrying the net on one shoulder

650.g: ਜਾਨੁਕ ਵਾ ਕੇ ਮਧ ਨ ਸਾਸਾ ॥੧੯੩॥
650.t: jaanuk vaa ke madh na saasaa ||193||
650.e: He was standing there for the sake of the fish in such a way as if his body had become breathless.193.
He was standing with the desire of catching one fish in such a way as if someone standing with patience and detached from all his paraphernalia

650.g: ਇਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਨੇਹ ਨਾਥ ਸੌ ਲਈਐ ॥
650.t: eeh bidh neh naath sau lieeaai ||

650.g: ਤਬ ਹੀ ਪੂਰਨ ਪੁਰਖ ਕਹ ਪਈਐ ॥੧੯੪॥
650.t: tab hee pooran purakh keh pieeaai ||194||
650.e: Dutt thought that if such a love was observed for the sake of the Lord, then that perfect Purusha i.e. the Lo
End of the description of the adoption of Fisherman as the seventh Guru.
Now begins the description of he adopt of Maid-servant as the Eighth Guru
CHAUPAI
When the sage Dutt reached the abode of Daksha Prajapati, he was greatly pleased alongwith his army

651.e: There the sage Dutt saw a maid-servant, who, being intoxicated, was rubbing the sandalwood.195.

651.g: ਏਕ ਚਿਤ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਆਪਨ ਘਰ ਮਾ ॥
651.t: ek chit havai aapan ghar maa ||
651.e: That lady of good conduct was grinding sandalwood single-mindedly in her home
She had concentrated her mind and seeing her even the portrait was getting shy.196.
Dutt went that way alongwith the Sannyasis in order to meet her, but she did not raise her head and see whether some king or some pauper was going.197.

651.g: ਜਾ ਕੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਨਾਥ ਸੰਗਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥੧੯੮॥
651.t: jaa kee preet naath sa(n)g laagee ||198||
651.e: Seeing her impact, Dutt accepted her as the eighth Guru and said, “Blessed is this maid-servant, who is absorbed in love with that Lord.”198.
When such a love is observed with that Lord, then He is realized

651.g: ਬਿਨੁ ਚਿਤਿ ਦੀਨ ਹਾਥਿ ਨਹੀ ਆਵੈ ॥
651.t: bin chit dheen haath nahee aavai ||

651.e: He is not achieved without bringing humility in the mind and all the four Vedas tell this.199.
End of the description of the adoption of Maid-servant as the eighth Guru.
Now begins the description of the adoption of the Trader as the Ninth Guru.
CHAUPAI
Then taking his disciples alongwith him, Dutt, the Yogi with matted locks, moved further
When, passing through the forests, cities and mountains, they went forward, there they saw a trader coming.200.
His coffers were full of money and he was moving with a good deal of merchandise, he had many bags full of cloves and no one could enumerate them.201.

651.g: ਰਾਤਿ ਦਿਵਸ ਤਿਨ ਦ੍ਰਬ ਕੀ ਆਸਾ ॥
651.t: raat dhivas tin dhrab kee aasaa ||

651.e: He desired for more wealth day and night and he had left his home for selling his articles
He had no other desire except his trade.202.

651.g: ਛਾਹ ਧੂਪ ਕੋ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਨ ਮਾਨੈ ॥
651.t: chhaeh dhoop ko traas na maanai ||

651.g: ਰਾਤਿ ਅਉ ਦਿਵਸ ਗਵਨ ਈ ਠਾਨੈ ॥
651.t: raat aau dhivas gavan iee Thaanai ||
651.e: He had no fear of sunshine and shade and he was always musing of moving forward day and night

651.g: ਪਾਪ ਪੁੰਨ ਕੀ ਅਉਰ ਨ ਬਾਤਾ ॥
651.t: paap pu(n)n kee aaur na baataa ||

651.e: He had no concern for virtue and vice and he was only absorbed in the relish of trade.203.

651.g: ਤਾ ਕਹ ਦੇਖਿ ਦਤ ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤੂ ॥
651.t: taa keh dhekh dhat har bhagatoo ||

651.g: ਜਾ ਕਰ ਰੂਪ ਜਗਤਿ ਜਗ ਮਗਤੂ ॥
651.t: jaa kar roop jagat jag magatoo ||

651.e: Seeing him, Dutt, the devotee of the Lord, whose person was revered throughout the world, thought in his mind that in such manner the Lord be remembered, only then that Supreme Purusha i.e. the Lord can be realized.204.
End of the description of the adoption of he Trader as the Ninth Guru.
Now begins the description of the adoption of the Lady-Gardener as the Tenth Guru.
CHAUPAI
The sage forsaking all desires and observing great silence moved further in a state of apathy
He was a great knower of the Essence, a silence-observer and a lover of the Lord.205.

652.g: ਮਹਾ ਮੁਨੀ ਹਰਿ ਕੇ ਰਸ ਪਾਗੀ ॥
652.t: mahaa munee har ke ras paagee ||
652.e: He was a great sage, absorbed in the love of he Supreme Purusha i.e. the Lord

652.g: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭਗਤ ਖਟ ਗੁਨ ਰਸ ਲੀਨਾ ॥
652.t: braham bhagat khaT gun ras leenaa ||

652.g: ਏਕ ਨਾਮ ਕੇ ਰਸ ਸਉ ਭੀਨਾ ॥੨੦੬॥
652.t: ek naam ke ras sau bheenaa ||206||
652.e: He was a devotee of Brahman, the knower of he philosophies of the six Shastras and the one who remained absorbed in the Name of the Lord.206.

652.g: ਸੁਰ ਨਰ ਮੁਨਿ ਸਭ ਕੋ ਮਨ ਮੋਹੈ ॥
652.t: sur nar mun sabh ko man mohai ||
652.e: The white body of the great sage was alluring the gods, men and sages

652.g: ਜਹ ਜਹ ਜਾਇ ਦਤ ਸੁਭ ਕਰਮਾ ॥
652.t: jeh jeh jai dhat subh karamaa ||

652.e: Wherever Dutt, the sage performing good actions went, all those who resided there, achieved passivity.207.

652.g: ਰਾਮ ਭਗਤਿ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਉਠਿ ਲਾਗੈ ॥
652.t: raam bhagat sabh hee uTh laagai ||
652.e: Seeing him, all the illusions, attachment etc, fled away and all were absorbed in the devotion of the Lord

652.g: ਨਿਸਿ ਦਿਨ ਰਹੈ ਏਕ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਈ ॥੨੦੮॥
652.t: nis dhin rahai ek liv laiee ||208||
652.e: The sins and ailments of all were destroyed, all remained engrossed in the meditation of one Lord.208.
The sage met a lady-gardener there, who was shouting continuously
The sage feeling the notion of her shouts in his mind, adopted her the tenth Guru.209.
He, who will serve the Lord, he will destroy the ego, which is the origin of the world

652.g: ਸਤਿ ਬੋਲਿ ਯਾ ਕੀ ਹਮ ਮਾਨੀ ॥
652.t: sat bol yaa kee ham maanee ||

652.e: Who will actually be awakened from the sleep of maya, he will enshrine the Lord the sleep of maya, he will enshrine the Lord in hi heart the sage accepted the voice of the lady-gardener as true and as the power of kindling the knowledge of Yoga.210.
End of the description of the adoption of the Lady-Gradener as the Tenth Guru.
Now begins the description of the adoption of Surath as the Eleventh Guru
CHAUPAI
Then the sage Dutt, practising all the arts of Yoga, moved forward
His glory was infinite and he seemed to be the second God.211.

652.g: ਸਭ ਹੀ ਕਲਾ ਜੋਗ ਕੀ ਸਾਧੀ ॥
652.t: sabh hee kalaa jog kee saadhee ||

652.e: That great adept and the silence-observing purusha practiced all the skill of Yoga
Seeing his extreme glory and impact, the seat of Indra also trembled.212.
MADHUBHAAR STANZA BY THY GRACE
The generous sage, full of innumerable attributes, was absorbed in the devotion of the Lord and was under the submission of the Lord.213.
Forsaking the royal enjoyments that king of Yogis had adopted Sannyas and Yoga for the devotion and desire of meeting the Lord.214.
The beauty of the face of that perfect incarnation was enormous
He was sharp like dagger and was also skilful in many prominent sciences.215.
That charming sage had unique greatness, unlimited glory and generous mind.216.

653.e: He was a god for Sannyasis and for the virtuous people he was mysterious, unmanifested and of unparalleled greatness.217.
His temperament was auspicious, the impact marvelous and the greatness unlimited.218.
There was a king name Surath there who was attached with his assets and society who worshipped Chandi uninterruptedly.219.
The king, who was extremely powerful and had complete control of his kingdom, was skilful in all the sciences and was under the submission of the goddess.220.
He served the goddess Bhavani night and day and remained unattached with only one desire in his mind.221.
He used to worship Durga always in various ways and made offerings.222.
That king was enromusly praiseworthy, treasure of virtues and had such a pure body that on seeing him, even the ganges felt shy.223.
Seeing him, Dutt became extremely pure in intellect and completely lustrous.224.
Seeing his limbs, even Ganges became shy, because he was enormously praiseworthy and a treasure of virtues.225.
The sage saw that he was bright like light, ever unattached and a king of Sannyasis with marvelous temperament.226.
Dutt saw his serving nature and he was extremely pleased in his mind.227.

654.e: He seemed to Dutt as a king of supreme intellect, bedecked with all the accomplishments.228.
That king was unconquerable, illustrious, elegant and respectful for all religions.229.
That long-armed king was virtuous and cared for all his subjects.230.
That long-armed king was a great Sovereign, a great Yogi and a monarch of Dharma.231.
That king of kings resembled the figure of Rudra
He was free from anxieties and remained absorbed in Yoga.232.
MADHUBHAAR STANZA
Seeing him, Dutt, the king of Yogis, who was in the garb of a Rawal, and who was theking of Sannyasis, and respectable for all, he was allured towards him.233.
He saw him like pure moon and found him that his actions were immaculate and in accordance with Yoga.234.
That Sannyasi king was the destroyer of impiety, he went everywhere in his kingdom and was the abode of Dharma.235.
His Yoga was indestructible and wearing his loin-cloth, he moved everywhere in his kingdom.236.
His action and duties were illustrious and not liable to decay
He was the commander of all and was like a stream of Sannyas.237.
He was the destroyer of ignorance, skilful in sciences, the destroyer of impiety and a devotee of Sannyasis.238.
He was the servitor of the Lord, he was felt everywhere by his subjects, a king in Sannyas and he was embellished with all learnings.239.
He was the destroyer of impiety, a devotee of the path of Sannyas, of Jivan-mukta (redeemed while living) and was skilful in all learnings.240.
He was absorbed in good deeds, an unattached Yogi
He was like unmanifested Dharma devoid of Yoga his limbs were healthy.241.
He was never in ire, even slightly
No vice touched him and he ever flowed like the river of Dharma.242.
He adopted Sannyas and was the supreme authority of Yoga
He was the devotee of Brahman, the originator of the world.243.
That king wearing matted locks, had abandoned all the stores of materials
And he wore waist-cloth.24.
He performed actions of Sannyas and adopted Rawal religion
He always remained in bliss and was the destroyer of lust etc.245.
The tabors were being played, hearing which all the sins had fled away

655.e: His body had been smeared with ashes and all were getting allured towards him.246.
He wore loin-cloth and spoke occasionally
He was the adopter of piety and destroyer of sin.247.
The horn was being blown and the sins were running away
The orders were given there that the religious texts be read.248.
In that holy country, assuming the religious garb, the prayer was being held, thinking of that one wearing the lion-cloth as effulgence.249.
He was devoid of misfortune and attached to Sannyas
He was supremely immaculate and friend of all.250.
He was absorbed in yoga, having indescribable form
He was a Sannyasi king.251.
He was the hero of heroes and practiser of all the disciplines
He was a Sannyasi, performing underrfiled actions.252.
He was like that Lord, who is imperishable, and just, the remover of injustice.253.
He was the destroyer of Karmas, the servitor of all, everywhere, unattached and glorious.254.
He was the goer to all the places, the remover of sins, beyond all ailments and the one who remained a pure Yogi.255.

655.g: ਇਤਿ ਸੁਰਥ ਰਾਜਾ ਯਾਰ੍ਰਹਮੋ ਗੁਰੂ ਬਰਨਨੰ ਸਮਾਪਤੰ ॥੧੧॥
655.t: eit surath raajaa yaarrahamo guroo baranana(n) samaapata(n) ||11||
655.e: End of the description of the Elventh Guru, the king Surath.
Now begins the description of the adoption of a Girl as the Twelfth Guru
RASAAVAL STANZA
Then Dutt moved further seeing him, the sins fled away
The thunderous sound of the songs continued like the song of the peacocks in the forest.256.
The horns were sounded in the sky and the sins of the earth ran away

656.e: He made offerings to the goddess and there was the discussion about the four Vedas.257.
Recitation of all the Shrutis was performed for that Sannyas at the suitable place
The great practices of Yoga were held and there was atmosphere of detachment.258.
There was discussion of six Shastras and the recitation of the Vedas and the Sannyasis observed great silence.259.
Then Dutt move still further and seeing him, the sins fled away
There he was a girl, making the three worlds blessed ones.260.
This authority of Dharma and the great celibate saw a doll in her hand.261.
She was playing with it and she loved it so much that she drank water and continued to play with it.262.
All those silence-observing Yogis went to that side and they saw her, but that girl did not see them and did not stop playing,263.
The teeth the girl were like the garland of flowers
She was absorbed in frolic like the creeper clinging to the tree.264.
Then Dutt, seeing her, eulogized her and accepting her as his Guru, he was absorbed in his great mantra.265.
He accepted her as his Guru and in this way, adopted the mantra
In this way, Dutt adopted his twelfth Guru.266.
The beauty of that girl was unique and marvelous
She appeared to be a store of intellect the sage saw her.267.
Then he saw her again and again in various ways and accepted her quality in his mind and body.268.

657.e: After adopting he as his Guru, he offered her approbation and then moved further like the flame of fire.269.

657.g: ਇਤਿ ਦੁਆਦਸ ਗੁਰੂ ਲੜਕੀ ਗੁਡੀ ਖੇਡਤੀ ਸਮਾਪਤੰ ॥੧੨॥
657.t: eit dhuaadhas guroo laRakee guddee kheddatee samaapata(n) ||12||
657.e: End of the description of the adoption of a girl playing with her doll as his twelfth Guru.
Now begins the description of an Orderly as the Thirteenth Guru
TOMAR STANZA
Then the great Dutt, who was a treasure in eighteen sciences and
Had a fine physique, used to remember the Name of the Lord at day-dawn.270.
Seeing his bright and blemishless limbs, the waves of Ganges felt shy
Looking at his marvelous figure, the kings became shyful.271.
He saw an orderly, who had many qualities, even at midnight, he was standing at the gate
In this way, during the rainfall, he stood firmly without caring for the rain.272.
Dutt saw that Vikram-like individual full of qualities at midnight and he also saw that it was greatly pleased in his mind.273.
He seemed standing like a golden statue single-mindedly
Seeing his concerntration, Dutt was greatly pleased in his mind. 274.
He thought that this man was not caring for cold or hot weather and there is no desire of some shade in his mind he was standing on one foot without even slightly turning his limbs.275.
Dutt went near him and looked down upon him, learning. a bit
He was standing detachedly in that desolate atmosphere at midnighgt.276.
It was raining and the water was spreading on the earth
All the beings of the world ran away in fear.277.
This orderly was standing at the gate of the king like this and was repeating the name of the goddess Gauri-Parvati in his mind
He was standing on one foot, without even slightly turning his limbs.278.
A dreadful sword was shining in his hand like a flame of fire and
He was standing solemnly without seeming to have friendliness for anyone.279.
He was not even raising his foot slightly and he was in the posture of playing trick in many ways

658.e: He was a devotee of the king dyed unswervingly in the love of the Lord.280.
Because of heavy rain, all the animals and birds were going from various directions to their homes in order to take shelter.281.
He was standing detachedly on one foot and taking his sword in one of his hands, he was looking extremely lustrous.282.
There was no other idea in his mind except his master and he was standing on one foot like a column standing in the battlefield.283.
Wherever he placed his foot, he firmly fixed it there
At his place, he was not getting wet and seeing him the sage Dutt kept silent.284.
The sage saw him and he seemed to him like a part of a blemishless moon
The sage abandoning his shyness and accepting him as his Guru, fell at his feet.285.
The blemishless Dutt, accepting him as his Guru, absorbed his mind in his love and in this way adopted him as the Thirteenth Guru.286.
End of the description of the Thirteenth Guru.
Now begins the description of the Fourteenth Guru
RASAAVAL STANZA
Dutt moved further, seeing whom the sins ran away whosover saw him he saw him as his Guru.287.
Seeing that lustrous and glorious sage, the sins ran away and if there was anyone like the grat Shiva, it was only Dutt.288.
Whosoever saw him, saw the god of love in him
He considered him like Brahman and destroyed his duality.289.
All the women were allured by that great and illustrious Dutt and
They were not anxious about garments and ornaments.290.
They were running like the boat moving forward in the stream
None of the young, old and minors remained behind.291.

659.e: The sage, the authority on Dharma, saw a women,
Who looked like Parvati or Indrani.292.
She was looking like the Lakshmi of the kings
She was glorious like the beautiful damsels of Madra Desha.293.
She might be Sita, or the prowess of the kings, or the chief queen of some king or the moving figure behind Ram.294.
She might be Yamuna, united with the glory of the god of love
She was like the goddess of the goddesses and the heavenly damsel of the demons.295.
She was looking like Savitri, Gayatri, the supreme goddess amongst the goddesses and the chief queen amongst the queens.296.
She was a princess skilful in mantras and tantras and seemed like Hansani (a female swan).297.
Looking like the heated gold in fife, she seemed like Shachi, the wife of Indra
It seemed that Brahma had himself created her.298.
She was like Lakshmi and supremely glorious
She was pure like the sunrays.299.
She was mercurial like the sexual arts
She was looking splendid like Rajeshwari or was like a specially like Gauri-Parvati.301.
She was like the beloved queen of Ram and glorious like Gauri-Parvati.301.
She was superb amongst the arts of kingdom and looked like the youthful spring and seemed like the rosary of Raginis (the female musical modes).302.

660.e: She looked like Megh-Malhar, or Gauri Dhamar or the daughter of Hindol, descending from the sky.303.
That fortunate woman was engrossed in arts and absorbed in Shastras she was the devotee of her Lord.304.
She was looking like Rambha, Shachi, the special creation of Brahma, Gandharva woman or the daughter of Vidyadhars.305.
She, seemed swinging like Rambha, Urvashi and Shachi.306.
She looked like a Gandharva woman, like the daughter of Vidyadhars or the queen combined with royal glory.307.
She seemed like a princes or like Parvati, the beloved of Rudra and seemed like pure light-incarnate.308.
She was a fascinating beautiful woman
She appeared like a mercurial woman, portrait-like and glorious.309.
She was looking beautiful like the rivers, Ganges, Yamuna and Sarasvati or the city of Dwarka.310.
She was looking like Yamuna, Kankala, Kameshwari and Indrani.311.
She was the destroyer of fear, a pillar-like damsel, a spring-lady or an authoritative woman.312.
She was illustrious, pure and like enlightning effulgence
She was a glorious fairy.313.
She was glorious like the moon and the sun
She was supremely immaculate and radiant.314,
She was a Naga-girl and the destroyer of all sufferings
She was mercurial and glorious.315.
She was Sarasvati-incarnate, destroyer of anger, having long hair
She was like the flash of lighning.316.
She was a Kshatriya woman, a canopied queen and a glorious and beautiful damsel like the canopy.317.
Her doe-like eyes worked like arrows and she was pretty like the radiance of lotus or the moonbeams.318.
She was a Gandharva woman or a Vidyadhar girl or the spring like lady or a beloved of all the people.319.
She was the beloved of Yadveshwar (Krishna) and a charming woman like Draupadi
She appeared like the chief queen swinging in a swing.320.
She, being studded with gold, seemed to be descending from the sky

661.e: She was like a portrait of gold with the golden effulgence.321.
She was lotus-eyed with supreme radiance
She was a heroine with moon-like temperament spreading coolness.322.
She was radiant like the queen of Nagas
Her eyes were like those of a doe or lotus.323.
She was a unique one with infinite radiance
Her unblemished beauty was the king of all the kings.324.
MOHANI STANZA
There was radiant glory on the face of that youthful woman
Her eyes were like a doe and the speech like a nightingale she was mercurial, youth and moon-faced.325.
Her laughter was like lightning amongst the clouds and her nostril was extremely glorious
She was wearing. Pretty necklaces and doe-eyed one had embellished her wrist nicely.326.
That woman of elephant-gait was like a fascinating heavenly damsel and that sweetly smiling lady uttered very sweet words
Seeing her pure diamond necklaces, the lightning was feeling shy.327.
She was firm in her religion and performed good actions
She appeared as the remover of suffering in the way as if she was a stream of piety there was brilliance on her face and her body was completely healthy.328.
Dutt saw that beautiful and mercurial woman, who according to her actions was observing Sati Dharma (the conduct of truth)
She was the remover of suffering and was loved by his beloved she composed and uttered the poetic stanxas.329.
She was fascinating like the heavenly damsels like Rambha, Urvashi, Mohinin etc. and these heavely damsels, seeing her, bowed their faces and feeling shy, they went back to their homes.330.
The beautiful ladies like Ganddharva women, goddesses, Girja, Gayatri, Mandoddari, Savitri, Shachi etc. seeing her glory felt shy.331.
The Naga-girls,, the Yaksha women, the ghost, fiends, and Gana Women all were devoid of radiance before her.332.
That comely lady was the remover of all sufferings, giver of happiness and moon-faced

662.e: Even in the garb of Naga-girls, Gandharva-women, Yaksha-women and Indrani, she looked an extremely charming woman.333.
The eyes of that intoxicated youthful woman were tightened like the arrows and she was glistening with the radiance of youth
She had worn a rosary around her neck and the glory of her face seemed like the gleaming fire.334.
That queen of the earth was a canopied goddess and her eyes and words were pure
She was capable of alluring the demons, but she was the mine of learning and honour and lived unattached.335.
She was good, gentle and a lady of fine features she was giver of comfort she smiled mildly
She was the devotee of her beloved she remembered the Name of the Lord she was alluring and pleasing.336.
She was the devotee of her beloved and standing alone she was dyed in only one dye
She had no desire whatsoever and she was absorbed in the memory of her husband.337.
She neither slept nor ate food she was devotee of her beloved and a vow-observing lady
She was beautiful like Vasanti, Todi, Gauri, Bhupali, Sarang etc.338.
She was glorious like Hindol, Megh, Malhar, Jaijavanti, Gaur, Basant, Bairagi etc.339.
She was emotional like Sorath, Sarang, Bairai, Malhar, Hindol, Tailangi, Bhairavi and Deepak.340.
She was expert in all musical modes and the beauty itself was getting allured on seeing her
If I describe her glory of all types, then there will be an extension of another volume.341.
That great vow-observing Dutt saw vow-observing lady and touched her feet alongwith other hermits with matted locks

662.g: ਤਨ ਮਨ ਭਰਤਾ ਕਰ ਰਸ ਭੀਨਾ ॥
662.t: tan man bharataa kar ras bheenaa ||

662.g: ਚਵ ਦਸਵੋ ਤਾ ਕੌ ਗੁਰੁ ਕੀਨਾ ॥੩੪੨॥
662.t: chav dhasavo taa kau gur keenaa ||342||
662.e: He accepted that lady, being absorbed in the love of her husband with her body and mind, as his fourteenth Guru.342.

662.g: ਇਤਿ ਪ੍ਰਿਯ ਭਗਤ ਇਸਤ੍ਰੀ ਚਤੁਰਦਸਵਾ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਮਾਪਤੰ ॥੧੪॥
662.t: eit piray bhagat isatree chaturadhasavaa guroo samaapata(n) ||14||
662.e: End of the description of the adoption of the fully-devoted lady as his fourteenth Guru.
Now beings the description of the adoption of the Arrow-maker as his Fifteenth Guru
TOTAK STANZA
Adopting the fourteenth Guru, the sage Dutt, blowing his conch, moved further
After wandering through the East, West and North and observing silence, he moved towards the Southern direction.343.
There he saw a city of portraits, where there were temples everywhere

663.e: The king of that place had killed many deer and lions with his dagger.344.
The king took the four division of his army with him
The banners of the army were fluttering and the studded garments were worn by all the warriors the beauty of all of them was making the beauty of all other places shyful.345.
An arrow-maker was sitting there, and appeared to be lifeless
The small and big drums and the tabors etc. resounded.346.

663.g: ਦਲ ਨਾਥ ਲਏ ਬਹੁ ਸੰਗਿ ਦਲੰ ॥
663.t: dhal naath le bahu sa(n)g dhala(n) ||

663.e: The king was with his army and that army was rushing forth like the clouds of doomsday
The horses were neighing and the elephants were trumpeting hearing the roaring of the elephants, the clouds were feeling shy.347.
That army was moving peacefully, while felling the trees and drinking the water from the water-currents, seeing which all were getting allured.348.
The sun and the moon were frightened from that army and seeing that king, all other kings of the earth were feeling happy
Various kinds of musical instruments including the drums resounded.349.
Various kinds of colourful ornaments including Noopar and Kinkini looked splendid and there was the plastering of sandal on all the faces
All of them were moving an talking happily and were returning to their homes happily.350.
They were wiping the essences of rose and otto from their faces and there was comely antimony in their eyes
The pretty faces of al looked fine like ivory and even Ganas and Gandharvas were pleased to see them.351.
There were pretty necklaces around the necks of all and there were frontal marks of saffron on the foreheads of all

663.g: ਤਿਹ ਜਾਤ ਭਏ ਸਨ ਸੈਨ ਮਗੰ ॥੩੫੨॥
663.t: teh jaat bhe san sain maga(n) ||352||
663.e: This enormous army was moving on that path.352.

663.g: ਫਿਰਿ ਆਇ ਗਏ ਤਿਹ ਪੈਂਡ ਮੁਨੰ ॥
663.t: fir aai ge teh pai(n)dd muna(n) ||

663.g: ਸਿਰ ਨੀਚ ਮਨੋ ਲਿਖ ਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਧਰੰ ॥੩੫੩॥
663.t: sir neech mano likh chitr dhara(n) ||353||
663.e: The sage Dutt, blowing his conch reached on that path were he saw an arrow-maker with his bowed head, sitting like a portrait.353.

663.g: ਹਸਿ ਬੈਨ ਸੁ ਭਾਤਿ ਇਮੰ ਉਚਰੰ ॥
663.t: has bain su bhaat ima(n) uchara(n) ||

663.g: ਕਹੁ ਭੂਪ ਗਏ ਲੀਏ ਸੰਗਿ ਦਲੰ ॥
663.t: kahu bhoop ge le'ee sa(n)g dhala(n) ||

663.g: ਕਹਿਓ ਸੋ ਨ ਗੁਰੂ ਅਵਿਲੋਕ ਦ੍ਰਿਗੰ ॥੩੫੪॥
663.t: kahio so na guroo avilok dhiraga(n) ||354||
663.e: The great sage, seeing him, said this, “Where had the king gone with his army?” That arrow-maker replied, “I have not seen anyone with my eyes.”354.
The sage, seeing his stable mind, was wonder-struck
That complete and great ascetic never swerved that unattached person with vice-less mind was infinitely glorious.355.
Because of his complete austerity there glory on his face and he was like a vice-less celibate

664.e: His now was perfect and the body distinctive he was persistent, vow-observing and like the son of sage Atri.356.
The sage Dutt seeing his arrows and meditation, was greatly pleased

664.g: ਹਠ ਛਾਡਿ ਸਬੈ ਤਿਨ ਪਾਨ ਪਰੰ ॥੩੫੭॥
664.t: haTh chhaadd sabai tin paan para(n) ||357||
664.e: Adopting him his fifteenth Guru and leaving all his persistence he accepted him as his redeemer.357.

664.g: ਇਮਿ ਨਾਹ ਸੌ ਜੋ ਨਰ ਨੇਹ ਕਰੈ ॥
664.t: eim naeh sau jo nar neh karai ||

664.e: In this way, whosoever loves the Lord, he crosses this infinite ocean of existence

664.g: ਤਨ ਕੇ ਮਨ ਕੇ ਭ੍ਰਮ ਪਾਸਿ ਧਰੇ ॥
664.t: tan ke man ke bhram paas dhare ||

664.e: Removing the illusions of his body ad mind, Dutt fell down at the feet of his Fifteenth Guru in this way.358.
End of the description of the adoption of an Arrow-maker as the Fifteenth Guru.
Now begins the description of the adoption of a vulture as the Sixteenth Guru
TOTAK STANZA
The sage was alongwith his disciples having smeared his face with ashes and wearing the ochre-coloured clothes
He was singing the praises of the Lord with his mouth and was moving unattached with all kind of desires.359.
Various sounds were created with the mouth and the sage Dutt’s body was allied with many types of magnificence
He was moving silently in various countries far and near and was meditating on the Lord in his mind.360.

664.g: ਗ੍ਰਿਹਿ ਜਾਤ ਉਡੀ ਗਹਿ ਮਾਸੁ ਮੁਖੰ ॥
664.t: gireh jaat uddee geh maas mukha(n) ||
664.e: There he saw a vulture, who was holding a piece of flesh in his mouth and flying

664.g: ਲਖਿ ਕੈ ਪਲ ਚਾਵੰਡਿ ਚਾਰ ਚਲੀ ॥
664.t: lakh kai pal chaava(n)dd chaar chalee ||

664.g: ਤਿਹ ਤੇ ਅਤਿ ਪੁਸਟ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਥ ਬਲੀ ॥੩੬੧॥
664.t: teh te at pusaT pramaath balee ||361||
664.e: Seeing it, more powerful four vultures moved forward.361.

664.g: ਅਤਿ ਜੁਧੁ ਤਹੀ ਤਿਹੰ ਸੰਗ ਮੰਡੀ ॥
664.t: at judh tahee tiha(n) sa(n)g ma(n)ddee ||
664.e: They flew in the sky and there they began to fight with that vulture

664.g: ਤਜਿ ਮਾਸੁ ਚੜਾ ਉਡਿ ਆਪ ਚਲੀ ॥
664.t: taj maas chaRaa udd aap chalee ||

664.g: ਲਹਿ ਕੈ ਚਿਤ ਚਾਵੰਡਿ ਚਾਰ ਬਲੀ ॥੩੬੨॥
664.t: leh kai chit chaava(n)dd chaar balee ||362||
664.e: Whe dropped the pieced of flesh on seeing these powerful vultures and flew away.362.

664.g: ਤਜਿ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਭਾਈ ਥਿਰ ਭੂਮਿ ਥਲੰ ॥
664.t: taj traas bhaiee thir bhoom thala(n) ||
664.e: Seeing those four vulture, even the earth below became stable out of fear seeing them,

664.g: ਲਖਿ ਤਾਸੁ ਮਨੰ ਮੁਨਿ ਚਉਕ ਰਹ੍ਯੋ ॥
664.t: lakh taas mana(n) mun chauk rahayo ||

664.e: The sage was startled and adopted them (it) as the Sixteeth Guru.363.

664.g: ਕੋਊ ਐਸ ਤਜੈ ਜਬ ਸਰਬ ਧਨੰ ॥
664.t: kouoo aais tajai jab sarab dhana(n) ||

664.g: ਕਰਿ ਕੈ ਬਿਨੁ ਆਸ ਉਦਾਸ ਮਨੰ ॥
664.t: kar kai bin aas udhaas mana(n) ||
664.e: If anyone getting unattached with all the desires, forsakes all the assets

664.g: ਇਨ ਚੀਲਨ ਜਿਉ ਸ੍ਰੁਤ ਐਸ ਕਹੈ ॥੩੬੪॥
664.t: ein cheelan jiau srut aais kahai ||364||
664.e: Then only he can be considered an ascetic make his understanding like these vultures.364.
End of the description of the adoption of a Vulture as Sidxteenth Guru.
Now begins the description of the adoption of a Fishing Bird as the Seventeenth Guru
TOTAK STANZA
After adopting the vulture as the seventeenth Guru with unattached mind, Dutt proceeded again on his path
He was producing various types of sounds form his mouth and hearing the same, the gods, Gandharvas, men and women, all were getting pleased.365.
The persistent and ascetic sage reached near a stream, where he saw a flying bird named ‘Mahiggir’ near the jumping fish.366.

665.e: With concentrated mind, he was stable at one place in the sky and his limbs were extremely white and pretty

665.g: ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਰਹ੍ਯੋ ਗਡ ਮਛ ਮਨੰ ॥੩੬੭॥
665.t: eeh bhaat rahayo gadd machh mana(n) ||367||
665.e: His mind was absorbed in the fish and he was not seeing anyone else.367.

665.g: ਤਹਾ ਜਾਇ ਮਹਾ ਮੁਨਿ ਮਜਨ ਕੈ ॥
665.t: tahaa jai mahaa mun majan kai ||

665.g: ਉਠਿ ਕੈ ਹਰਿ ਧਿਆਨ ਲਗਾ ਸੁਚ ਕੈ ॥
665.t: auTh kai har dhiaan lagaa such kai ||
665.e: These the Guru went and took bath and getting up mediated on the Lord,

665.g: ਨ ਟਰੋ ਤਬ ਲੌ ਵਹ ਮਛ ਅਰੀ ॥
665.t: n Taro tab lau veh machh aree ||

665.g: ਰਥ ਸੂਰ ਅਥਿਓ ਨਹ ਡੀਠ ਟਰੀ ॥੩੬੮॥
665.t: rath soor athio neh ddeeTh Taree ||368||
665.e: But that enemy of the fish, concentrated his attention on the fish even till sunset.368.

665.g: ਰਥ ਭਾਨੁ ਹਟਿਓ ਨਹੀ ਧ੍ਯਾਨ ਛੁਟੰ ॥
665.t: rath bhaan haTio nahee dhayaan chhuTa(n) ||
665.e: He remained unwavered in the sky and did not even think of the sunset
Seeing him, the great sage observed silence and accepted him as the Seventeenth Guru.369.
End of the description of the adoption of the Fishing Bird as the Seventeenth Guru.
Now begins the description of the adoption of a Hunter as the Eighteenth Guru
TOTAK STANZA

665.g: ਉਠਿ ਜਾਤਿ ਭਏ ਬਨ ਮਧਿ ਮੁਨੰ ॥
665.t: auTh jaat bhe ban madh muna(n) ||
665.e: After taking bath and singing the praises of the Lord, the sage went into the forest,

665.g: ਰਥ ਸੂਰਜ ਕੇ ਪਗ ਬਾਜ ਫਸੈ ॥੩੭੦॥
665.t: rath sooraj ke pag baaj fasai ||370||
665.e: Where there were the trees of saal and tamaal and in the dense shade of those trees, the light of the sun could not reach.370.

665.g: ਰਿਖਿ ਜਾਤ ਭਏ ਹਿਤ ਜੋਗ ਜਹਾ ॥
665.t: rikh jaat bhe hit jog jahaa ||

665.e: There the sage a tank and also within the foliage he saw a hunter looking splendid like gold.371.
He had in his hand a bow and arrows of white colour, with which he had killed many deer

665.g: ਜਹ ਕਾਨਨ ਥੋ ਤਹ ਜਾਤ ਭਏ ॥੩੭੨॥
665.t: jeh kaanan tho teh jaat bhe ||372||
665.e: The sage came out from that side of the forest alongwith his people.372.

665.g: ਮੁਨਿ ਰਾਜ ਮਨੰ ਰਿਤੁ ਰਾਜ ਬਨੇ ॥
665.t: mun raaj mana(n) rit raaj bane ||
665.e: Many persons of the magnificence of gold,

665.g: ਰਿਖਿ ਸੰਗ ਸਖਾ ਨਿਸਿ ਬਹੁਤ ਲਏ ॥
665.t: rikh sa(n)g sakhaa nis bahut le ||

665.e: Accompanied the sage Dutt and they all saw that hunter.373.
Those sages raised thunderous sound an dreadful tumult at that place and

665.g: ਜਲ ਪੀਵਤ ਠਉਰ ਹੀ ਠਉਰ ਮੁਨੀ ॥
665.t: jal peevat Thaur hee Thaur munee ||

665.g: ਬਨ ਮਧਿ ਮਨੋ ਰਿਖ ਮਾਲ ਬਨੀ ॥੩੭੪॥
665.t: ban madh mano rikh maal banee ||374||
665.e: Scattering at various places they began to have their food and drink.374.
Those sages smeared their white bodies with ashes, practiced various postures and

665.g: ਰਿਖਿ ਸਰਬ ਚਹੂੰ ਚਕ ਦਾਸ ਥੀਏ ॥੩੭੫॥
665.t: rikh sarab chahoo(n) chak dhaas the'ee ||375||
665.e: Performed various Karmas like Neoli (Purging of intestines), while wandering in all the four directions.375.
They absorbed themselves in various practices completely without the element of lust

665.g: ਸਿਵ ਕੀ ਜਨੁ ਜੋਗ ਜਟਾ ਪ੍ਰਗਟੀ ॥੩੭੬॥
665.t: siv kee jan jog jaTaa pragaTee ||376||
665.e: Their matted locks appeared the manifestation of the matted locks of Shiva.376.

665.g: ਸਿਵ ਤੇ ਜਨੁ ਗੰਗ ਤਰੰਗ ਛੁਟੇ ॥
665.t: siv te jan ga(n)g tara(n)g chhuTe ||

665.g: ਇਹ ਹੁਇ ਜਨ ਜੋਗ ਜਟਾ ਪ੍ਰਗਟੇ ॥
665.t: eeh hui jan jog jaTaa pragaTe ||
665.e: Their Yogic matted locks waved like the waves of the Ganges emanating from Shiva

665.g: ਤਪ ਸਰਬ ਤਪੀਸਨ ਕੇ ਸਬ ਹੀ ॥
665.t: tap sarab tapeesan ke sab hee ||

665.g: ਮੁਨਿ ਜੇ ਸਬ ਛੀਨ ਲਏ ਤਬ ਹੀ ॥੩੭੭॥
665.t: mun je sab chheen le tab hee ||377||
665.e: They performed various kinds of austerities following the practices of earlier ascetics.377.

665.g: ਸਬ ਹੀ ਰਿਖਿ ਅੰਗਨ ਜਾਨ ਲਏ ॥
665.t: sab hee rikh a(n)gan jaan le ||
665.e: All the various practices which have been described in Shrutis (Vedas), they were all performed by these sages

666.g: ਰਿਖਿ ਮੋ ਗੁਨ ਤਾਸ ਸਬੈ ਦਮਕੈ ॥੩੭੮॥
666.t: rikh mo gun taas sabai dhamakai ||378||
666.e: All the qualities of these sages flashed like lightning amongst the clouds.378.

666.g: ਰਿਖਿ ਕੇ ਤਿਮ ਸੋਭਤ ਜੋਗ ਜਟਾ ॥
666.t: rikh ke tim sobhat jog jaTaa ||
666.e: The matted locks waved on the heads of the Yogis like the rays coming out of the sun

666.g: ਜਿਨ ਕੀ ਦੁਖ ਫਾਸ ਕਹੂੰ ਨ ਕਟੀ ॥
666.t: jin kee dhukh faas kahoo(n) na kaTee ||

666.e: Those whose suffering ended on seeing these sges.379.

666.g: ਨਰ ਜੋ ਨਹੀ ਨਰਕਨ ਤੇ ਨਿਵਰੈ ॥
666.t: nar jo nahee narakan te nivarai ||

666.e: Those men and women, who had been cast in hell, they were redeemed on seeing these sages

666.g: ਜਿਨ ਕੇ ਸਮਤਾ ਕਹੂੰ ਨਾਹਿ ਠਟੀ ॥
666.t: jin ke samataa kahoo(n) naeh ThaTee ||

666.g: ਰਿਖਿ ਪੂਜਿ ਘਟੀ ਸਬ ਪਾਪ ਘਟੀ ॥੩੮੦॥
666.t: rikh pooj ghaTee sab paap ghaTee ||380||
666.e: Those who had any sin within them, their sinful life endeed on worshipping these sages.380.
On this side, this hunter was sitting, on seeing whom, the animals used to run away

666.g: ਤਿਹ ਜਾਨ ਰਿਖੀਨ ਹੀ ਸਾਸ ਸਸ੍ਰਯੋ ॥
666.t: teh jaan rikheen hee saas sasrayo ||

666.g: ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਜਾਨ ਮੁਨੀ ਕਹੁ ਬਾਨ ਕਸ੍ਰਯੋ ॥੩੮੧॥
666.t: mirag jaan munee kahu baan kasrayo ||381||
666.e: He did not recognize the sage and condidering him a deer, he aimed his arrow at him.381.

666.g: ਸਰ ਪੇਖ ਸਬੈ ਤਿਹ ਸਾਧ ਕਹੈ ॥
666.t: sar pekh sabai teh saadh kahai ||

666.g: ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਹੋਇ ਨ ਰੇ ਮੁਨਿ ਰਾਜ ਇਹੈ ॥
666.t: mirag hoi na re mun raaj ihai ||
666.e: All the ascetics saw the arrow and also saw that the sage was seated like a deer

666.g: ਅਸ ਦੇਖਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੰ ਮੁਨਿ ਰਾਜ ਲਜੇ ॥੩੮੨॥
666.t: as dhekh dhiraRa(n) mun raaj laje ||382||
666.e: That person his bow and arrows from his hand and felt ashamed on seeing the resoluteness of the sage.382.

666.g: ਬਹੁਤੇ ਚਿਰ ਜਿਉ ਤਿਹ ਧ੍ਯਾਨ ਛੁਟਾ ॥
666.t: bahute chir jiau teh dhayaan chhuTaa ||

666.e: After a long time, when his attention was broken, then he saw the great sage with matted locks

666.g: ਕਸ ਆਵਤ ਹੋ ਡਰੁ ਡਾਰਿ ਅਬੈ ॥
666.t: kas aavat ho ddar ddaar abai ||

666.g: ਮੁਹਿ ਲਾਗਤ ਹੋ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਰੂਪ ਸਬੈ ॥੩੮੩॥
666.t: muh laagat ho mirag roop sabai ||383||
666.e: He said. “How al of you have come here after relinquishing your fear? I am seeing only the deer everywhere.”383.
The sage, seeing his resoluteness, and accepting him as his Guru, praised him and said,

666.g: ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਸੋ ਜਿਹ ਕੋ ਚਿਤ ਐਸ ਲਗ੍ਯੋ ॥
666.t: mirag so jeh ko chit aais lagayo ||

666.e: “He, who is so much attentive towards the deer, then think that he is absorbed in the love of the Lord.”384.

666.g: ਮੁਨ ਕੋ ਤਬ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਪ੍ਰਸੀਜ ਹੀਆ ॥
666.t: mun ko tab prem praseej heeaa ||

666.e: The sage accepted him as his eighteenth Guru with his melted heart

666.g: ਮਨ ਮੋ ਤਬ ਦਤ ਬੀਚਾਰ ਕੀਆ ॥
666.t: man mo tab dhat beechaar keeaa ||

666.g: ਗੁਨ ਮ੍ਰਿਗਹਾ ਕੋ ਚਿਤ ਬੀਚ ਲੀਆ ॥੩੮੫॥
666.t: gun miragahaa ko chit beech leeaa ||385||
666.e: The sage Dutt thoughtfully adopted the qualities of that hunter in his mind.385.

666.g: ਹਰਿ ਸੋ ਹਿਤੁ ਜੋ ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਕਰੈ ॥
666.t: har so hit jo ieh bhaat karai ||

666.e: He, who will love the Lord in this way, he will ferry across the ocean of existence

666.g: ਜਗ ਤੇ ਫਿਰਿ ਆਵਨ ਜਾਨ ਮਿਟੈ ॥੩੮੬॥
666.t: jag te fir aavan jaan miTai ||386||
666.e: His dirt will be removed with the inner bath and his transmigration will end in the world.386.

666.g: ਗੁਰੁ ਜਾਨ ਤਬੈ ਤਿਹ ਪਾਇ ਪਰਾ ॥
666.t: gur jaan tabai teh pai paraa ||

666.g: ਭਵ ਭਾਰ ਅਪਾਰ ਸੁ ਪਾਰ ਤਰਾ ॥
666.t: bhav bhaar apaar su paar taraa ||
666.e: Accepting him as his Guru, he fell at his feet and ferried across the dreadful ocean of existence
He adopted him as his eighteenth Guru and in tthis way, the poet has mentioned the save in verse-form.387.

666.g: ਸਬ ਹੀ ਸਿਖ ਸੰਜੁਤਿ ਪਾਨ ਗਹੇ ॥
666.t: sab hee sikh sa(n)jut paan gahe ||

666.e: All the disciples gathered and caught his feet, seeing which all the animate and inanimate beings were startled
All the animals, birds, gandharvas, ghosts, fiends etc. were wonder-struck.388.
End of the description of the adoption of a Hunter as the Eighteenth Guru.

666.g: ਅਥ ਨਲਨੀ ਸੁਕ ਉਨੀਵੋ ਗੁਰੂ ਕਥਨੰ ॥
666.t: ath nalanee suk uneevo guroo kathana(n) ||
666.e: Now begins the description of the adoption of the Parrot as the Ninteenth Guru
KRIPAN KRIT STANZA
The sage, benevolent in qualities, was a thinker about learning and always practiced his learning.389.
Seeing his beauty, the god of love felt shy and seeing the purity of his limabs, the Ganges was wonder-struck.390.
Seeing his comeliness all the princes felt pleased,
Because he was the greatest scholar and generous and accomplished person.391.
The glory of his limbs was indescribable
He was pretty like the god of love.392.
He performed many practices detachedly night and day and
Had relinquished all the desires because of the unfoldment of knowledge.393.
The sage Dutt, the king of Sannyas looked very beautiful like Shiva,
While enduring the sunshine on his body, allied with unique comeliness.394.
The beauty of his limbs and face was perfect and

667.e: Powerful his limbs, practising Yoga, did not bend.395.
Through extremely comely, he remained desireless night and day
And adopting the qualities, the sage lived detachedly.396.
Being absorbed in unexpressible Yoga, he was far away from all foundnesses
Even on forsaking all the royal luxuries, he always remained healthy.397.
That kind sage, was allied with qualities
He was a man of good intellect, a resolute vow-observer and merciful.398.
Enduring coldness on his body, his mind never got impaired and in this way after many years, he had been victorious in Yogs.399.
When that Yogi talked, the leaves of the trees swerved
And knowing the attributes of the Lord, he did not disclose anything to others.400.
He used to drink hemp, roamed here and there blew his horn and
Remained absorbed in the meditation of the Lord.401.
His limbs and mind both remained stable
Absorbed in meditation, he remained engrossed in the practice of Yoga.402.
While performing austerities, he never felt any suffering
And being absorbed in various types of devotional ideas, he always remained engrossed in devotion.403.
These sages, who relinquished their homes,
Subsisted on air and remained silent.404.
These sages, supreme amongst Sannyasis understood the internal mysteries
They were the age with mysterious mind.405.
They felt the inner Light and remained detached
They were full of virues and were no prone to destruction.406.
They were adorable for Brahmins, and masters of mysterious qualities

668.e: They were god of gods, who never begged alms etc.407.
They were masters of Sannyasis and supremely mighty people
Someone talked about their story and someone walked with them.408.
These gentle sages were masters of infinite qualities
They were persons of good intellect and stores of wisdom..409.
These sages in the garb of Sannyasis, were without malice and
Remembering that Lord, were merged (absorbed) in that Great, wise and unrealizable Lord.410.
Indra, moon-god and wind-god silently remembered the Lord.411.
The Yakshas, birds and oceans wer raising tumult in astonishment.412.
The sea alongwith his powers was visualizing that God of gods and mysterious Lord.413.
Seeing these Yogis, the pleasures and sexual enjoyments were getting illusioned in wonder.414.
Forsaking their arms, weapons and canopies, the people were falling at the feet of these sages.415.
Th musical instruments were being played
There was the sound of thunderous music and the songs were being sung.416.
The god Surya and the heavenly damsels leaving their self-restraint, were getting pleased with them.417.
Seeing hem the Yakshas and birds were getting pleased and there was a run amongst the kings for their sight.418.

669.e: These Yogis who had been immersed in Yoga and who had withdrawn from all enjoyments,
Had been wearing the ochre-colored clothes of various countries. 419.
These Yogis of firm conduct and sinless Karmas had abandoned all enjoyments.420.
These vow-observing Yogis of good conduct and sinless Karmas had given up all evil actions.421.
These were the people who had destroyed attachment and deceit and
Performers of good actions like the waters of all the sacred rivers.422.
